en: *The Great Zhou Catalogue of Determined Scriptures*, Fascicle One:
List of Mahāyāna Sūtras Translated Individually. List of Mahāyāna Sūtras Translated Individually: Two Hundred and Eighty-three Works in Five Hundred and Twenty-five Fascicles.
*The Buddha-mudrā Samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle.
The above was translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty;
it appears in the Changfang Record.
*One Scroll of the Sutra for Binding Oneself with a Girdle When Encountering Bandits*, translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.

*Jūzé jīng* (Sūtra on the Incantation for Thieves), one fascicle; also known as *Chúbì záihài zhòu* (Incantation for Eliminating and Warding off the Harm of Thieves). Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Shisiyi jing* (Sūtra on the Fourteen Intentions), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty; recorded in Sengyou’s *Lù*.

*Baoji sanmei wenshu wen fashen jing* (The Ratnakūṭa Samādhi Sūtra on Mañjuśrī’s Inquiry into the Dharma-body), one fascicle, also titled *Weiri baoji sanmei wenshushili wen fashen jing*; six sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Míngdù wǔshí xiàoji jì jīng* (Sūtra on the Fifty Evaluations of the Perfection of Wisdom), in two scrolls; also known as the *Wǔshí xiàoji jì jīng*, consisting of forty-four sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Yuánjiā era of the Later Han dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Names of the Four Hundred Samādhis*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Padmāvatī-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Mahāyāna Vaipulya Prajñā-essence Sūtra*, one fascicle, one sheet. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
*Renbenyusheng jing* (Sūtra on the Human Being’s Original Desire for Birth), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao in the second year of the Yongshou era of Emperor Huan of the Later Han.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on Kāśyapa’s Compilation*, one fascicle, nine sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Inquiry to the Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle; also known as the *Wénshǔ Jīng*, twenty sheets. Translated by Zhi Chen during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty.
*Guangming sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of Radiance), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Loujiachen during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Nei liu boluomi jing* (Sutra on the Six Inner Pāramitās), one fascicle. Translated by the lay devotee Yan Fotiao during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Moha qinjìn jing* (Sutra of Great Diligence), one fascicle, also titled *Da qinjìn jing* (Sutra of Great Diligence). Translated by Zhi Qian during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty.
*The Scripture on Dharani Phrases*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
*Vajrasamādhi-prakṛtiviśuddhy-avināśy-aniruddha-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Vajraviśuddhi-sūtra*. Eight sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty.
The *Huaji tuoluoni jing* (Sutra of the Flower Accumulation Dhāraṇī), one fascicle, three sheets, translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty; recorded in the *Baochang lu*.
It appears in the *Dharmodgata lu*.
*The Twelve Gates Mahāvaipulya Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Record.
*The Sūtra of the Nine-Colored Deer*, one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu period.
Extracted from the *Dharmottara-lu*.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra of Thirty Verses on the Buddha’s Past Deeds* (or without the word "sūtra"). Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
*Pusa shengdi jing* (Sūtra on the Birthplace of the Bodhisattva), one fascicle; also titled *Chamajie jing*, nine sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Found in the Changfang lu.
*Chujia Gongde Jing* (Sutra on the Merit of Leaving Home), one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu period;
listed in the *Changfang Lu*.
*Chujia Gongde Jing*, one fascicle, two sheets. *Wenshushili Pusa Jing* (Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva Sutra), one fascicle. Both translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sānguǐ wǔjiè shénwáng míng jīng* (Scripture on the Names of the Deity Kings of the Three Refuges and Five Precepts). To its right, Seng’an states it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin period.
Extracted from the *Sēngyòu lù*.
*The Scripture of the Names and Merits of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Scripture of the Names of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Círénwèn bāshízhǒng hǎo jīng* (Sūtra on the Eighty Minor Marks), also simply called the *Bāshízhǒng hǎo jīng*, translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Bósa sānshí'èrxiàng jīng* (Sūtra on the Thirty-two Marks of a Bodhisattva), one fascicle; also known as the *Sānshí'èrxiàng yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Thirty-two Marks). Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Yanjingding jing* (Sūtra on the Purity of Concentration), one fascicle; also known as *Xushi jing* (Sūtra on the Succession of Generations). Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra of the Girl Ratnadattā*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra of the Samādhi of the Dharma-Rules of Sumati*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*The Sūtra of the Elder’s Son Suvarṇāvabhāsa*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Líɡòu gài jīng* (Sūtra on the Canopy Free from Defilement); translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Hui-ming jing* (Sūtra on Wisdom-Clarity), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Xin-ming jing* (Sūtra on Mind-Clarity), one fascicle, three sheets. Also titled *Xin-ming nü fanzhi fu fanzhi shi jing* (Sūtra on the Offering of Rice Gruel by the Brahmin Woman Mind-Clarity). Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Dharmottara-lu*: *The Scripture on the Illusionist Rṣyaśṛṅga*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng-lù*.

The *Samādhi Sūtra Asked by the Bodhisattva Samantacakṣus*, one fascicle in three (or two) rolls; also titled the *Sūtra on the Concentrated Mind of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra*, sixty-three pages; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). One fascicle, two rolls, forty sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Dà'ān era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Dá mó yù duō luò lù* (Catalogue of Dharmodgata).
*Zhòngyòu jīng* (Sūtra on the Multitude of Benefactors), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Shíděng zàngjīng* (Sūtra on the Tenfold Treasury), one fascicle, also titled *Sānzuǎn yuèmíng jīng* (Sūtra of the Three Turnings of the Moon-Brightness). Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mìjì jīngāng lìshì jīng* (Sūtra of the Secret-Trace Vajra-mighty-one), in five or eight fascicles, totaling one hundred thirty-two sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the first year of the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty.
*Juedaosu jing* (One Scroll), translated by Zhu Fahu of the Jin dynasty; recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
It appears in the *Neidian lu*.
*Zhizhongdebeneijing* (Sūtra on Planting the Roots of All Virtues), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
appears in the Changfang lu.
*Moyijing* (Sūtra on Māra’s Rebellion), one fascicle, twenty-two sheets. First appearance: translated by Zhu Fahu during the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Master Chángfáng).

*Mílè púsà suowèn běnyuàn jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Vows Asked by Maitreya Bodhisattva), one fascicle; also titled *Mílè púsà běnyuàn jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Vows of Maitreya Bodhisattva) or *Mílè púsà nán jīng* (Sūtra on the Interrogation of Maitreya Bodhisattva); nine sheets. Translated during the Western Jin dynasty by Zhú Fǎhù.
From the *Chūn-ten-roku* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures):
*Jimmikyō* (Sūtra of Daily Illumination), one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Miroku ni tenshin kyō* (Sūtra of Maitreya Taking Female Form), one fascicle; also known as *Miroku Bosatsu ni tenshin kyō*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Ji zhufangdengxue jing* (Sūtra on Rescuing Those Who Study the Vaipulya), one fascicle, fourteen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Za zhous jing* (Sūtra of Miscellaneous Dhāraṇīs), one fascicle in three rolls; translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Mengshi jing* (Sūtra on Fierce Offerings), one roll; also titled *Mengshidao jing*; translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *A-vé-yuè-zhì zhē jīng* (Sūtra on the Avaivartika), in three or four fascicles; alternatively titled the *A-vé-yuè-zhì jīng* (Avaivartika Sūtra) or the *Bùtuìzhuǎn fǎlún jīng* (Sūtra on the Non-retrogressive Wheel of Dharma); seventy-seven sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Jueding zongchi jīng* (Sūtra of the Decisive Dhāraṇī), ten sheets; also titled the *Jueding zong jīng* (Sūtra of the Decisive Totality) or the *Jue zongchi jīng* (Sūtra of the Decisive Dhāraṇī). Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Miè shífāng míng jīng* (Sūtra on Extinction in the Ten Directions of Darkness). Initially, one edition lacked the character "miè" (extinction); it consists of six sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Guangxi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture of the Deer Mother*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture of the Eightfold Yang Divine Incantation*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture of the Eightfold Yang*, three sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Samādhi of Concentrated Mind*, one fascicle. Dao’an states: [it was translated by Dharmarakṣa].
Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
listed in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

One fascicle: *The Scripture of the Names of the Fifty-three Buddhas that Eradicates Sin*. [Also] the *Scripture of the Tathāgata-treasury of Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Wu dynasty.
Appearing in Sengyou’s Catalogue.
*Chuyao jing* (Scripture on Essential Exits), one volume in twenty fascicles. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
Appears in Sengyou’s Catalogue.
The *Sūtra on the Previous Life of the Buddha Siṃhacandra*, one fascicle, seven pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taian era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Dharmodgata-lu*.
*The Scripture on Attaining Great Merit by Reciting the Names of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions*, one fascicle.
Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it is recorded in Sengyou’s catalog.
*The Scripture on the Names of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions for the Extinction of Sin*, one fascicle.
Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
It appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Scripture on the Name of King Buddha Abundant and Majestic Virtue*, one fascicle.
Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it is recorded in Sengyou’s catalog.
*The Bodhisattva Guṇaratnaprabhā Asks about Upholding the Sūtra*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Bodhisattva Daśabhūmika-caryā-pratipatti-sūtra*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that... [this was translated by Dharmarakṣa].
Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in Sengyou’s *Lu*.
One fascicle, titled *Huayan Jingjing Jing* (The Avataṃsaka Sūtra on Purity). Regarding this, Dao’an stated: [text follows].
Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in Sengyou’s *Lu*.
One fascicle of the *Fumuyu poyu jing* (Sūtra of the Parable of the Floating Wood). Right: Dao’an says: [End of entry].
Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.
One fascicle of the *Dharani-gatha-sutra*. Regarding this, Dao’an stated: [text follows].
Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

One fascicle of the *Maudgalyāyana Ascends to the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens Sūtra* (one version lacks the character "heaven"); translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty, following the *Benevolent King Sūtra* (Pūrṇabhadra).
*Pǔshǒu tóngzhēn jīng* (The Scripture on the Youthful Truth of Universal Chief), one fascicle. Translated by Zhú Fǎhù during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of the One Hundred and Forty Vows of the Bodhisattva Mahāprabhāsa*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Jiyin pusa yuan jing* (The Sūtra on the Vows of the Bodhisattva Jiyin), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Samanatabhadra bodhisattva jing* (The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra), one fascicle, eight pages. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Yuankang era of the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Pusa kuxing jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Austerities), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Da Kang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Bodhisattva’s Admonition Against Sleep*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Alternative Version of the Bodhisattva’s Past Deeds*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Bodhisattva’s Original Arising* (without the character "qi"). Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Rebuke of Domestic Faults*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Púsà rúyì shéntōng jīng* (The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Supernatural Power of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Bǎosà qiú wǔmù fǎ jīng* (The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Seeking of the Five Eyes), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Pusa daoxing liufajing* (The Sutra on the Six Dharmas of the Bodhisattva’s Practice), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Pusa chudi jing* (Sūtra on the First Stage of the Bodhisattva), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Pusa shi daodi jing* (Sūtra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra on King Prasenajit’s Intention to Attack Aṅgulimāla*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Universal Monarch Endowed with the Seven Jewels*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Discourse between Mañjuśrī and the Woman Liyi*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty; highly similar to the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*.
*Chūjōbōroku* (Record of Zhang Fang).
*Inshihachi bosatsu gyō igyōhō kyō* (Sūtra on the Easy Practice Method for Bodhisattvas Who Have First Aroused the Resolve), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūjōbōroku*.
*Pusa zaxing fahang jing* (Sutra on the Miscellaneous Practices and Dharma-practices of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty;
listed in the *Changfang lu*.
*Pusa suoxing sifa jing* (Sutra on the Four Dharmas Practiced by Bodhisattvas), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Pusa wufa xing jing* (Sūtra on the Fivefold Practice of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Six Dharma Practices of Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sūtra on Purifying the Buddha-land*, one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra on the Pure Land*. Translated by the śramaṇa Bai Fazhu of Henei during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of two sheets of the *Xiánzhě wǔfú jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Blessings of the Worthy), translated by the śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Weidai pusa jing* (The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Weidai), one fascicle. Translated by Bai Fazang during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
*Tantetu tuoluoni jing* (The Dhāraṇī Sutra of the Tantu Mountain), one fascicle. Translated by Bai Fazang during the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Arising and Manifestation of the Tathāgata*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazang of Henei during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Shoudajing* (Sūtra on the Arrival of the Head), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Bai Fazang of Henei during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Zhengyijing* (Sūtra on the Correct Meaning), one fascicle. Second appearance. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
*The Sūtra on the Parinirvāṇa of King Śuddhodana*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Collection of Various Sūtras on the Names of Bodhisattvas*, one section in two fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Sūtra on the Bestowal of the Body by King Māndhātṛ*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma-pavilion).

*Aśokarājāvyākaraṇa-sūtra* (The Scripture on King Aśoka Receiving the Prediction), one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthita during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù.
The *Udayana-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, also titled the *Udayana-rāja-buddha-pratimā-karaṇa-sūtra*, six sheets. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Chūzōhōroku* (Record of Changfang).
One fascicle, seven sheets. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chūzōhōroku*.
*The Scripture on the Thirty-seven Factors of Enlightenment*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmaruci during the Taikang era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Scripture on Gathering Flowers to Contravene the King and Receiving the Buddha’s Prediction*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by Zhu Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Qīfó suǒjié máyóu shùzhòu jīng* (Sūtra on the Oil-Pressing Incantation Recited by the Seven Buddhas), an alternative version; translated at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty by Zhu Tanwulan.
*Tuolinbozhou jing* (The Sutra of the Dhāraṇī of the Alms Bowl), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Great Deity’s Mother’s Vow-Mantra*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Eyu fayu shenzhou jing* (The Scripture of the Divine Incantation of the Dharmaparyāya of Eyu), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Jie riyu shenzhou jing* (Sūtra of the Incantation for Resolving the Calamity of the Day), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Liushen ming shenzhou jing* (Sūtra of the Incantations of the Names of the Six Deities), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Huànshī bātā shénzhòu jīng* (also titled *Bōtuóyòu*) was translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Tán tè luó má yóu shù shén zhòu jīng* (Sūtra on the Description of Divine Spells with Tāntrika Sesame Oil). Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Má yóu shǔ shénzhòu jīng* (Sesame Oil Discourse on the Divine Spell Sūtra). Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mánílóduàn Shénzhòu Ānmó Jīng* (The Divine Incantation Massage Sutra of Maṇirāta). Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán at Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yīwáng wéilóuyán shénzhòu jīng* (The Scripture on the Divine Incantation of the Medicine King Vairocana), one fascicle; also known as *Ānān suowèn yīwáng wéilóuyán zhòu* (The Incantation of the Medicine King Vairocana Asked by Ānanda). Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán at Yǎngdū during the reign of Emperor Xiàowŭ of the Eastern Jin dynasty.

These were translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty; they are recorded in the *Changfang lu* (Catalogue of Changfang). They include: one fascicle of the *Longwang zhoushui yujing* (Sutra of the Dragon King’s Incantation for Bathing), one fascicle of the *Shiba longwang shenzhoujing* (Sutra of the Divine Incantations of the Eighteen Dragon Kings), one fascicle of the *Zhiyu zhoujing* (Sutra of the Incantation to Cease Rain), one fascicle of the *Qingyu zhoujing* (Sutra of the Incantation to Request Rain), one fascicle of the *Qinshui shenzhoujing* (Sutra of the Divine Incantation for Offering Water), one fascicle of the *Huanshi ayizou zhoushoujing* (Sutra of the Incantations of the Illusionist Ayizou), one fascicle of the *Zhoushui jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Water), one fascicle of the *Zhuoyao jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Medicine), one fascicle of the *Zhududu jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Poisons), one fascicle of the *Chi ju shenzhoujing* (Sutra of the Divine Incantation of Holding Phrases), one fascicle of the *Zhushiqi bing jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Seasonal Epidemics), one fascicle of the *Zhuxiaer jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Infants), one fascicle of the *Zhuchi jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Teeth), one variant version of the *Zhuya tong jing* (Sutra of Incantations for Toothache), or alternatively titled the *Chitong zhuyantong jing* (Incantation for Toothache and Eyeache), and one fascicle of the *Maniluo dan shenzhoujing* (Sutra of the Divine Incantation of Manilodana). One fascicle of the *Wuyan wen jing* (Sutra of the Five Eyes) is also included. All of the above are recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jing liu boluomi jing* (Sutra on Purifying the Six Pāramitās), one fascicle. Translated by Buddhabhadra during the Eastern Jin dynasty;
included in the *Huadu si lu* (Catalogue of Huadu Monastery).

*Wenshushili fayuan jie jing* (Sutra of Mañjuśrī’s Verses on Making Vows), one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra in the second year of the Yuanxi era (420 CE) during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One *zhǒng* (section) of the *Cānjīng* (Dhyāna Sūtra) in four fascicles; translated by Jñātāmitra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Wǔgài yíjié shīxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Loss of Practice through the Knot of Doubt and the Five Hindrances), one fascicle; second edition. Translated by Jñānagupta during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Bósa chūtāi jīng* (Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Abiding in the Womb), one work in five fascicles, totaling one hundred twenty-three sheets. Translated by Zhu Fonian at Cháng'ān during the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Zhōngyīn jīng* (Sūtra on the Intermediate State) in two volumes, totaling twenty-seven sheets; translated in Cháng'ān during the Later Qín period by Zhú Fóniàn.
Recorded in the *Nèidiǎn lù*.
*Pusa puchu jing* (The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Universal Abiding), one work in three fascicles; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Canjing* (Scripture on Dhyāna), one work in three fascicles, also titled *Pusa chanfa jing* (Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Methods of Dhyāna); identical to the *Zuochan sanmei jing* (Scripture on the Samādhi of Seated Dhyāna). This Mahāyāna text clarifies contemplative practice and was translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Appearing in the two Qin catalogs and the Baochang lu.
*Bodhicittotpādana-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
*Mahā-upāya-kauśalya-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin, as recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dharaṇīkośa-sūtra*, one volume; translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Huāshǒu jīng* (Flower-Hand Sūtra), also titled the *Shè zhū shàngēn jīng* (Sūtra on Gathering All Roots of Goodness); alternatively in ten, eleven, twelve, or thirteen fascicles. Translated by Kumārajīva in Cháng'ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha Asking about the Merit Obtained from Upholding this Sūtra*, one fascicle, six pages. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān during the Later Qín period.

*Qianfo yinyuan jing* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Thousand Buddhas), one fascicle, twenty-one sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva during the seventh year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Appears in the *Dafang* (Changfang) catalog and the *Dharmodgata* catalog.
*The Scripture on the Wife of the Elder Dharmamati*, one fascicle, three pages. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin dynasty;
appears in the *Dharmoktara Record*.
*The Scripture on the Dānapāramitā Practiced by All Benefactors*, one fascicle, four pages. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Dharmottara-lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha-field of Immeasurable Bliss*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Zhūfǎ wúxiāng jīng* (Sutra on the Signlessness of All Dharmas), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Bǎochàng lù*.
*Sālarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages; translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin dynasty.
Appears in the *Dharmoktara-lu*.
*Bhadramukha-sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled *Bhadramukhā-devī-sūtra*—three pages; translated by the śramaṇa Fajian during the reign of the Western Qin dynasty under the Qifu clan.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of Prince Sudāna*, one fascicle, twenty-four sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Fǎjiān at the New Temple in Jiangling, Henan, during the reign of Qífú Guórén of the Western Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Place of the Bodhisattva’s Birth*, also titled the *Sūtra on the Questions of Magadha*; translated by the śramaṇa Fǎjiān during the Qiǔfú period of the Western Qin dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.
*Bodhisattvabhūmiviniścayasamgrahaṇī-sūtra*, one volume in ten fascicles. Translated by Dharmakṣema at Guzang during the Northern Liang dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.

The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra, one work in four fascicles; also known as the Dantidhāraṇī Sūtra, the Vaipulya-Dantidhāraṇī Sūtra, or the Dhāraṇī of Sixty-Two Sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Fa-zhong of the Northern Liang during the Gaochang Commandery.
*Gongde bao yiguang pusa jing* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Single-Ray of Merit-Treasure), one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang period.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Da jixi zhou jing* (Sūtra of the Great Auspicious Mantra), one work in four fascicles, forty-four pages, or two fascicles; translated by Tanyao during the tenth year of the Taihe era of the Later Wei dynasty.
It appears in the *Dharmottara-lu*.
*Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśa-sūtra*, one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Niyata-niyatamudrā-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-five sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded by Dharma Master Chujingtai.
*The Sūtra on the Prophecy of Kṣemadatta*, one fascicle, four pages. Translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Yīqiè fǎ gāowáng jīng* (Sūtra of the High King of All Dharmas), one fascicle, twenty sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Xinghe era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Paramārthadharmavijaya-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra*, one work in eight fascicles (or seven or six), totaling one hundred thirty-two sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Buddhanāma-sūtra*, in thirteen (or twelve) rolls and three hundred sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the Zhengguang era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, nine sheets, titled *Bàngfó jīng* (Sūtra on Slandering the Buddha). Translated by Bodhiruci in Luoyang and Ye between the second year of the Yongping era and the Tiānpíng era of the Later Wei dynasty.
*Yinse nü jing* (Sutra of the Silver-Colored Woman), one fascicle, seven sheets. Translated by Buddhayaśas at Baima Monastery in Luoyang during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Abhayaśrī-dārikā-sūtra*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated by Buddhayaśas at the Baima Monastery in Luoyang during the Yuanxiang era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Tathāgata-siṃhanāda Sūtra*, one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Buddhayaśas together with Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty;
recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*The Bodhisattva-caturdharma Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci at Jinhua Temple in the capital of Ye during the Later Wei period.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Saṃghāṭa-sūtra*, four scrolls and fifty-nine pages. Translated at the capital of Ye by Prince Moposhouna of the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).

*The Sūtra of the Brahmin Śubhavyūha’s Inquiry of Devadatta*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan at Jiyuan Temple in Yangdu during the fourth year of the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
*Mahābherīhāraka-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, thirty-six pages. Translated by Guṇabhadra at Dong'an Temple during the Song dynasty.
The *Dàyì jīng* (Sūtra of Great Meaning), one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Buddha Enters the Sūtra on the Ambrosial Subduing and Rectifying of the Mind*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Great Twelve Gates Sūtra*. Translated during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra.
*The Sūtra of King Aśoka*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of the Liu Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Sūtra on Killing a Dragon to Save a Nation*, one fascicle; extracted from the sixth fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Benxing liu boluomi jing* (Sutra on the Original Practice of the Six Pāramitās), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Zhōngyīn jīng* (Sutra on the Intermediate State), one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Ānán jiàn shuǐguāng ruì jīng* (The Scripture on Ānanda Seeing the Auspicious Omen of the Light of Water). Translated by the monk Huìjiǎn of the Lùnyè Temple during the reign of Emperor Xiào Wŭ of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Samitiya-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Sūtra on the Vinaya Used by the Wise*. Translated during the era of Emperor Ming of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Faju in Guangzhou.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
*The Tathāgata-enlightened-wisdom-inconceivable Sūtra*, one fascicle in five rolls. Translated during the era of Emperor Ming of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Zhu Fajian at Guangzhou.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Samudramati-sūtra*, one fascicle, seven rolls; *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra*, one fascicle, five rolls. Both were translated at Guangzhou by the śramaṇa Zhu Fajian during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Song dynasty.
They appear in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Guānshìyīn Chànhuǐ Chúzuí Jīng* (The Sutra of Avalokiteśvara’s Repentance for the Eradication of Offenses), one fascicle. Translated by the *śramaṇa* Fayi during the Yongming era of the Southern Qi dynasty; recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Sqī Fó Gè Shuō Jì Jīng* (The Sutra of the Verses Spoken by Each of the Seven Buddhas), one fascicle; *Pútí Fúczàng Fǎhuà Sānmèi Jīng* (The Sutra of the Samādhi of the Dharma-Transformation of the Bodhi-Treasury of Merit), one fascicle; *Ānmù Zhòu Jīng* (The Sutra of the Incantation for Ancestral Tombs), one fascicle. These were all translated by the *śramaṇa* Shi Daobei during the Southern Qi dynasty.
*Pusa bao yun jing* (The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Ratnamegha), one fascicle. Translated by Saṃghavarman during the first year of the Putong era of the Liang dynasty.
Appears in the Baochang lu.
*Uruvilvā Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the lay devotee Mudaoxian during the fifteenth year of the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang Lu*.
*Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā Sūtra*, one work in two fascicles. Translated by Saṃghabhadra at the Zhanyun Pavilion during the seventeenth year of the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
One fascicle, ten scrolls: the *Bodhisattvabhūmivikrīḍita-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*. Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Luoyang.
From the *Baocang lu* (Record of the Treasure Collection):

*The Scripture on the Dhāraṇī for Protecting All Children*, one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci while he was in Luoyang and Ye.

*Randeng jing* (The Scripture on Lighting Lamps), one fascicle; also titled *Shideng gongde jing* (The Scripture on the Merit of Offering Lamps). Translated by Ratnamati during the Northern Qi dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jian bao sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Seeing Jewels), one fascicle, ten scrolls. Translated by Narendrayaśas at Ye during the Tiāntǒng era of the Northern Qi dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Anuttarāśrayasūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes. Translated by the śramaṇa Paramārtha during the second year of the Yongding era of the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Vistīrṇadharmamukhaparyāyasūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Paramārtha at the Zhìzhì and Wángyuán monasteries in Guangzhou during the Chen dynasty.
*Zhongzhong zaji jing* (Sutra of Various Miscellaneous Incantations), one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture of the Woman Dṛḍhā*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture of the Firm Woman*, six sheets. Translated by Narendrayaśas at Xingshan Monastery in the second year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in Changfang’s Catalogue.
*The Scripture of the Bodhisattva Protector of the Nation*, one fascicle in two volumes, forty-two pages. Translated by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the Neidian lu (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures).
*The Sūtra of the Tathāgata Supreme Lamp King of the East*, one fascicle, thirteen pages. Translated at Daxingshan Monastery by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures):

One fascicle of the *Wúsuǒyǒu púsà jīng* (Aśvaghosa Bodhisattva Sūtra), consisting of four scrolls and sixty sheets. Translated at Daxingshan Temple by Jñānagupta and others during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù*.
*Dàfāngguǎng zǒngchí jīng*, one fascicle, thirteen sheets. Translated by Vinitaruci during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Fajie Tixing Jing* (Sūtra on the Essential Nature of the Dharmadhātu), one fascicle, ten sheets. Translated at Xingshan Monastery by Śīlananda during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Rare and Wondrous Measurement of Merit*, one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta in the sixth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*The Sūtra of the Divine Mantra of the Names of the Twelve Buddhas*, also known as *The Sūtra on the Measurement of Merit for Removing Obstacles and Extinguishing Sin*, one fascicle, eight sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta at Daxingshan Temple in the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Rúlái fāngbiàn shànqiǎo zhòu jīng* (The Sūtra of the Tathāgata’s Skillful Means and Mantras), one fascicle, eleven pages. Translated by Jñānagupta during the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma-Repository).
*Śubhasiddhikumāra-sūtra*, one fascicle, two rolls, twenty sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta during the eleventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
*The Scripture of the Girl Candrottarā*, two fascicles, twenty-seven sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta in the tenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Included in the *Neidian lu*.

The Mahādharmolkā Dhāraṇī Sūtra, one volume in twenty fascicles and three hundred pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Jñānagupta and others at Daxingshan Temple in the Western Capital during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

*The Scripture of the Names of Five Thousand Five Hundred Buddhas*, one volume in eight fascicles, totaling one hundred twenty-six pages. Translated at Xingshan Temple in the Western Capital by Jñānagupta during the thirteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Zhūfó hùniàn jīng* (Sūtra on the Protection and Mindfulness of All Buddhas), one fascicle, ten scrolls. Translated by Jñānagupta and others at Xingshan Monastery in the Western Capital during the fourteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Mahātejas-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty scrolls, three hundred and sixty-five pages. Translated at Xingshan Monastery in Chang’an by Jñānagupta, Dharmagupta, and others during the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Guānchá zhūfǎ xíng jīng* (Sūtra on Observing the Practices of All Dharmas), consisting of four scrolls and sixty sheets. Translated at Xingshan Monastery by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta during the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Lì zhuāngyán sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Power Adornment) in three scrolls and thirty-six sheets. Translated by Yaśas at Dàxīngshàn Monastery in Chāng'ān during the Kāihuáng era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chu-nei-dian-lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures):
*Mahāsannipāta-dṛṣṭāntarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, two volumes, thirty-two pages. Translated at Xingshan Monastery by Jñānagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).
One fascicle of the *Padmavaktra-sūtra*, two volumes, twenty-three sheets. Translated by Narendrayaśas during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*The Scripture on Arousing the Pure Mind*, one fascicle in two volumes, twenty-seven pages. Translated by Jñānagupta at Xingshan Monastery during the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle, eleven sheets of the *Chusheng putixin jing* (Sūtra on the Arising of the Bodhicitta), translated by Jñānagupta in the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty;
recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Śreṣṭhīdevaputraparipṛcchāsūtra*, one fascicle, sixteen sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta in the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty;
recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*Dharmāgraparamārājasūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-two sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta at Xingshan Monastery in the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures:

*Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, ten rolls, one hundred and forty sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha at Śrīprabha Monastery during the early years of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).
*The Scripture of Divination and Observation*, one fascicle in two rolls; translated by the foreign śramaṇa Bodhimitra.
On the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month of the first year of the Tiāncè Wànwuì era, it was compiled and promulgated by imperial decree.

*The Sutra of the Dhāraṇī of the Pure Avalokiteśvara and Samantabhadra*, one fascicle, five sheets. Translated on the eleventh day of the fifth month in the fourth year of the Yonghui era of the Great Tang by the Venerable Monk Zhitong of Zongchi Monastery in the Western Capital.
Compiled and promulgated by imperial decree on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month of the first year of the Tiānchè Wànsuì era.

*Dhāraṇīsaṃgraha-sūtra*, one volume in twelve fascicles, totaling three hundred and fifty sheets. Translated at Huírì Monastery in the Western Capital by the Tripiṭaka Master Ajitavatra (translated as Wújí Gāo) from Central India on the fifteenth day of the fourth month of the fifth year of the Yǒnghuí era of the Great Táng.
Compiled and promulgated by imperial decree on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month of the first year of the Tiān-cè Wàn-suì era.

One fascicle of the *Eight Maṇḍala Sūtra*, also titled the *Sūtra Asked by the Bodhisattva Siṃhamati*. Translated at Cí'ēn Monastery in the Western Capital by the Tripiṭaka Master Nadi from North India during the second year of the Longshuò era of the Great Táng.

The Scripture on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Vimalamati Regarding the Paying of Homage to the Buddha-Dharma, in one fascicle and five sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Nadi from North India during the Longshuo era of the Great Tang dynasty, in the third year [663 CE].
The *Sahasraparivarta Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Ṣaḍakṣara Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle;
the *Dhāraṇī Spoken by Seven Koṭis of Buddhas*, one fascicle; the *Divine Mantra that Accords with the Intent of All Tathāgatas*, one fascicle;
the *Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Heart-Mantra Sūtra*, one fascicle; or the *Sūtra on the Tathāgata Teaching and Admonishing King Jayasena*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra of King Śatruñjaya*, ten sheets; *The Extremely Rare Sūtra*, one scroll, five sheets; *The Sūtra of the Peerless*, one scroll, two sheets;
*The Dhāraṇī of the Heart of All Buddhas*, one scroll, two sheets; *The Sūtra on the Merit Arising from Upholding the Names of the Seven Buddhas*, one scroll, five sheets;
*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Prediction of the Duration of the Dharma at the Time of His Parinirvāṇa*, one scroll, five sheets.
*The Sūtra on Praising the Merits of the Mahāyāna*, one fascicle, five pages; *The Sūtra on the Stage of Buddhahood*, one fascicle, ten pages;
*The Sūtra Revealing the Merits of Boundless Buddha-lands*, one fascicle, two pages; *The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Victorious Banner Arm-Seal*, one fascicle, two pages;
*The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity*, one fascicle, two pages; *The Eight Names of Samantaguhyadhara*.
*Āṭānāṭīya-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets; *Lokadhara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, seven sheets;
*Nidāna-āryamārga-sūtra*, one fascicle, five sheets; *Ṣaṇmukha-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets; *Prajñā-hṛdaya-sūtra*, one fascicle, one sheet;
*Devaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle, three sheets; *Dvādaśāṅga-pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra*, one fascicle.
*The Sutra on the Samādhi of the Divine Transformation of Silent Illumination*, one fascicle, two pages;

translated by Xuanzang of the Great Tang. *The Mahāyāna Sutra on the Four Dharmas*, one fascicle, one page; *The Sutra on the Merit of Building Stūpas*, one fascicle, two pages; *The Vaipulya Siṃhanāda Sutra*, one fascicle, six pages; all translated by Divākara at the Eastern Taiyuan Monastery in the first year of the Yonglong era of the Great Tang.

*Mahāyāna-bhadrakalakṣaṇasūtra*, one fascicle, eight pages. Translated by Divākara at the Guīníng Yùan of Xītāiyuán Temple in the Western Capital during the second year of the Yongchún era of the Great Táng.
The Mahāyāna-Ghanavyūha-sūtra, one fascicle in three volumes and sixty-three pages; translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlabhadra of the Great Tang.

The Saptakoṭi-Buddhamātṛ-hṛdaya-Mahācundī-dhāraṇī-sūtra, one fascicle in four pages; translated by Śīlabhadra at the West Taiyuan Temple in the Western Capital during the first year of the Chuigong era of the Great Tang.

The Mahāvaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra, one volume in twelve fascicles, totaling two hundred and forty-six pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara at the Western Taiyuan Temple, Guining Yuan, in the Western Capital during the first year of the Chuigong era of the Great Tang.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Wisdom Torch*, one fascicle, four pages; *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Assembly of All Buddhas*, one fascicle, four pages. These two sūtras were translated at the Great Zhou East Temple by the Tripiṭaka Master of Khotan, Devendraprajña, in the second year of the Tiānshòu era of the Great Zhou dynasty.

The *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī for Attaining Sovereignty through Seeking Whatever One Desires*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of India at Tiangong Temple during the second year of the Changshou era of the Great Zhou dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Divine Incantation of the Dharma Gate for Protecting Life*, one fascicle, thirteen pages. Translated by Bodhiruci at Foshouji Monastery during the second year of the Changshou era of the Great Zhou dynasty.

*Mahāyāna-vajramuṣṭi-maṇiratna-bodhisattva-caryā-prakaraṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-one pages; *Śrīmatī-dārikā-paripṛcchā-mahāyāna-sūtra*, one fascicle, five pages. These two sūtras were translated at the Eastern Temple of the Great Zhou by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of South India in the second year of the Changshou era of the Great Zhou dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha Spoken by Mañjuśrī*, one fascicle in two volumes (or one volume), twenty-seven pages. Translated in the second year of the Changshou era of the Great Zhou dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci at the Eastern Temple of the Great Zhou.

*Pusa daodi jing* (Bodhisattva-bhūmi Sūtra), one fascicle; Master Dao’an states it was translated from the Vaipulya section. *Mahācakra-vartana sūtra*, one fascicle. *Mahākṣema-paripṛcchā sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively called the *Mahākṣema sūtra*. *Bodhisattva-samācara sūtra*, one fascicle. *Bodhisattva-daśauḍumbara sūtra*, one fascicle. *Bodhisattva-pūrvayoga sūtra*, one fascicle. *Mahāgandhavaiśravaṇa-kṣīṇaśraddha-bhikṣu-prabhṛti-tāraṇa sūtra*, one fascicle. The old catalogs refer to this as the *Kṣīṇaśraddha-bhikṣu sūtra*, large version. The *Zangjing* (Canon) records one fascicle. The aforementioned eight sūtras are classified by Sengyou’s catalog as "Ancient Heterodox Sūtras" (*gu yi jing*).

*The Collection of Dhāraṇīs*, one fascicle, ten rolls, one hundred and eighty-seven pages; also known as *The Sūtra of Miscellaneous Mantras*. *The Śūraṅgama Samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle, two rolls. *The Sūtra on the Birth of Bodhi*, one roll. *The Vīra Samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle, two rolls. The above were translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan.
*Jueding zui fu jing* (Sutra on Determining Sin and Merit), one fascicle; translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang period.
*Dafa du jing* (Dharma-du Sutra), one work in two fascicles; translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin period.
The Great Zhou Catalogue of the Collected Scriptures, Volume One;
The Great Zhou Catalogue of the Collected Scriptures, Volume Two.
Compiled by the śramaṇa Mingquan and others at the Foshousiji Monastery by Imperial Decree.
Catalogue of Mahāyāna Scriptures Translated More Than Once, Volume One. One hundred and eighty works, totaling one thousand three hundred and ninety fascicles. Volume One:

*The Great Vaipulya Buddha Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, one work in sixty fascicles (or fifty fascicles), totaling one thousand eight hundred and seven sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Buddhabhadra at Daochang Temple in Yangzhou during the fourteenth year of the Yixi era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Dōushā jīng* (Tathāgatotpattisambhava-sūtra), five sheets; translated by Zhi Chen at Luoyang during the Zhongping era of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Original Acts of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; also known as the *Sūtra on Original Acts*, thirteen sheets. Translated by the lay practitioner (upāsaka) Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
This is the prose version of the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, without the verses.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Jìngxíng pǐn jīng* (Sūtra on the Chapter of Pure Conduct), also titled *Púsà běnyè jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Vows of Bodhisattvas); translated by Zhīqiān during the Wu dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Jianbei yiqiezhi gongde jing* (The Sutra on Gradually Preparing for the Merit of All-Knowledge), one fascicle, five rolls, one hundred and twenty-two pages; translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin during the seventh year of the Yuankang era.
This *Daśabhūmika* chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
The *Dafangguang Shidi Jing*, one fascicle—also titled *Pusa Shidi Jing* or simply *Shidi Jing*—consists of seven sheets. It was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
This is the "Ten Abodes Chapter" from the *Avataṃsaka*.
It appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya Bodhisattva Daśabhūmika Sūtra*; translated by the Śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
*Foshuo jingangzang wen pusa xing jing*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu in Chang’an during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Chapter on Transcending the World*, one fascicle, six rolls, one hundred and nineteen pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in the first year of the Yuankang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
This is the "Chapter on Transcending the World" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Púsà shízhù jīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Abodes of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa.
This is the "Ten Abodes" chapter (*Daśabhūmika*) of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Rúlái xīngxiǎn jīng* (Sūtra on the Manifestation of the Tathāgata), in four scrolls, also titled the *Xīngxiǎn rúhuàn jīng* (Sūtra on the Manifestation of Illusory Reality), totaling seventy-seven sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the Yuánkāng era of the Western Jìn dynasty.
The "Chapter on the Arising of Nature" from this *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

The one-fascicle *Sūtra on the Fundamental Vows of All Bodhisattvas Seeking Buddhahood*, consisting of eleven sheets, is the "Chapter on Pure Conduct" from the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*; it was translated by the lay devotee Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
One fascicle of the *Shízhù jīng* (Ten Stages Sūtra) in twelve scrolls; translated by Niè Dàozhēn during the Tàikāng era of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Mahāvaipulya Bodhisattva Daśabhūmika Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the lay devotee Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
This version is largely identical to that translated by Dharmarakṣa, with only minor differences.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva Dashū jīng* (Sutra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva). Third edition. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhabhadra from North India during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva-benyè jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Vows of Bodhisattvas) is a re-translation of the "Jìngxíng pǐn" (Chapter on Pure Conduct). The *Chángfáng lù* states: "The *Benyè jīng* mentioned above was translated by Buddhabhadra of the Eastern Jin."
From the *Jingtai lu*.
One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva-daśabhūmi-dharmasthiti-sūtra*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Buddhabhadra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
This is the "Ten Stages" chapter (*Daśabhūmika*) from the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*.
The *Chángfáng lù* states:
"Translated by the lay devotee Niè Dàozhēn during the Tàikāng era of the Jìn Emperor Huìdì.
One fascicle of the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra*. [Note: The above was translated by Zhīduōmì of the Eastern Jìn."
*The Scripture on the Ten Abodes of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; the second [entry] from the right. Translated by Jītamitra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Daśabhūmika-sūtra*, one work in four fascicles (or five fascicles), ninety-seven sheets. Translated during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva together with Buddhayaśas.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zhuāngyán pútíxīn jīng* (Sūtra on Adorning the Bodhicitta), the second translation; it is largely identical with minor differences to the "Bodhisattva-daśabhūmika-parivarta" translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. The above was translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva in the Hongshi era of the Later Qin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Lú mójiā jīng* (Rāmaka-sūtra), one fascicle in three or four rolls, totaling seventy-four sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jiān of the Western Qin;
it is also said to have been translated by Ānfǎxián of the Cao Wei.
This "Entering the Dharma Realm" chapter (*Lokadhātupraveśa-parivarta*) of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra* appears in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).

The one-fascicle *Rāmāyaṇa-sūtra* (*Luomojia jing*), translated during the Wei dynasty by An Faxian, differs from this version in its degree of detail. The present text was translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Dharmakṣema.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dàfāngguǎng púsà shìdì jīng* (The Vaipulya Sūtra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva). This second edition differs slightly from the *Púsà shìdì jīng* translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty. It was translated by the śramaṇa Jikaya at Beitaï during the Yánxīng era of the Northern Wei dynasty.
This *Huayan shizhu pin* (Chapter on the Ten Abodes of the Avataṃsaka) was previously listed in the *Changfang lu*.

The *Xinli ruyin famen jing* (Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of Entering the Seal through the Power of Faith), one fascicle in five rolls and ninety-three pages, was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmaruci at Luoyang during the Zhengshi era of the Northern Wei.
This *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* appears in the *Neidian lu*.

*The Buddha’s Avataṃsaka Entering the Tathāgata’s Inconceivable Realm Sūtra*, one fascicle (or two fascicles), twenty-eight pages. Translated during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by the śramaṇa Jñānagupta, together with Dharmagupta, at Xingshan Monastery in the Western Capital.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dàfāngguǎng fó huáyán jīng xù rù fǎjiè pǐn* (The Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Continued Chapter on Entering the Dharma Realm), consisting of eleven sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Divākara at Xitāiyuán Temple in the Western Capital during the first year of the Chuǐgōng era of the Great Táng.
Newly included in the canon:

*The Sūtra of the Flower Ornament of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Chapter on the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha*, one fascicle (or two fascicles), thirteen pages. Translated by the Khotanese śramaṇa Divākara at the Wei-guo East Temple in the Divine Capital during the first year of the Yongchang era of the Great Tang.
Newly included in the canon:

*The Great Vaipulya Buddha-avatamsaka Sūtra, Section on Cultivating Loving-kindness*, one fascicle, nine pages. Translated by the Khotanese śramaṇa Divākara at Dazhou Dōngsì in the Shen-du capital during the second year of the Tiānshòu era of the Great Zhou dynasty.
Newly included in the catalog:

*The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha-sambhava Sūtra*, one volume in two fascicles (also titled *The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgata-gotra-miṭa-kośa Sūtra*), fifty-one pages; *The Daśaprakāra-janma-dharma Sūtra* from the *Avataṃsaka*, one volume; *The Buddhanāma Sūtra*, one volume; *The Bodhisattvanāma Sūtra*, one volume; an excerpt from the *Avataṃsaka*, one volume; *The Daśabhūmika Sūtra*, one work in four volumes; and *The Gradual Preparation of the Ten Stages*, one volume. These thirty-six preceding scriptures are all branches of the *Avataṃsaka*.

The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, one volume consisting of six hundred fascicles and twelve thousand sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the Yu Hua Palace in Fangzhou during the fourth year of the Xianqing era of the Great Tang.
This one section of the sutra contains both single and combined translations.

The *Daoxing banruo jing* (Aṣṭasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra), one fascicle, ten scrolls, one hundred ninety-four pages: translated by the śramaṇa Zhi Loujiachen at Luoyang in the second year of the Guanghe era of the Later Han dynasty.
This is recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
It is the *Xiǎopǐn jīng* (Shorter Version Sūtra).

The ancient version is titled *Yí rì shuō bānrě jīng*, one fascicle; it is also known as *Fó yí rì móní bǎo jīng*, *Móhēyǎn bǎoyán jīng*, or *Dàbǎojī jīng*. It consists of twenty-five sheets. It was translated in Luoyang during the Jiānchū year of Emperor Huán’s reign in the Later Han dynasty by the śramaṇa Zhīlóujiāchèn.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Dàoxíng jīng* (Sūtra of the Practice of the Way), translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Foshuo during the Jiaping era of the Later Han;
recorded in the *Zhū Shíxíng lù* of the Later Han.

*The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle in four or six rolls, also titled *The Mahāprajñāpāramitā-ananta-sūtra*, totaling one hundred and six pages. Translated during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty by the lay devotee (upāsaka) Zhi Qian at Liangzhou.
*Mahāprajñāpāramitā-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the lay practitioner (upāsaka) Zhi Qian during the Jianxing era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

The *Wu pin jing* (Sūtra in Five Chapters), one volume in five fascicles, also titled the *Dazhidu wuji jing* (Sūtra of the Great Perfection of Wisdom), is identical to the *Xiao pin banruo* (Shorter Prajñāpāramitā). It was translated by the śramaṇa Kang Senghui during the Wu period, in the year of the Red Bird (222–280 CE), specifically during the reign of Emperor Qi of the Right Wei dynasty.
Appearing in the two catalogs of Sengyou and Changfang:
*The Sutra of the Buddha’s Bequeathed Sun-Moon Mani Jewel*, one fascicle, nineteen sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
Appears in the catalog of Changfang.

The *New Sūtra on the Practice of the Path* (Xīndáoxíngjīng), one volume in ten fascicles or seven fascicles; this is the second edition, also known as the *Small Version* (Xiǎopǐn). It consists of one hundred and eighty-five sheets. It was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa at Luoyang and Jiangzuo during the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Renwáng bānrě jīng* (Benevolent Kings Prajñā Sūtra), consisting of two fascicles or one fascicle of thirty-one sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin during the Yongjia era.
Extracted from the *Ji lu* (Miscellaneous Records) of the Jin Dynasty.

One fascicle of the *Xiaopin jing* (Shorter Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra), seven scrolls; the second translation. Translated by Dharmarakṣa in Luoyang during the fourth year of the Taishi era of the Western Jin.
This is recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
It differs entirely from the old *Dàoxíng* translated by Zhú Fóshuò during the Han dynasty.

*The Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra of Radiant Praise*, one fascicle, in fifteen (or ten) rolls, totaling two hundred and fifty-one pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in Chang’an during the seventh year of the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of four scrolls of the *Dàzhìdù wújí jīng* (Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra); the *Yìshàn sì lù* states it is extracted from the *Dàpǐn* [Sūtra]. Right, Dào'ān says it was translated by Zhú Fǎhù during the Jìn dynasty.
Recorded in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

One fascicle of the *Fangguang banruo jing* (Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra), consisting of thirty fascicles—or alternatively twenty fascicles—totaling five hundred and thirty sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Mokṣala and others at Cangyuan in Chenliu during the first year of the Yuankang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures):

*Móhē Bānruò Bōluómì Dàoxíng Jīng* (The Sutra on the Practice of the Path of the Mahāprajñāpāramitā), one volume in two fascicles, also simply called *Dàoxíng*. Translated by the lay devotee Weishidu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.

The *Baoshang lu* records that the *Dazhidu jing*, one fascicle in four scrolls, according to the catalog of Yishansi, was translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Jñānagupta from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. (Right) [This concludes the entry]. Eastern Jin śramaṇa Jñānagupta’s translation.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Móhē bānrě bōluómì jīng chāo Cháng'ān pǐn* (Excerpts from the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra: The Chang’an Chapter), five fascicles; also known as the *Xūpútí pǐn* (Subhūti Chapter) or the *Cháng'ān pǐn jīng* (Sūtra of the Chang’an Chapter), totaling eighty-three sheets. Translated during the Jiànyuàn era of the Former Qín by the śramaṇa Dharmapriya together with Zhu Fóniàn.
Recorded in the *Chūn-ien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

*Fàngguāng bōrěbōluómì jīng* (The Sutra of the Radiant Prajñāpāramitā), one volume, twenty fascicles; the second translation. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Cháng'ān during the Hongshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Renwáng bānruò jīng* (Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra) in two scrolls; this second edition differs slightly in wording from that translated by Dharmarakṣa. It was translated in the third year of the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; thirteen sheets of paper from Śrāvastī. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Cháng'ān during the third year of the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, consisting of thirty fascicles, or forty fascicles, or twenty-seven fascicles, totaling six hundred and nineteen sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng’ān during the fifth year of the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xiǎopǐn bānruò bōluómì jīng* (Shorter Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra), in ten, seven, or eight fascicles; this is a different translation of the same text as the *Pútí jīng*. It consists of one hundred and fifty-four sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān during the tenth year of the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Dàmíngdù jīng* (Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra), comprising four scrolls and one hundred and six pages. Translated by the Northern Liang śramaṇa Dàogōng at Xīyuán.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the *bhagavat* [Bodhiruci] on sixteen sheets of paper during the second year of the Yongping era of the Later Wei dynasty by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at the capital of Luoyang.
Recorded in the *Chu nei dian lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures):

*Manjusri-prajnaparamita-sutra*, one fascicle or two fascicles, with the character "shuo" (to speak) added [in the title], twenty-four sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Mandaraka in Yangzhou during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
*The Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra Spoken by Mañjuśrī*, one fascicle. The above sūtra is the second translation;
it is slightly superior to the two-fascicle version produced by Mandara.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Saṃghavarman of Fu Nan during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù.

*Renwang banruo jing*, one fascicle. The above was translated at Baoyue Temple by the Śramaṇa Paramārtha of the kingdom of Ujjayinī in the third year of the Datong era, during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty.
This is extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
It differs slightly from the version translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.

*Śrīdevī-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, one fascicle, seven rolls, one hundred twenty-four sheets. Translated in the sixth year of the Tiānjiā era of the Chen dynasty by the Prince of the Yuezhi kingdom, Vighnaśūra, at Xingye Monastery in Jiangzhou.
Furthermore, the *Hongfu lu* and other catalogs state it was translated at Yangzhou;
this appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle, fourteen sheets of paper. Right: Translated by the Śramaṇa Paramārtha at the Zhizhi and Wangyuan Monasteries in Guangzhou during the Yongding era of the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra* in three volumes. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śānavāsa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou dynasty at the Four Heavenly Kings Temple in Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra Capable of Severing [Delusion]*, one fascicle, twenty-one sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Xuánzàng at Dàcí'ēn Monastery in the Western Capital during the Yǒnghuī era of the Táng dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnaintien lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Shixiang banruo jing* (Sūtra on the Prajñā of True Reality), nine pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Dazhou Dongsì in the Shen-du capital during the second year of the Changshou era of the Great Zhou dynasty.
*Mahāyāna-ratnavyūha-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty sheets. The aforementioned *Chángfáng-lù* states it was translated during the Jin dynasty.

*Mahāratnakūṭa-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Mahāratna-sūtra*, the *Ratna-sūtra*, or the *Maṇiratna-sūtra*—twenty sheets. The aforementioned *Neidiàn-lù* states that this is a different translation of the same original text as the *Buddhavaṃśa-ratnākara-sūtra* by Zhi Chen and the *Mahāyāna-ratnavyūha-sūtra*.

*The Sutra of the Divine Incantation of Prajñāpāramitā*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*. *The Sutra of the Comprehensive Collection of the Meaning of the Infinite*, two fascicles; excerpted from the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*. The thirty-six sutras preceding these were all branches of the *Prajñāpāramitā*.
The *New Compilation of the Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*, sixty fascicles. Compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Sengjiu of Zhaoti Monastery during the sixth year of the Kaihuang era.
The *Chángfáng Lù* states: [as above].
He left home at a young age and specialized in the studies of the Bao-fang (Ratnakoṭa) school.
According to the Sanskrit original,
this Mahāsaṃnipāta Sūtra consists of one hundred thousand verses.

As the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta, who is currently translating the scriptures, has stated on several occasions:

however, as Mahāyāna practitioners, they requested that he remain to receive offerings.
The royal palace itself possessed the three great Mahāyāna sūtras: the Mahāprajñāpāramitā, the Mahāsannipāta, and the Avataṃsaka.
It consists of one hundred thousand verses.
However, as we move further away from the Sage,
ordinary consciousness gradually grows dim, and one can no longer maintain them all in memory.
I have excerpted and transcribed these according to my capacity;
consequently, the Sanskrit original is incomplete,

This was because it had previously been translated by the scholar Zhituan,
and later by Kumārajīva.

When Guṇabhadra arrived during the Qi dynasty, [the pivot was finally set].
The *Candragarbha-sūtra* in twelve fascicles was translated [earlier];
until the Kaihuang era, Yaśas further translated the *Sūryagarbha-sūtra* in fifteen fascicles.
Since both are included within the original chapters of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, [they are considered part of it].
Truly joyful and leaping with delight, I have immediately compiled these according to their combination into sixty fascicles.
*The Scripture of Śāriputra Questioning the Jewel Woman*, one fascicle; extracted from the second fascicle, translated by An Shigao during the Later Han period.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Shēnyuè zhǎngzhě huìguò gòngfó jīng* (Sūtra on the Elder Shen Yue Repenting His Faults and Making Offerings to the Buddha), also titled *Yóuqǐ zhǎngzhě huìguò jīng* (Sūtra on the Elder Youqi Repenting His Faults). Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle titled *The Sūtra of Śāriputra’s Praise of the Inconceivable Teachings of the Jewel Woman*, also known as the *Sūtra of Praising the Jewel Woman*; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Bāguāng jīng* (Sūtra of the Eight Radiances). Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, one work in twenty-seven fascicles. Translated for the first time in Luoyang during the Jianhe era of the Later Han dynasty by the Yuezhi śramaṇa Lokakṣema.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Achamó jīng* (Akṣayamati-sūtra) in four volumes; its original title was the *Achamó púsà jīng*. It was translated at Wuchang by the Indian śramaṇa Vighna during the third year of the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Dàcí wújiǎn jīng* (Sūtra on Great Compassion Without Diminution). Translated by Zhīqiān during the Wù period.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Akṣayamati-nirdeśa Sūtra*, one fascicle, two volumes. Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Akṣayamati Sūtra*, one fascicle, four volumes. This second translation differs slightly from the version translated by Weiqinan. Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle: *The Sūtra on the Questions of the Jewel Maiden Regarding the Thirty-two Marks* (also known as the *Sūtra on the Questions of the Jewel Maiden*, or alternatively the *Sūtra on the Thirty-two Matters*, or the *Sūtra on the Gates*). Translated during the Wu dynasty by the lay practitioner Zhi Qian.

*The Scripture on the Demoness Hearing the Buddha Preach the Dharma and Attaining a Male Body*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by the Upāsaka Zhi Qiān during the Wú Hǎngwǔ era of the Three Kingdoms period (right). Excerpted from the *Dàjí jīng*.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Demoness Asking for a Male Body*. The above was translated by Kang Senghui during the Wucheng era of the Wu dynasty.
It appears at the end of the "Chapter on the Past" in the *Bǎochuáng fēn* (Ratnaketu-parivarta).
From the *Baochang lu*:
One fascicle in two volumes, the *Bodhisattva-jingxing jing* (Sūtra on the Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas). Translated by the śramaṇa Kang Senghui in Jianye during the Wucheng era of the Wu dynasty;
this is the "Ratna-keśa-parivarta" (Chapter on the Jewel Topknot) from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*.
Extracted from the Record of Zhu Daozu.
*The Scripture on the Demon King Entering the Abode of Suffering*, one fascicle.
To its right, Dao’an states it was translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu; it is recorded in Sengyou’s Catalogue.
*The Sūtra on King Prasenajit Reaching the Jewel Monastery through the Buddha’s Spiritual Power*, one fascicle.
Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; it is recorded in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Scripture on the Eighteen Unshared Qualities*, one fascicle.
Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty and is recorded in Sengyou’s catalog.
*The Scripture on the Questions of the Devaputra Tiāngxīng Regarding Compassion*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this [was also translated by Zhu Fahu].

*Fǎwáng biànxīn jīng* (Sūtra on the Transformation of the Body of the Brahma King), one fascicle. Translated by Zhú Fǎhù of the Western Jin dynasty; recorded in Sēngyòu’s catalog. Translated by Zhú Fǎhù of the Western Jin;
recorded in Chángfáng’s catalog.
*Catuḥ-vaśitā-abhijñā-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Mahākaruṇā-sūtra*, one work in eight fascicles (or seven, or six), totaling one hundred twenty-seven sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa at Cháng'ān during the Yuánkāng era of the Western Jin.
This is the "Chapter on the Sovereign King Dhāraṇī of the Great Assembly," which appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

It is the *Bǎojié púsà suowèn jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of Bodhisattva Ratnabandhu), one fascicle in two volumes, also titled *Púsà jìngxíng jīng* (Sūtra of the Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas), totaling forty-eight sheets. It was translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fahu during the Taixi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
This is the "Baoji pin" (Chapter on Ratnaśikhin) from the *Mahāsannipāta*. It appears in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

The *Wújìnyì jīng* (Akṣayamati-sūtra), one volume in four or five fascicles, is the second translation produced from the same original as the *Āchāmò jīng* (Akṣayamati-sūtra), totaling eighty-six pages. It was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in Cháng'ān during the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng Lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
