One fascicle of the *Bǎonǚ Wèn Huì Jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Precious Woman on Wisdom), the second translation, which is identical to that produced by Zhīqiān of the Wú dynasty; also included in the four-fascicle *Bǎonǚ Jīng* (Sūtra of the Precious Woman) translated by Zhú Fǎhù of the Western Jìn.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù.

*Mūkyōbosatsu kyō* (The Scripture of the Bodhisattva of Silence), one fascicle in two volumes; alternatively titled *Mugongudōji kyō* (The Scripture of the Silent Youth), forty-one sheets. Translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa.
This is the "Chapter on Silence" from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*, recorded in the catalogue of Nie Daozhen.

The *Ratnāvalī-paripṛcchā-prajñā-sūtra* consists of one work in four fascicles, or alternatively three fascicles; it is also titled the *Sārthavāhī-sūtra* or the *Ratnāvalī-samādhi-sūtra*. It comprises sixty-three sheets. To the right [of this entry], it was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa at Chang’an in the eighth year of the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty.
The "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Ratnacūḍa" from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra* was extracted by Nie Daozhen.

The *Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra*, one volume in seven fascicles (or four fascicles), is the third translation; it is also called the *Akṣayamati-bodhisattva-sūtra* and consists of one hundred and six sheets. It was translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa at Chang’an during the Yongjia era of the Jin dynasty.
This is the "Akṣayamati-parivarta" from the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*.
It appears in the *Chángfáng-lù*.
The *Guǎngwèi púsà zào qībǎotī jīng* (One Scroll), translated by Niè Dàozhēn during the Yuánkāng era of Emperor Huì in the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Wúyán púsà liútōng fǎ jīng* (The Sutra on the Propagation of the Dharma by Bodhisattva Wúyán), found in the seventeenth fascicle; translated by Niè Dàozhēn during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.

*Pusa daoshi xing jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva Path and Its Practice), one fascicle. Found in the third fascicle; translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sutra of the Bodhisattva of Silence*, one fascicle (alternatively titled *The Sutra of the Youth of Silence*, or two fascicles, forty-one pages). Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Initial Generation of the Resolve*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Essential Practice of the Unobstructed Dharma-Gate*, one fascicle. Appears in the twelfth fascicle [of the *Chusansongli jing mulu*]. Translated by Nie Daozhen of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Bodhisattva-śīla-kāya-vaśitā-sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *Vaśavarti-rāja-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-tathāgata-avavāda-sūtra*. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Pusa jie zizai jing* (Sūtra on the Sovereignty of the Bodhisattva Precepts), one fascicle. The above was translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
It appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Questioning of the Four Youthful Princes*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Prince’s Subjugation and the Arising of the Path-Mind*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Mózhǐ wénfó shuōfǎ dénánshēn jīng* (Sūtra on the Demoness Hearing the Buddha Preach the Dharma and Attaining a Male Body), the second translation; it shares the same title as the previously translated *Bìmó shì Mùlián jīng* (The Demoness Tempts Maudgalyāyana) but differs in its text. It was translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Zhūtiān wèn rúlái jìngjiè bùkěsīyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Inconceivable Realm of the Tathāgata as Questioned by the Various Heavens), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
See: *Shuǐshìjiè jīng* (One fascicle). Translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin dynasty during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángzhōu.
*The Sūtra on the Gift of the Precious Woman*, one fascicle. Translated by Jīvaka (祇多蜜) during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Past Infinite Radiance Pure Buddha-land Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Sūtra on the Buddha’s Equal Transformation and Manifestation of Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.

*The Scripture on the Conversion of Māras*, one fascicle; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. [It is] among the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra* (right). Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, one work in thirty fascicles (or forty fascicles); the second translation. [It was] translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng’ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qin.

Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*. One fascicle of the *Bófǎdizi huà mózǐ jìsòng jīng* (Sūtra of the Verses on the Buddha’s Disciple Converting the Son of Māra); one fascicle of the *Dàbái mówáng jiànxìn jīng* (Sūtra of the Great White Māra King’s Firm Faith); one fascicle of the *Guò mófǎjiè jīng* (Sūtra on Passing through the Realm of Māra); and one fascicle of the *Fó qǐngkài chè shífāng jīng* (Sūtra of the Buddha’s Sigh Pervading the Ten Directions). These four fascicles were all translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng’ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Īśvararāja-sūtra*, two scrolls, forty-one sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān in the ninth year of the Hongshǐ era of the Qin dynasty.
This is the "Chapter on the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīśvararāja" from the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*.
It appears in Sengrui’s *Biographies of the Two Qin Translators* (*Monk Rui Er-Qin Lu*).
The *Māyakarma-sūtra*, one fascicle, appears as the eleventh fascicle of the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*; the above was translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Teaching of the Bodhisattva’s Supernormal Powers of the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle. Baochang states that it is also titled *Ākāśa-sūtra*. Translated by Buddhayaśas of the Later Qin;
recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.

*The Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja*, one fascicle, in eight or six rolls; also titled *The Vaipulya Sūtra of the Lord Gaganagañja*. This is a second edition of the text, consisting of one hundred and eight sheets, which corresponds to the version of the *Rāmaṅga Sūtra* translated by Dharmabhadra. It was translated by the śramaṇa Śrīghana during the reign of Qifu Guoren of the Later Qin dynasty at Hena.
This is the *Gaganagañja-parivarta* from the *Mahāsannipāta-sūtra*.
It appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-daśacakra-sūtra*, in eight fascicles (or seven fascicles), totaling one hundred twenty-four sheets. Translated by the Northern Liang śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Guzang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Ākāśagarbha-sūtra* in five rolls; the second translation, made by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema of Northern Liang at Guzang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra, one work in thirty fascicles (or thirty-two or twenty-nine fascicles), the third translation, totaling six hundred and four pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Guzang during the Xuanshi era of the Northern Liang dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Fēnxùn wáng wèn jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of King Veṣṭhila), two scrolls, forty-two sheets; the second translation. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bodhiruci of the Later Wei dynasty at the capital of Luò.
Recorded in the *Chu-nei-dian-lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures):
One fascicle of the *Akṣayamati-sūtra*, six scrolls, eighty-six pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhìyán at Jǐyuán Monastery in Yángzhōu during the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Tíofú zhòngshēng yè jīng* (Sūtra on the Karma of Taming Sentient Beings), found in the third volume; translated by the śramaṇa Shi Zhìyán during the fourth year of the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ākāśagarbha-bodhisattva-mantra-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmamitra in Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Guan xukongzang pusa jing* (Sūtra on the Visualization of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha), one fascicle; also titled *Xukongzang jing* (Ākāśagarbha Sūtra) or *Xukongzang guan jing* (Sūtra on the Visualization of Ākāśagarbha). Two sheets. Translated in Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty by Dharmamitra.
From the *Jingtai lu*:
One fascicle of the *Akṣayamati-nirdeśa-sūtra* in ten rolls; translated during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Fajian at Guangzhou.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

The Mahāvaipulya Candragarbha Sūtra, one volume in ten or fifteen fascicles, comprising two hundred and fourteen sheets. Translated at Tiānpíng Monastery by the śramaṇa Narendrayaśas together with Fǎzhì during the second year of the Tiāntóng era of the Northern Qí dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sumeru-garbha-sūtra* in two scrolls and thirty-eight pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Yashas of the Northern Qi at Tiānpíng Temple.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dìngyì Tiānzǐ Suǒwèn jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Devaputra Samāhita-mati), five scrolls in total; translated during the reign of Emperor Wŭ of the Northern Zhou dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master and Dhyāna Master Jñānayaśas of Magadha. [Categorized under] the *Mahāsannipāta*.
The Zhou official Zangcheng,
together with his two disciples, Yaśaḥkūṭa and Jñānagupta,
[acted] for the Grand Chancellor, Duke Jin Tang, Yuwen Hu.
Translated at the Four Heavenly Kings Temple (Skt. Caturmahārājakāyika-vihāra) in the Old City of Chang’an;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-sūryagarbha-sūtra*, in ten or fifteen rolls, totaling two hundred and four sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Narendrayaśas at the Daxingshan Temple in the Western Capital during the fourth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Mahāsannipāta-Āryaśūra-sūtra*, one volume, in five or six fascicles, comprising ninety-three sheets. Translated by the śramaṇas Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta at Dàxīngshàn Temple in Chāng'ān during the fourteenth year of the Kāihuáng era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle, two scrolls of the *Xūkōng yùn púsà jīng* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha). Translated by Jñānagupta in the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
It is recorded in the *Nèidiǎn lù* that it says: [text follows].

Fourth, the *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva Daśacakra Sūtra*, one fascicle in ten scrolls. This was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the Great Ci’en Monastery in the capital during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.

Extracted from the *Lù* (Catalogues) of Inner and Outer Scriptures: One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*, eight volumes, totaling one hundred twenty-eight sheets; One fascicle of the *Dharmacitta-dhāraṇī Sūtra*; One fascicle of the *Ratnaketu-dhāraṇī Sūtra*; One fascicle of the *Sūtra on Not Engaging in Litigation with Brahmins and Others*; One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Buddha Entering Samādhi and Emitting Great Radiance from a Single Hair*; One fascicle of the *Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Bodhisattva’s Ornamentation of Necklaces*; One fascicle of the *Sūtra on King Guṇavyūha Inviting the Buddha for Eighty-four Thousand Years*. The above seventy-eight sūtras are branches of the *Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*.

*Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one work in forty fascicles (or thirty-six fascicles), totaling eight hundred and forty-seven sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Xi-liang during the third year of the Xuansi era of the Northern Liang dynasty.
Extracted from the Zhudaozu lu.

*The Hu-baniehuan jing* (The Parinirvāṇa Sūtra of the Barbarians), one volume in two fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Lujia Chen during the Jianhe era of Emperor Huan of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Sengyou lu*.
*The Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*, one work in two fascicles. [This is] the abbreviated version by the foreigner An Faxian of the Cao Wei dynasty, consisting of the first section in two fascicles.
The *Changfang lu* states:
Extracted from the Zhudaozu lu.
One fascicle of the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, in two rolls and forty-eight pages; the second extraction. Translated by the foreign upāsaka Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
The *Xùpǐn* (Preface Chapter) and *Āitànpǐn* (Chapter of Lamentation) constitute two fascicles.
The *Chángfáng lù* states that these were extracted from the *Zhú Dàozǔ Wǔlù* (Wu Records of Zhu Daozu).

The *Parinirvāṇa Sūtra*, one work in two fascicles; also titled the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* and the *Vaipulya-parinirvāṇa Sūtra*; fifty sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in the fifth year of the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one volume in six fascicles, or ten fascicles, totaling one hundred and sixty-four pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Faxian at Dàochǎng Monastery in Yángdū during the thirteenth year of the Yìxī era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
The upper volume consists of six fascicles, extracted from Zhu Daozu’s *Miscellaneous Records* from the Jin Dynasty.
*The Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated in the thirteenth year of the Yixi era of the Eastern Jin.
It was produced at Daochang Monastery by Xie Xuan and Xie Shi, the two Commandants (Sikong).
An old catalogue states that Juexian was the one who translated it for Buddhabhadra.
Recorded by transcription from the pen of Baoyun.
This is the first ten fascicles of the earlier section of the Great Sūtra, the "Chapter on the Questions of the Great Assembly.
It is found in the *Jian Daozu lu* (Record of the Patriarchs of the Dharma).
Or ten fascicles.
*Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, one work in twenty fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhimeng at Xiliangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Zhu Hui* and *Song Qi* catalogs.

*The Parinirvāṇa Sūtra*, one fascicle; the second edition, which differs slightly from that translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty, is recorded in the catalogs of Sengyou and Baochang. It was translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra at Xinsi Monastery in Jingzhou in the first year of the Xiaojian era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dàbēi jīng* (Mahākaruṇā-sūtra), one fascicle, five rolls, one hundred sheets. Translated by Yaśas in Xiangzhou during the ninth year of the Tianbao era of the Qi dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Sūtra of the Four Youthful Disciples* (Skt. *Caturdāraka-sūtra*), three fascicles; one volume added; thirty-two characters per page; forty-two sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

The Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra, Section on Cremation, in two fascicles; also known as the Section on Jhāpana (Funeral Rites). Translated during the Linde era of the Tang dynasty by the monk from South India, Yanabhadra.
Together with the monk Huìníng of the Tang state,
it was translated at Bólíngguó in Jírénán.
At the beginning of the Yífēng era, Liáng Nándí, the Governor-General (Dūdú) of Jiāozhōu, brought the scripture to the capital.
In the third year, the presiding monk of Da Ci’en Monastery, Linghui,
submitted a memorial at the Three Offices of the Eastern Palace regarding what had been presented, requesting its implementation.
The Three Offices issued a notification that the matters should be carried out for the benefit of all concerned.
The monk Huili of Taoyuan Monastery in the western part of Chang’an composed the preface.
On the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month of the first year of the Tiace Wansui era,
it was compiled and promulgated by imperial decree.

The *Nāmaguṇavarṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Parideva-sūtra*, one work in two fascicles—a different translation of the same text as the *Vaipulya-parinirvāṇa-sūtra* comprising thirty-five sheets. These fourteen preceding sūtras are all branches of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*.

The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, one work in eight fascicles; this single work consists of a combined translation totaling one hundred and eighty-nine sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Jñānagupta at Xingshan Monastery during the second year of the Renshou era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chu neidian lu*:

*Fahua sanmei jing* (The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Lotus), one fascicle, six rolls; one version contains the character "zheng" (correct). Translated by the śramaṇa Zhi Qianglianglou in the city of Jiaozhou during the first year of the Gannu era of the Former Wei.
Recorded by brush by Shi Daosheng.
Included in the Changfang lu.
*The Sūtra of the Buddha Summoning His Sons with the Three Chariots*, one fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian during the Wei dynasty of the Later (Later Wei).

The *Guangshiyin jing* (Sutra of Avalokiteśvara), one fascicle, appears in the *Chángfáng lù*. It is the same as the *Zhèngfǎhuá jīng* (Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra) translated by Dharmarakṣa in the second year of the Yongjia era of the Western Jin dynasty.
It appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Pumenpin jing* (The Scripture on the Universal Gate), one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Sāyufenduoli jing* (The Scripture on the Saṃpuṇḍarīka), one work in six fascicles. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi country in the first month of the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Records of Zhu Daozu.

*Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, one volume in ten fascicles, totaling two hundred and twenty-one sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in Chang’an during the seventh year of the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.

Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Fāngděng Fǎhuá Jīng* (Vaipulya Lotus Sutra), one volume in five fascicles. Translated by Zhī Dàogēn in the first year of the Xiánkāng era of Emperor Chéng of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Zhú Dàozǔ Lù* (Catalogue of Zhú Dàozǔ).
The *Baoshang lu* (Record of Baochang) from the Xiao Liang dynasty states:

"The *Fahua*, translated by Kumārajīva; the *Miaofa lianhua sanmei* (Lotus Samādhi); the *Fenduo li* (White Lotus); and the *Fangdeng fahua* (Vaipulya Lotus)—these are different translations of the same original text."

The *Pumenpin jing* (Universal Gate Chapter Sutra), one fascicle; the second translation, which is largely identical to that produced by Dharmarakṣa. Translated during the Eastern Jin dynasty by the śramaṇa Jīvaka.
Recorded in the *Daozu lu* and the *Sanzang ji* as the second translation.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Jin dynasty;
they were separated by nearly a hundred years.

The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, one fascicle in seven volumes and one hundred seventy-five pages, was translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an during the seventh year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù.

One fascicle of the Guānshìyīn jīng (Sūtra of Avalokiteśvara), following the Míofǎliánhuá jīng (Lotus Sūtra of the Wondrous Dharma). Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān.
*Guanshiyin Guan Jing* (The Scripture on the Contemplation of Avalokiteśvara), one fascicle. Translated by Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang, during the Song dynasty at Gaochang.
Recorded in the *Changfang Lu*.

*Fahua sanmei jing* (The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Lotus), one fascicle, twelve sheets. Translated by Zhìyán at Jǐyuán Monastery in Yángzhōu during the fourth year of the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
The Devadatta Chapter, the Twelfth of the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma. Transmitted from the right [tradition] during the Yongming era of the Southern Qi dynasty.
The śramaṇa Faxian obtained the Sanskrit original at the Kingdom of Khotan.
The *Dharmaparyāya-offering* was translated at Waguan Monastery in Yangzhou;
it appears in the *Changfang lu*.

Regarding the "Verses on the Repeated Recitation of the Universal Gateway Chapter of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*": during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta from the country of Gandhāra in North India, together with Yuwen [Xiao] of the Liang Prince of Qiao, translated this at Longquan Monastery in Yizhou.

The Six Dhāraṇīs of the Lotus Sūtra, including those of Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, translated during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang; these were previously included in Jingmai’s *Catalogue of Translated Scriptures* among the sixteen preceding sūtras.
Sixth is the complete edition in ten fascicles; from the *Shenghe* (Combined) edition, there are sixteen translations.
*Dazhou kan ding zhong jing mulu*, Fascicle 2;
*Dazhou kan ding zhong jing mulu*, Fascicle 3.
Imperial Edict of the Empress of the Great Tang for the Compilation by the Śramaṇas Mingquan and Others at Foshouji Monastery;
Volume Two. Catalogue of Mahāyāna Scriptures Translated Multiple Times, Volume Two. One hundred and sixty-eight works in three hundred and thirty-eight fascicles.

Combined with the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra*, one work in five fascicles. The above [comprises] the three versions by Zhi Min-du, Zhi Qian, Zhu Fa-hu, and Zhu Shu-lan, combined during the Western Jin dynasty.
These are combined into one section, appearing in the Changfang lu (Catalogue of Changfang).

This is the ancient *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, one volume in two fascicles; it was first produced during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty, translated by the lay devotee Yan Fotiao of Qingxin in Linhuai at Luoyang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-acintyadharmaparyāya-sūtra*, in three fascicles (or two), also titled the *Buddhadharma-purapraveśamārgadvāra-samādhi-sūtra*. Translated by the lay practitioner (*upāsaka*) Zhīqián during the Huáwǔ era of the Wú dynasty.
It differs slightly from the version translated by Yan Fotiao during the Later Han dynasty.
It appears in the Chángfáng Lù (Record of Chángfáng).
*Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, one fascicle, two rolls, fifty-two pages. Translated at Wuchang by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-acintyadharmamukha-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes (or one volume), also titled the *Pǔrùdàomén jīng* (Sūtra on Universally Entering the Gate of the Path). Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in the second year of the Tàishān era of the Western Jin dynasty.
The third edition is largely identical with slight variations to the translations by Yan Fotiao of the Han dynasty and Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty;
it appears in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*Śaṃvimalakīrti-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in Sengyou’s *Lu*.

*Vimalakīrti-sūtra*, one work in three fascicles, the fifth translation; alternatively in two fascicles, or titled *Sīwéimójié jīng*. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Shulan at Luoyang in the sixth year of the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra*, four scrolls; the third edition, translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Saṃghapāla (Zhìduōmì).
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra, one fascicle in three rolls and seventy pages, translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān in the eighth year of the Hongshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

It states: *The Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra*, one fascicle, six scrolls, one hundred and ten sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Xuanzang at the Great Cien Monastery during the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
The ten aforementioned sūtras were translated from the same original;
logically, their principles should not differ.

*Mahāvaipulya-cūḍāmaṇi-sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled *Sutasoma-kumāra-sūtra*, also titled *Vimalakīrti-putra-praśna-sūtra*, also titled *Cūḍāmaṇi-sūtra*. Initially issued in twenty-one sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in the second year of the Yongjia era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dàfāngděng dǐngwáng jīng* (Mahāvaipulya-uṣṇīṣarāja-sūtra). This second extraction has slightly different wording compared to the *Dàdǐngwáng jīng* translated by Dharmarakṣa. The latter was translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
*Mahāyāna-cūḍāmaṇi-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty by Prince Candraprabha of the kingdom of Ujjayinī.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three aforementioned sūtras are different translations from the same original source concerning the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa*.
*Foyu jing* (Sūtra on the Buddha’s Words), one fascicle, three pages; translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu* (Catalogue of Changfang).
*Foyu jing* (Sūtra on the Buddha’s Words), one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma Jñānagupta during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou dynasty.
This appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding sūtras are translations of the same original text.

*Guān púxián púsà jīng* (Sūtra on the Visualization of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Cháng'ān. Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Guān púxián púsà xíngfǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Method of Practice for Visualizing Samantabhadra Bodhisattva), one fascicle. Also known as the *Shēngōngdé jīng* (Sūtra of Profound Merit) or the *Púxián guān jīng* (Sūtra of the Visualization of Samantabhadra). Seventeen sheets. Translated by Dharmamitra at Dào-chǎng Temple in Yángzhōu during the Yuánjiā era of the Song dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.
The first two sutras above are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sutra on the Contemplation of the Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*, one fascicle; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
*The Scripture on the Bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*, one fascicle, twenty-one pages. Translated at Daolin Monastery by Jñānayaśas during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
The first two sutras above are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sutra of King Suvarṇavarṇa*, one fascicle, eight pages; translated by Dharmaruci at the capital of Luoyang during the Later Wei dynasty.
*The Sūtra of King Suvarṇavarṇa*, one fascicle. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci of the Northern Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on King Bimbisāra Visiting the Buddha and Making Offerings*, one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on King Bimbisāra Asking the Buddha about Offerings*, one fascicle. Translated by Upaśūna at Ye City in the second month of the second year of the Xinghe era of the Northern Wei.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two sutras above are different translations of the same original text.
*Púsà hē sèyù jīng* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Rebuke of Form and Desire), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva Heshi yu jing* (Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Rebuke of Form and Desire); this appears to be a different version than that translated by Kumārajīva, being the second translation. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
The first two sūtras above are different translations of the same original text.

*Jiǎzhǎng yīnyuè jīng* (Sūtra of the Elder’s Melodious Joy), one fascicle; also titled *Yīnyuè jīng* (Sūtra of Melodious Joy) or *Jiǎzhǎng yīnyuè bùlánjiāshè jīng* (Sūtra of the Elder’s Melodious Joy and Pūraṇa Kāśyapa); five sheets. Translated by Zhīqián during the Wu dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Elder’s Pleasing Voice*, one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
It appears in the Chángfáng Record.
The two sūtras mentioned above are different translations of the same original text.
*Śrīmālā-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Śrīmālā-siṃhanāda-ekayāna-mahopāya-sūtra*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmayaśas during the reign of Emperor An of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śrīmālādevī-siṃhanāda-ekayāna-mahā-upāya-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-two sheets. Translated by Guṇabhadra at the capital of Yang during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chūn-ting-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
The first two sutras above are different translations of the same original text.

*Fó shuō bù sīyì guāng púsà jīng* (Sutra Spoken by the Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha), one fascicle; also titled *Wú sīyì guāng háotóng púsà jīng* (Sutra of the Child-like Bodhisattva Acintyaprabha), fourteen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Acintya-guṇa-sūtra* (in four fascicles, or two fascicles, totaling thirty-seven sheets), translated during the reign of Emperor Qi of the Wei dynasty.
Also known as the *Guṇa-sūtra*.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Acintyaprabhā-kumāra-bodhisattva-sūtra*, also titled *Acintyaprabhā-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden during the Hongshí era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
The first three scriptures are translations of the same original text.
Only the *Ming ershi ji jing* (Sūtra of the Twenty Verses on Illumination), one fascicle, translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu Kingdom, remains.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

The single-fascicle *Vimokṣa-viṃśati-gāthā-sūtra* is largely identical with minor variations to the version translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty; the above was translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two sutras above are translations of the same original text with different versions.
*Sūmatī-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Sūmatī-bodhisattva-sūtra*; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sūmaṭī-bodhisattva-sūtra*. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The aforementioned two sutras are different translations of the same original text.
*Mahā-upāya-paṛipṛcchā-avipratisāra-sūtra* (Great Sutra on the Requital of Kindness through Great Expedient Means), seven fascicles; translated during the Han dynasty by Zhi Chen.
Recorded in the Changfang lu.
The *Mahā-upāya-kṛtajñatā-sūtra* consists of one work in seven fascicles, which elucidates the two wisdoms.
The first five fascicles explain dwelling and practice in order to repay kindness;
the sixth fascicle explains the Buddha’s retinue, their birth, the dates and months of their birth, and the length of their lifespans.
Furthermore, it is recorded that one who does not receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts shall not obtain a human body.
This is excerpted from the *Zhudaozu lu* (Record of Zhu Daozu) and the first volume of the *Sapoduo ji* (Sarvāstivāda Records).
From the *Baoshang lu*:
The first two scriptures above are the same original text translated separately.
*Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*, one fascicle in four volumes; translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmakṣema of Northern Liang during the reign of Emperor An of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

*Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra-ratna*, one volume in four fascicles, totaling one hundred and four pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra at Daochang Temple in Yangzhou during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù.
*Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra*, one fascicle, ten scrolls, two hundred and three pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye in the second year of the Yánchāng era of the Later Wèi dynasty.
Recorded in Changfang’s Catalogue.
The first three scriptures are translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture of the Questions of the Brahma God Viśeṣacinti* (one fascicle, six volumes; third translation), totaling one hundred and eighteen pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the third year of the Tiānpíng era of the Later Wei dynasty.
It is recorded in the *Neidian lu* that this is the same text as the six-fascicle *Cittadhāraṇī-sūtra* translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty,
and the four-fascicle *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna-sūtra* (or *Siddhārthabuddhi-sūtra*) translated by Kumārajīva during the Qin period; these are different translations of the same original.

*The Scripture on the Questions of the Brahma-Devaputra Cittadhara*, one fascicle in four rolls; also titled *The Scripture on Equalizing and Governing All Dharmas*, *The Scripture on the Brahma-Devaputra Cittadhara*, *The Scripture on Adorning the Buddha-Dharma*, or simply *The Scripture on Holding the Mind*. It consists of one hundred and four pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the seventh year of the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Siyi fànti suowèn jīng* (Suvikrāntavikramī-paripṛcchā-sūtra) in four scrolls; the second edition is identical to the version of the *Shèngsīwéi jīng* translated by Dharmarakṣa, differing by ninety-four pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān during the fourth year of the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Abhisaṃbodhi-saṃdarśana-nirdeśa-parivarta-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Exposition of the Manifestation of Non-retrogression), one fascicle, four scrolls, seventy-one pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng’ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).

There is one work titled *Guangbo yanjing bude zhuan falun jing* (The Sūtra of the Vast, Pure, and Unregressing Wheel of Dharma), in either four fascicles or six fascicles; it is also called *Guangbo yanjing* or *Bude zhuan falun jing*, comprising seventy-eight sheets. This was translated during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Zhìyán, together with the śramaṇa Bǎoyún, at Jiyuansi in Yangdu.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The first two sutras are translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture on the Profound Secret Liberation* (*Shēnmì jiětuō jīng*), one fascicle, five rolls, eighty-three pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Luoyang in the third year of the Yánchāng era of the Later Wèi dynasty.
I have seen the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

The *Jièjié jīng* (Sūtra on the Unraveling of the Knots), one fascicle, is found in the fourth chapter, first section, spanning ten sheets of the *Xiānshēnmì jīng* (Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra). To the right [of this entry], it was translated by the śramaṇa Paramārtha from Ujjayinī at the Zhìzhǐ and Wángyuán Monasteries in Guǎngzhōu during the first year of the Yǒngdì era of the Chen dynasty.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

The *Jiětuō liǎoyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Definitive Meaning of Liberation), one fascicle in two volumes or one volume, is the first two chapters of the *Shēnmì jiětuō jīng* (Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra), comprising twenty-one pages. It was translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra at Dōng'ān Temple in Yángzhōu during the twelfth year of the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
According to the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng):
One fascicle of the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*, five rolls, seventy-three sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Xuánzàng at Cí'ēn Monastery in the capital during the Zhèngguān era of the Great Táng.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).
The four aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Dà yún mì zàng púsà wèn dà hǎi sān mèi jīng* (The Sūtra on the Great Ocean Samādhi Asked by the Bodhisattva Mahāmegha-guhya), one fascicle; translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-nirnimitta-sūtra*, in five fascicles (or four), also known as the *Mahāmegha-sūtra*. Translated in Cháng'ān by the Śramaṇa Zhú Fóniàn of Liángzhōu during the Later Qín dynasty under Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fāngděng dà yún jīng* (Mahāvaipulya-mahāmegha-sūtra), in six scrolls or five scrolls; also known as the *Dà fāngděng wúxiàng dà yún jīng*, the *Dà yún wúxiàng jīng*, or the *Dà yún mìzàng jīng*; ninety-three pages. According to the *Bǎochàng lù*: [it states that...]
Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at the Neiyuan Temple in the capital of Liang;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Great Cloud Wheel Sūtra, Chapter on Invoking Rain*, Volume 111. This was translated during the fifth year of the Tiānhé era of the Zhou Wǔdì reign by the Tripiṭaka Master Śayanayaśas.
Translated at the Four Heavenly Kings Temple in the Old City of Chang’an.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Dà yún qǐng yǔ jīng* (The Great Cloud Rain-Invoking Sūtra), twenty-one pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta of the Later Zhou dynasty in Chang’an.

Consulting the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog), it is recorded that the *Dayunlun qingyu jing* (Great Cloud Wheel Sutra for Invoking Rain) in one fascicle and two scrolls, comprising one hundred chapters and twenty-eight sheets, is the *Dayun jing* (Great Cloud Sutra). It was translated by the Śramaṇa Narendrayaśas during the fifth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-mahāmegha-varṣaprārthana-sūtra*, nine sheets. Translated during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by the śramaṇas Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta at Xingshan Monastery in the Western Capital.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Mahāmegha-guhyagarbha-bodhisattva-varṣa-sūtra*. The above eight sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
New compilation: *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, eight fascicles. This one work consists of eight fascicles.
Furthermore, there are three versions of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*:
the first is the four-fascicle version translated by Dharmakṣema;
the second is the five-fascicle version translated by Jñānagupta.
Furthermore, the translation by Paramārtha consists of seven fascicles.
Its preface states briefly:
"Dharmakṣema, the Dharma Master, remarked that the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra* was incomplete and lacked certain chapters and sections."
Whenever I sought out the texts and deliberated upon their meanings,
I believed this teaching was well-substantiated;
yet, despite my repeated comparisons and examinations, I found no definitive indication, leaving me to ponder it deeply both day and night.
During the Dading era of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, by imperial decree,
Zhang Ji and others from the inner court were sent to invite the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha (translated into Chinese as Zhendi) from Ujjayinī in Western India.
Carrying with him both sutras and śāstras, he respectfully received the imperial decree.
In the first year of the Taicheng era, he translated a catalogue of various scriptures;
however, it was found that four sections were missing: the *Tri-kāya-vibhaṅga*, the *Karmāvaraṇa-prahāṇa-dhāraṇī*, the *Paramaviśuddhabhūmi*, and the *Ākāśapūrṇamanoratha*.
Now, it has been separately compiled into seven fascicles.
Among the two hundred and sixty sūtras newly arrived,
there are further included the "Chapter on the Dhāraṇī of the Silver Lord" and the "Chapter on the Entrustment."
The Dharma Master translated it;
the Śramaṇa Yancong subsequently reviewed and collated it,
compiling it into eight fascicles.
The complete fulfillment of the *pin* (sections) and *bu* (divisions) begins from this point.
The *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*, one volume in four fascicles and fifty-six sheets, was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Guzang during the Xuanshi era of the Northern Liang dynasty.
Consulting the *Chángfáng lù*:

one fascicle of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra*, consisting of seven, eight, or six scrolls and one hundred and fifteen sheets. Translated during the Liang dynasty in the first year of the Chengsheng era by the śramaṇa Paramārtha at Zhengguan Temple and at the residence of Yang Xiong.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

The *Jīnguāngmíng jīng gèngguǎng shòuliàng dàbiàn tuóluóní jīng* (The Sūtra of the Golden Light Further Extending the Span of Life through the Dharani of Great Eloquence), one volume in five fascicles, is the second translation. It was translated during the reign of Emperor Wǔ of the Northern Zhou dynasty by the Upāsaka from the country of Yōu, the Śramaṇa Yeshéjíduō, at Guishèng Temple.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

Regarding the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the "Entrusting" chapter (*Parindanā-parivarta*) and the "Silver Lord" chapter (*Rūpyaprabha-parivarta*) are combined into one fascicle in the translation by Dharmakṣema of the Liáng period; they consist of four fascicles in the translation by Paramārtha of the Liáng period, and six fascicles [in other versions].
The five-fascicle translation by Zhou Jueduo lacks these two chapters; therefore,
they are now reissued here.
The above was translated during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by Śīlananda and Dharmagupta at Xingshan Monastery in Chang’an.
It appears in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
These first five scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Pratyutpanna-samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle in two or three rolls, totaling fifty-seven pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhi Chen at Luoyang in the second year of the Guanghe era of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty.
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra* is a later re-translation of the final ten chapters; according to the record of Dharma Master Jìngtài, it was separately translated during the Later Han dynasty by Zhī Chèn.

*Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra*, two fascicles. An old catalog states it is the *Mahāpratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra*, or one fascicle; this is the second edition. It was translated in Luoyang by the Indian śramaṇa Buddhasena during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra*, consisting of two scrolls and forty-seven pages; Dao’an states it is extracted from the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra*. [Note: Translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa.
I have seen the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Bānzhōu sānmèi niànfó zhāng jīng* (Sūtra on the Chapter of Mindfulness of the Buddha through the Pratyutpanna Samādhi) is the "Chapter on Walking" from the *Bānzhōu jīng*; it was translated during the Han dynasty and appears in the *Zhēnjì sì lù* (Record of Zhēnjì Monastery).
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Bhadra*, one fascicle; these are the first four chapters of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*. The above was recorded in the catalog of Zhenji Temple.
The preceding six sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra on the Illusion-like Samādhi*, one work in two fascicles (or one fascicle); translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, two scrolls of the *Rúhuàn sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Illusion-like Samādhi), the second translation; it shares the same title as the two-scroll version of the *Bānzhòu sānmèi jīng* translated by Zhīqiān during the Han dynasty, with slight differences in wording and phrasing. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jītāmī from the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

The *Rúhuàn sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Illusion-like Samādhi) consists of one volume—either four, three, or two volumes—comprising sixty-six sheets. It was translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Dàfāngděng shànzhùyì tiānzǐ wèn jīng*, one fascicle in four rolls, totaling sixty-eight pages; translated by Dharmagupta at the Translation Hall in the Shànglín Garden of the Eastern Capital during the Dàyè era of the Sui dynasty.

Extracted from the *Lidai Sanbao Ji* (Records of the Three Jewels Through the Ages): *The Sūtra of the Questions of the Holy Devaputra Susthitamati*, one fascicle in four volumes. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jñānagupta at Daxingshan Temple during the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Questions of the Holy Devaputra Susthitamati*, in three or four fascicles; this is a different translation from the same original as the *Yúhuàn sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Illusory Samādhi) by Dharmarakṣa, totaling fifty-five sheets. Translated in the third year of the Xinghe era of the Later Wei dynasty (541 CE) by the śramaṇa Gautama Prajñāruci at Ye City.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The first three scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Fóshēng dāolì tiān wèi mǔ shuōfǎ jīng* (The Scripture on the Buddha Ascending to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to Preach the Dharma for His Mother), one fascicle, in two or three rolls, comprising thirty-six sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in Cháng'ān during the Tàikāng era of Emperor Wŭ of the Western Jìn dynasty.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog).

The *Daoshenzu wuji bianhua jing* (Sutra on the Infinite Transformations of the Divine Foot) in one fascicle and four scrolls—also titled *He dao shenzu* (The Divine Foot that Unifies the Way)—is recorded in Sengyou’s catalog as having been translated either in two or three scrolls; it is the second translation and consists of fifty-one sheets. It was translated by the śramaṇa An Faqin at Luoyang during the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue),
which states that this is a separate translation of the same text as the *Buddha Ascends to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to Preach the Dharma for His Mother Sūtra*, translated by Dharmarakṣa.
The titles differ slightly.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha Ascending to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to Preach the Dharma for His Mother*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmamitra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Record.
The first three [texts] were translated separately from the same original source.

*Sarvadharmāpravṛttinirdeśa-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, thirty-two sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an during the third year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
*Zhufa wuxing jing* (Sutra on the Non-Activity of All Dharmas), one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Guṇabhadra during the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Original Non-existence of All Dharmas*, one fascicle, three volumes, forty-eight sheets. Translated by the śramaṇas Jñānagupta and Gupta at Daxingshan Temple during the fifteenth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng), which states that the first three sutras share the same original text but were translated separately.
*Tathāgataratnatri-samādhi-sūtra*, one fascicle, two scrolls, also titled *Wújí bǎo jīng* (Sutra of the Infinite Treasure), forty sheets. Translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Jīvaka (祇多蜜).
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Wújíbǎo sānmèijīng* (Sūtra on the Treasure Samādhi of the Infinite), one fascicle, thirty sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa in the first year of the Yongjia era of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sutras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sutra of Immeasurable Life*, one fascicle in two volumes: translated by the śramaṇa An Shigao, the Crown Prince of the Kingdom of Parthia, during the reign of Emperor Huan of the Later Han dynasty at Luoyang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, two scrolls of the *Wúliàng qīngjìng jīng* (Sūtra of Immeasurable Purity); its initial appearance was also under the title *Wúliàng qīngjìng píngděng jué jīng* (Sūtra of Immeasurable Pure Equal Enlightenment). It was translated by the śramaṇa Zhi Loujiachen at Luoyang during the period from the Jiànhé to Zhōngpíng eras of Emperor Líng of the Later Hàn dynasty.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Wúliàng qīngjìng píngděng jué jīng* (Sūtra of the Immeasurable Pure and Equal Enlightenment), one volume in two fascicles, third edition, seventy sheets. Translated previously by the Prince of Gāoguīxiāng of the Wèi dynasty together with the śramaṇa Bóyán at the Bái-mǎ Temple in Luòyáng.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle in two volumes, the *Sanyesanfo sàtán guòdù rén dào jīng* (The Sūtra of the Samyaksaṃbuddha’s Salvation of Humanity), the second translation. The *Chángfáng lù* states: "The *Wúliàngshòu jīng* (Sūtra of Immeasurable Life) was translated at the Baima Monastery in Luoyang by the śramaṇa Kang Sengkai in the fifth year of the Jiaping era of the Former Wei."
Changfang says: This was excerpted from the *Ji lu* (Miscellaneous Records) of the Jin dynasty.

The one-fascicle, two-roll *Wuliangshou jing* (Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra), the second translation, differs slightly from that translated by An Shigao. It was translated during the Jiaping era of Emperor Qi of the Wei dynasty by the Śramaṇa Kāṅsēngjiè (Saṃghavarman) of the country of India at the Baima Monastery in Luoyang.
Extracted from the Chángfáng Lù (Record of Chángfáng).
*Píngděngjué jīng* (Sūtra of Equal Enlightenment), one fascicle. Translated by the Western Region śramaṇa Bóyán at Bǎimǎ Temple in Luoyang during the Gāoguīxiānggōng era of the Right Wèi dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of two scrolls, the third translation of the *Amitābha Sūtra*, which differs slightly from the translations by An Shigao of the Han dynasty and Saṃghavarman of the Wei dynasty; it consists of fifty-three pages. Translated during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty by the Upāsaka Zhi Qian.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, two scrolls, forty-six sheets; the fourth edition, identical in text to the versions translated during the Wu period by Zhi Qian, during the Wei period by Kang Sengkai, and by Bo Yan, though differing in certain details. It is also called the *Wúliàng qīngjìng píngděng jué jīng* (Sūtra of the Immeasurable Pure and Equal Enlightenment). Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in the second year of the Yongjia era of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Wúliàngshòu zhìzhēn děngzhèngjué jīng* (Sūtra on the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Truly Realized, Perfectly Enlightened One), one fascicle; also known as the *Lè fó tǔ jīng* (Sūtra on the Joyful Buddha-land) or the *Jílé fó tǔ jīng* (Sūtra on the Land of Ultimate Bliss). Translated by the śramaṇa Fǎlì in the first year of the Yuánxī era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Wúliàngshòu jīng* (Infinite Life Sūtra), one fascicle; also known as the *Āmítuó jīng*, five sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Cháng'ān during the fourth year of the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Xiǎowúliàngshòujīng* (Smaller Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra), one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Guṇabhadra at Zhìhuán Temple in Yángzhōu during the early years of the Xiàojian era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*New Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, one volume in two fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇa Buddhabhadra during the Yongchū era of the Song dynasty.
The *Chángfáng lù* states it was translated during the Eastern Jin.
The New Sūtra of Immeasurable Life, one work in two fascicles. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmamitra at the Jetavana Monastery during the Song dynasty;
recorded in the catalogue of Zhenji Monastery.
The *Amitābha Sūtra*, one fascicle, five sheets. Translated during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* (Wúliàngshòu jīng), one volume, two fascicles, the seventh translation, thirty-six sheets. Translated in the second year of the Yongchū period of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Bǎoyún at Dàochǎng Temple in Yángzhōu.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Contemplation of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life*, also titled the *Sūtra on the Contemplation of Immeasurable Life*, consisting of eighteen sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra at Dào-chǎng Temple in Yángzhōu during the Yuánjiā era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Guan wúliàngshòu fó jīng* (Sūtra on the Visualization of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life). The above was translated by Dharmamitra during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Bǎochàng lù*.
*The Sūtra on Praising the Pure Land and Being Received by the Buddha*, one fascicle, eleven pages. Translated at Ci'en Monastery by the śramaṇa Xuanzang during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
Previously, there were eighteen translations in twenty-seven fascicles, which differed in their earlier and later versions;
all were titled *The Sutra of Immeasurable Life*.
There is also one fascicle of the *Sutra of the Old Mother*, also titled *The Sutra of the Old Woman*, consisting of two sheets; it was translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu period.
*Laomu liuying jing* (The Scripture of the Six Heroines of the Elder Mother), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra of Mañjuśrī’s Perambulation*, one fascicle, six pages: translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the Yongping and Tianping eras of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, nine sheets: *Mañjuśrīcaryā-sūtra*. Translated in the sixth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by the Tripiṭaka masters Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta at Daxingshan Temple in Chang’an.
Extracted from the *Lù dìng ān shì lù* (Record of the Definitive and Peaceful Era). The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Jīngāng shàngwèi tuóluóní jīng*, one fascicle, sixteen pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas at Baima Temple in Luoyang and Huājīn Temple in Yedu during the period from the sixth year of Zhèngguāng to the second year of Yuànxuáng of the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Jīngāngchǎng tuóluóní jīng*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka masters Jñānagupta and Guptadatta at Daxingshan Temple in Changan during the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*Zhèng gōngjìng jīng* (Sūtra on Reverence for the Correct), one fascicle; also known as the *Wéidé tuóluóní zhōng shuō jīng* (Sūtra Spoken within the Vīrya-dhāraṇī) or the *Zhèngfǎ gōngjìng jīng* (Sūtra on Reverence for the True Dharma); five sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas at Baima Monastery in Luoyang and Jinhua Monastery in Ye between the sixth year of the Zhengguang era and the second year of the Yuangxiang era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on Skillful Reverence* (also titled *Sūtra on Reverencing Teachers*), seven sheets. Translated at Daxingshan Temple by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta during the sixth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
[This entry] is from the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The first two sūtras above are different translations of the same original text.

*Lìgòu shīnǚ jīng* (Sūtra of the Girl Liùjùshī), one fascicle; the initial portion consists of twenty-four sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa in the tenth year of the Tàikāng era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Wúgǒushī púsà yìngbiàn jīng* (also titled *Yìngbào jīng*), totaling twenty-six sheets. Translated during the Yuánkāng era of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty, up until the Yuánjiā era.
Translated by Nie Daozhen;
this is an alternative version of the *Vimaladattā-sūtra*,
as seen in the *Changfang lu* (Catalogue of Dharma Treasures).

*The Sūtra of the Girl Vimalā*, one fascicle, twenty-five sheets. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci at Jinhua Temple in the capital of Ye during the third year of the Xinghe era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Ajñāta-kauṇḍinya, Daughter of King Ajātaśatru*, one fascicle; first translated by Zhī Qián of the Wu [Dynasty].
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Aśokarājñī-āśudharmabodhisattva-sūtra*, also titled the *Aśokarāja-sūtra* or the *Āśudharmabodhisattva-sūtra*; seventeen sheets. Second translation. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa in the first year of the Jiànwǔ era of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
It differs slightly from the translation by Wu Shi Qian.
It appears in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*The Scripture of King Ajātaśatru’s Daughter Mṛgajā*, one fascicle; translated during the Western Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three fascicles are different translations of the same text.

*Wúyájì chí fǎmén jīng* (Sūtra on the Dharma-Gate of Boundless Retention), one fascicle; also known as the *Wújì jīng* (Sūtra of the Boundless) or the *Jīngāngshǒu nǚ suowèn jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Woman Vajramukhī); seventeen sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Shèngjiān (also named Fǎjiān) of the Western Qin dynasty.
Translated by Qifu Qiangui. Recorded in the Changfang lu (Catalogue of Dharma Master Changfang).
One fascicle of the *Anantadharmamukhaparivarta-sūtra*. The above was translated by Guṇabhadra at Xinsi Monastery in Jingzhou during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijayā Entering the Gate of Immeasurability*, one fascicle; also titled *The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of Entering the Gate of Immeasurability* or *The Sūtra of the Questions of the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijayā*. Nineteen sheets. Translated by the lay devotee and upāsaka Wàn Tiānyì at Yèdū during the Later Qí dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Āshudá jīng*, one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Jītami of the Eastern Jin; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Aśvadatta*, one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Song dynasty by the Indian śramaṇa Shi Zhu Fajian at Guangzhou.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra on the Dharma of the Ultimate Truth* (Paramārtha-dharmavijaya-sūtra), one fascicle, fifteen sheets; translated by Bodhiruci during the Yongping to Tiānpíng years of the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dàwēidēngguāng Xiānrén Wènyí jīng*, one fascicle, sixteen sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta at Xingshansi in Cháng'ān during the sixth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two sutras above are different translations of the same original text.
*Bābù fó míng jīng* (Sutra of the Names of Eight Classes of Buddhas), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Gautama Prajñāruci during the Northern Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bā fó míng hào jīng* (Sūtra of the Eight Buddha Names), four sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta at Daxingshan Temple in Chang’an during the sixth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
The two aforementioned sūtras are translations of the same original text.
*Bǎifó míng jīng* (Sūtra of the Names of One Hundred Buddhas), one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bǎifómíng jīng* (Sūtra of the Names of One Hundred Buddhas), consisting of six sheets; translated by Narendrayaśas in Yangzhou during the second year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Aṣṭamaṅgalika-sūtra*, one fascicle; some versions contain incantations. The first translation consisted of twelve sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Aṣṭamaṅgalika-sūtra*, second translation; three sheets. To the right: In the twenty-ninth year of the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Sòng dynasty, Guṇabhadra translated [this text] at the Xīn Temple in Jīngzhōu for the Minister of Works, the Prince of Nánjùn, Qiáo.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Bājíxiáng jīng* (Sūtra of the Eight Auspicious Ones). Translated by Saṃghavarman at the Shòuguāng Hall and other locations during the Liáng dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three preceding sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Nāgadattā-dhītṛ-sūtra*, one fascicle; first translation, four pages. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng-lù (Catalogue of Dharma-rooms).

*Longshi pusa benqi jing* (The Sūtra on the Previous Life of the Bodhisattva Nāgadatta), one fascicle; second translation. The old catalogues state: *Longshi benjing*, two sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two sūtras are the same original text translated separately.
*The Sūtra of the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara of the Amoghapāśa*, one fascicle; translated by Jñānagupta in the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Amoghapāśa-mantra-sūtra*, twelve pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at Cien Monastery during the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.

Extracted from the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Bukong juansuo zhuxin jing*, one fascicle. Translated by Bodhiruci at Foshouji Monastery during the second year of the Changshou era of the Great Zhou dynasty.
Newly included.
The first three volumes consist of different translations of the same text.
*The Sūtra on Maitreya’s Inquiry into His Original Vows*, one fascicle; translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Jīvaka (祇多蜜).
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of four sheets of the *Mile púsà suowèn jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva). Translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye between the second year of the Yongping era and the Tiān'píng era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures are the same original work with different translations.
*Wúsuǒxīwàng jīng* (Sūtra on Having No Expectations), one fascicle; also titled *Xiàngbù jīng* (Elephant-Step Sūtra); twenty-two sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
*Wushu xiwang jing* (Sutra on Having No Expectations), one fascicle. Translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Jītamiṭra.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding sutras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Elephant-Arm Sutra* (Xiang-ye jing), one fascicle: translated during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra.
It appears in the Chángfáng Record.
*Xiàngyè jīng* (Elephant-Axle Sūtra), one fascicle, eighteen sheets. Translated by Zhi Chen in Luoyang during the second year of the Zhongping era of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Dànmó yùduōluò lù*.
The two preceding sutras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra of the Rice Seedling*, one fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the catalogue of Zhenji Temple.

*Liǎoběnshēngsī jīng* (Sūtra on the Understanding of Fundamental Birth and Death), one fascicle; also titled *Dàomiǎn jīng* (Sūtra of the Rice Seedling), five sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Yìběn shēngsī jīng* (Alternative Version of the Sūtra on Birth and Death), one fascicle. Appears in the *Sēngyòu lù*.
The three preceding sūtras are translations of the same original text with different versions.

*Pratītyasamutpāda-sūtra*, one fascicle, two volumes, twenty-two pages: translated by Dharmagupta at the Translation Hall in the Shanglin Garden of the Eastern Capital during the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.
Consulting the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures), it records:

*Fenbie yuanqi jing* (Sūtra on the Analysis of Dependent Origination), one fascicle, two scrolls, twenty-two pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the Great Ci'en Monastery during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.
This is recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). The first two scriptures are translations of the same original text.
*The Scripture of the Great Compassion White Lotus*, one fascicle, in eight or ten rolls, totaling one hundred and sixty-five sheets. According to the record of Zhenji Temple:
This is a separate translation from the same original text as the *Karunāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.
The *Karunāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, one volume in ten fascicles, was first produced by the śramaṇa Daogong of the Northern Liang during the reign of Juqu Mengxun, the King of Xihe.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of ten scrolls of the *Beihuā jīng* (Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra), the second edition. Furthermore, the *Bǎochàng lù* states that it is also titled the *Beiliánhuā jīng* (Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra) and consists of two hundred and forty-three sheets. It was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Guzang, the capital of Liang, during the Xuanshi era of the Northern Liang dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Accomplishment of Great Compassion by the Brahmaṇa Ratnākara*, one fascicle. Translated during the Wu dynasty by Zhi Qian.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Brahmā-śikṣin Preaching His Dream to the Buddha*, one fascicle. Recorded as translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
see Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Scripture on the Brahmā-śikṣin Ratnasāgara Inviting the Tathāgata*, one fascicle. Recorded as translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
I have consulted Sengyou’s Catalogue.
*The Scripture on Dwelling in Seclusion*, one volume in ten fascicles; translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa.
According to Changfang’s Record of Works Included in the Canon:
A separate translation from the same original text as the *Mahākaruṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra*.

It appears in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Dharmafang). *Śuddhodana-māṇava-bodhicitta-praṇidhāna-sūtra*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
I have seen this in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Questions of Bodhisattva Ratnārcis regarding the Appearance of the Lotus Land*, also titled the *Bodhisattvaprakāśana-sūtra*, translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Fànzhì quàn zhuǎnlúnwáng fāpútíxīn jīng*. Regarding this, Sengyou’s catalog notes that Dao’an stated it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
It appears in the *Sēngyòu lù*.
*The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Śāntasvara Asking about the Five Corruptions*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Universal Monarch Resolving His Mind to Seek the Pure Land*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Five Hundred Princes Making Vows for the Pure Land*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazǔ of Hénèi during the Western Jìn dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Original Vows of the Bhikṣu Mahākāruṇika*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmagupta and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Transformation of His Body at the Assembly*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Six Movements of the Dhāraṇī Dharma-gate*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at the Xiaoyao Garden in Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Earth Quaking at the Buddha’s Seat in the World of Good Flowers in the East*, one fascicle. The aforementioned entry in Sengyou’s catalogue states that it was produced by Dharmarakṣa under the direction of Master Dao’an.
*The Sūtra on the Earth Quaking at the Buddha’s Seat in the World of Good Flowers in the East*, one fascicle. Translated during the Later Qin period by Kumārajīva.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Master Chángfáng).
*The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Practice of the Dānapāramitā in Past Lives*, one fascicle. Translated during the era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty by Guṇabhadra.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù.
*The Scripture on Selecting Among Various Evil Worlds in Future Times*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty;
included in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Scripture on Expounding the True Dharma with a Single Sound*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Shi Zhìyán in the fourth year of the Yuánjiā era during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang:
*The Sutra on Mañjuśrī Receiving the Prediction*, one fascicle; the above is from the Record of Zhenji Monastery.
*The Sutra on the World of the Past Buddha Fragrant Lotus*, one fascicle; the above is from the *Sutra of Compassionate Flowers* (*Baihuajing*).
According to the *Jianzhenjisi lu* (Record of the Jianzhen Monastery),
the twenty-one scriptures from the *Beihuajing* (Sutra of the Compassionate Lotus) onwards were all produced from the *Beihuajing*.
(*Dazhou kan ding zhong jing mulu*, Volume 3).
The Great Zhou Catalogue of All Scriptures, Volume Four, compiled by order of the Empress of the Great Tang by the śramaṇa Mingquan and others at the Fo-shou-ji Monastery.
Volume Three: The Catalogue of Mahāyāna Scriptures Translated More Than Once. Volume Three: One Hundred and Eighty Works, totaling Four Hundred and Twenty-one Fascicles.

*Shunquan fangbian jing* (Sūtra on Accordance with Expedient Means), one fascicle, two rolls, forty-three pages. The edition from the Chángfáng collection states it is also titled *Quánlì fangbian jing*, alternatively titled *Wéiquán fangbian jing*, alternatively titled *Shùnquán nǚ jing*, alternatively titled *Lèyīngluò zhuāngyán fangbian jing*, and alternatively titled *Zhuǎnnǚshēn púsà suowèn shòujué jing*. Translated by the śramaṇa Kāṅsēnghuì during the Chìwū era of the Sùnlìng period of the Wú dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of two scrolls, the *Shùnquán fāngbiàn jīng* (Sūtra on Accordance with Expedient Means), also titled the *Zhuǎnnǚshēn púsà jīng* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Transforming Female Gender) or the *Shùn nǚ jīng* (Sūtra of Accordance with Women); thirty-three pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).
The *Suiquan nü jing* (Scripture on Following the Woman of Expedient Means), one fascicle in two volumes, was translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it appears in the *Changfang lu* (Changfang’s Catalogue).
*Yue yingluo zhuangyan jing* (Sūtra on the Adornment of Joyful Necklaces), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yue yingluo zhuangyan fangbian jing* (Sūtra on the Expedient Means of the Adornment of Joyful Necklaces), one fascicle—also known as the *Dacheng yingluo zhuangyan jing* (Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Adornment of Joyful Necklaces) or the *Zhuan nushen jing* (Sūtra on Transforming the Female Body)—thirty sheets. Translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Shi Fǎhǎi.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The above five scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Púsà yíngluò jīng* (Bodhisattva-ābharaṇa-sūtra), one volume in twelve fascicles, or fourteen fascicles; also known as the *Xiànqián bào jīng* (Sūtra on Manifest Retribution). Translated by the Śramaṇa Jñātāmitra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bodhisattvamaṇyālaṃkāra-sūtra*, in sixteen, fourteen, or twelve fascicles, totaling three hundred and thirty-seven sheets. Translated in Cháng'ān by Zhú Fóniàn during the Former Qín dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):

*The Sūtra on the Original Vow and Activities of the Bodhisattva’s Diadem* (*Pusa yingluo benye jing*), one fascicle in two volumes, forty-two pages. Translated by Zhu Fonian in Chang’an during the Former Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle of two scrolls: the *Bodhisattva-ābharaṇa-mūlakarma-sūtra*. Translated by the śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan in the fourth year of the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yíngluò běnyè jīng* (The Scripture on the Original Acts of the Garland), one volume in two fascicles; also known as the *Púsà yíngluò jīng* (The Scripture of the Bodhisattva Garland), thirty-seven pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Dàoyán during the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The above five scriptures are different translations of the same original text.
*Guānfó sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Guānfó sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha), in ten rolls or eight rolls; also known as the *Guānfó sānmèi hǎi jīng* (Sūtra on the Ocean-like Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha); one hundred eighty-four pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Guṇabhadra in Yangzhou during the Yongchū era of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

The first two scriptures are translations of the same original text: the *Akṣobhyavyūha-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, also titled *Akṣobhya-sūtra* or *Akṣobhya-vyākaraṇa-bodhisattva-śikṣāpada-parivarta-sūtra*. First translation: forty-seven sheets. Translated by Lokakṣema in Luoyang during the Jianhe era of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*. One fascicle of two scrolls:

the *Āchù fóguó jīng* (Sūtra on the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha). Second extraction; also known as the *Āchù fóchà zhū púsà xuéjiè pǐn jīng* (Sūtra on the Chapter on the Training Precepts of the Bodhisattvas in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya), which differs slightly from the translation by Zhi Chen. Translated by Zhìdào gēn during the Cheng Emperor era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two scriptures above are translations of the same original text.

*The Tathāgata’s Adorned Wisdom Radiance Entering the Realm of All Buddhas Sūtra*, one fascicle (or two fascicles), also titled *The Sūtra on Transcending All Buddhas*, forty sheets. Translated by Dharmaruci at Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Xuānwǔ of the Later Wèi dynasty.
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.

There is one fascicle of the *Dù zhū fó jìngjiè zhìguāng yán jīng* (Sutra on the Adornment of the Light of Wisdom Entering the Realm of All Buddhas), also known as the *Rúlái zhuāngyán zhìhuì guānmíng rù yīqiè fó jìngjiè jīng* (Sutra on the Tathāgata’s Adorned Wisdom Light Entering the Realm of All Buddhas). This was translated between the second year of the Yǒngpíng era and the Tiānping era of the Later Wèi dynasty.
The śramaṇa Bodhiruci translated [this] in Luoyang and Ye;
it appears in the catalogue of Sengyou (Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālaṃkāra-sūtra*, with fifteen additional pages of characters. To its right, during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty, Mandaraka and Saṃghavarman [collated it].
Translated at three locations— the Shouguang Hall in Yangdu, the Zhanyun Pavilion at Zhengguan Monastery, and [another site]—
as recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
