These three aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recollection*, one fascicle, in six (or five) rolls; also known as *The Bodhisattva Sūtra on the Samādhi of Buddha-Recollection*. Total: 113 sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇadeva at the capital of Yangdu in the sixth year of the Daming era of the Song dynasty.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).

The *Mahāvaipulya Mahāsaṃnipāta Bodhisattva Buddhanusmṛti-samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle in ten rolls and one hundred thirty-two pages, was translated by Jñānagupta at the Translation Hall in the Shanglin Garden of the Eastern Capital during the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Lù* (Catalogue) of Inner and Outer Scriptures.
The first two sections comprise sixteen fascicles that are different translations of the same original text.

*Mahāsāṃghika-nirgrantha-putra-sūtra*, one volume in seven, eight, or ten fascicles, totaling one hundred and sixty-three pages. Translated by Bodhiruci at the residence of Prince Runan in the capital Luoyang during the first year of the Zhengguang era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Consulting the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng):

*The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Practice of Skillful Means, the Realm of Supernatural Transformations*, one fascicle in three rolls. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two sections, comprising ten fascicles, are different translations of the same text.
*The Scripture on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Dhāraṇīdhara*, one part in four fascicles (or three fascicles, sixty-one sheets). Translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa in Cháng'ān.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
The *Cijin pusa jing* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Dharmodgata), one fascicle in three rolls, was translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin;
this is recorded in the *Changfang lu* (Catalogue of Changfang).

The *Dharmaparyāya on Holding the World* (*Chishi jing*), one fascicle in four volumes, also titled the *Sūtra on the Dharma Seal* (*Fayin jing*), consisting of eighty-nine pages; translated by the śramaṇa Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Śubhabāhu-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, twenty-nine sheets. According to the record of Dharmottara, it was translated by the Śramaṇa Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
A different translation of the same text as the *Dhāraṇīdhara-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*.
One fascicle of an excerpt from the "Chapter on the Good Shoulder" (*Sujāta-parivarta*), taken from the *Bhadradatta-bodhisattva-sūtra*. The above is recorded in the catalogue of Zhenji Temple.
The five scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture on Mañjuśrī Manifesting the Treasure Store* (文殊師利現寶藏經), one fascicle in three or two rolls, also titled *The Scripture on the Adornment and Purity of Mañjuśrī’s Buddha-field* (文殊師利佛土嚴淨經), consisting of forty-nine sheets; translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mañjuśrī-prabhāsa-ratnagarbha-sūtra*, in two volumes and forty-nine sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhi Fadu in the first year of the Yongxing era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
It appears in Changfang’s Record.
The Record of Zhenji Temple states that it is a different translation of the same original text as the *Mahāvaipulya-ratnakaraṇḍa-sūtra*.

The *Mañjuśrī-prabhāsa-ratnagarbha-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, also titled the *Ratnagarbha-prakāśana-sūtra* or in three volumes; translated by the śramaṇa An-fa-qin of the country of Anxi at Luoyang during the Taian era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The first three sutras share the same original text but were translated separately.

*The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Huisang’s Inquiry on Great Skillful Means*, one fascicle, in two or one scrolls. Translated during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han by the lay devotee Yan Fotiao of Qingxin in Linhuai at Luoyang.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

It states: *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Huìshàng Asking about Great Skillful Means*, one fascicle in two volumes; also titled *The Scripture on Great Skillful Means* or *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Huìshàng*, or said to be originally called *The Scripture on Skillful Means and Expedients*, or *The Scripture on the Infinite Deliverance by Expedients*. It consists of thirty sheets and was translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the sixth year of the Tàikāng era of the Western Jìn dynasty.
I consulted the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

The *Mahāyānopāya-sūtra* (*Dàchéng fāngbiàn jīng*) consists of one fascicle in three volumes, or alternatively two volumes in forty-seven pages; it is the third appearance [of this text], slightly differing from the translation by Dharmarakṣa and Saṃghadatta. It is a separate translation of the same original as the *Bodhisattvaparipṛcchā-sūtra* (*Huìshàng púsà suowèn jīng*). It was translated in Luoyang by the Indian lay practitioner Zhu Nántí during the second year of the Yuánxī era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, two scrolls of the *Shànghuì púsà jīng* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Shànghuì), also known as the *Shànquán jīng* (Sūtra of Skillful Means), also known as the *Shànghuì púsà wèn shànquán jīng* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Shànghuì’s Inquiry into Skillful Means), also known as the *Dàchéng fāngbiàn jīng* (Mahāyāna Sūtra of Skillful Means), also named the *Dàshànquán jīng* (Great Sūtra of Skillful Means). Translated by the monk Saṃghadeva of Liangzhou during the Northern Liang dynasty.
According to the *Shixing lu* (Record of the Beginning of Prosperity), the first four scriptures share the same original text but have been translated separately.

The *Hongdao guangxian sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Extensive Manifestation of the Propagation of the Way) is one fascicle in four rolls; it is also called the *Anouda qingfo jing* (Sūtra on the Invitation of the Buddha by Anavatapta), or simply the *Jingangmen dingyi jing* (Sūtra on the Adamantine Gate of Concentrated Intent). Sometimes the word "samādhi" is omitted. It consists of sixty-three sheets. In total, there are four titles for this work, which contains ten chapters.
One manuscript contains only seven chapters,
lacking the middle three;
another manuscript contains only the first five chapters.
Translated at Chang’an by Dharmarakṣa in the second year of the Yongjia era of the Western Jin.
The record in the *Chángfáng lù* is as stated above.
Furthermore, the *Bǎochàng lù* lists six titles.
It is also titled the *Anavatapta Sūtra*, the *Anavatapta Nāgarāja Sūtra*,
and the *Sūtra on the Extensive Manifestation of the Buddha Way*.
The remainder is the same as the first entry.
*Anavatapta-nāgarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, fifty-three pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty in Chang’an.
Having consulted the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog), the above two works in six fascicles are translations of the same original text with different translations.

The *Puchao sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Universal Transcendence) consists of one work in three or four fascicles; this second edition is a different translation of the same original as the *Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra* translated by Zhi Chen of the Han dynasty. It is also titled *Wenshu puchao sanmei jing* (Mañjuśrī’s Sūtra on the Samādhi of Universal Transcendence) or simply *Puchao jing*. It comprises eighty sheets. To its right [is noted]: translated by Zhu Fahu at Chang’an during the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures):
*Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; the first sixty-four sheets were translated by Zhi Chen of the Later Han dynasty at Luoyang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
Furthermore, there is a second edition of the *Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra* in two fascicles; the right-hand version was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fàngbō jīng* (Sūtra on Setting Aside the Alms Bowl), one fascicle; a separate chapter from the *Pǔchāo jīng* translated differently [by Dharmarakṣa]. Recorded in Sengyou’s catalog as eight sheets. *Xīnběn jìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Innate Purity of Mind), one fascicle; an excerpt from the *Pǔchāo sānmèi jīng*. Dao’an states that it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty; it appears in Sengyou’s catalog.
*The Scripture on the Three Young Boys*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazang of Henei during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Scripture of Puśya the Youthful*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Dharma-pāla).
One fascicle of the *Wǎnggǔ zàoxíng jīng* (Sūtra on Past Deeds), translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthita during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jǔbō jīng* (The Scripture on Holding the Alms Bowl), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng lù (Chángfáng Catalogue).
*Wúwǒ jīng* (The Scripture on the Absence of Self), one fascicle. Translated by Zhú Tánwúlán at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángzhōu during the reign of Emperor Xiào Wǔ of the Eastern Jìn dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The twelve scriptures listed above were all translated from the *Pǔchāo sānmèi jīng* (Sutra of the Universal Surpassing Samādhi).

The *Dà guǎndìng jīng* (Great Consecration Sutra), one volume in twelve fascicles—or nine fascicles or five fascicles—totaling one hundred and twelve pages, was translated by Śrīmitra in Yangzhou during the Yuan Emperor’s reign of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūn-ien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

*Sān-guī-wǔ-jì-dài-pèi-hù-shēn-zhòu-jīng* (One Scroll on the Sutra of the Three Refuges, Five Precepts, and Protective Amulets for Guarding the Body). Right: Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
It appears in the *Sēng-yòu-lu* (Monk You’s Catalogue).
*The Sūtra of the Seven Thousand Two Hundred Divine Kings Who Protect Bhikṣus through Empowerment*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.

*The Sūtra of the Empowerment Mantra for Protecting Bhikṣuṇīs by One Hundred and Twenty Thousand Divine Kings*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa;
it appears in the *Sengyou lu*.
*The Sūtra of the Hundred-knot Spirit-King for Protecting the Body through Consecration*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Sūtra of the Spirit-King of the Palace and Residence for Guarding and Stationing the Left and Right*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
I have consulted Sengyou’s Catalogue.

*The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of Guanding’s Tomb and the Divine Incantations of the Four Quarters*, one fascicle. Regarding this, Dao’an states that it was translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
*The Great Divine Incantation Sūtra of the Sealing of Demons by Guanding* (1 scroll). Right: Dao’an states that this was translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
It is recorded in the *Sengyou lu*.
*The Great Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Consecrated Maṇiratna*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.

*The Sūtra of the Great Dhāraṇī for Summoning the Dragon Kings of the Five Directions and Subjugating Pestilence*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
*Jian sengyou lu*.
*Guanding fantsen zhousu ce jing*, one fascicle. The aforementioned [work] was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty, according to Dao’an;
it appears in the *Sengyou lu*.

*Guǎngjìng pǔguǎng jīng* (The Sūtra of Universal Extensiveness of Empowerment), one fascicle; also known as the *Pǔguǎng púsà jīng* (Sūtra of Bodhisattva Pǔguǎng) or the *Guǎngjìng suíyuàn wǎngshēng shífāng jìngtǔ jīng* (Sūtra of Empowerment for Rebirth in the Pure Lands of the Ten Directions According to One’s Vows). Dao’an states that it was translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
I have consulted Sengyou’s Catalogue (*Chu sanzang jiji*).

One fascicle of the *Suiyuan wangsheng jing* (Scripture on Rebirth According to One's Vows), also titled the *Puguang jing* (Universal Radiance Scripture), was translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
It appears in the catalogue of Dharmottara.
*Guanding jing* (Abhiṣeka Sūtra), one fascicle in nine rolls. Translated by Śrīmitra during the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
The *Changfang lu* states that it was extracted from the *Zalu*.

*Dajiangjun shenzhou jing* (Sūtra of the Divine Spells of the Great General), one roll. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in Yandu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Lóngwáng jièyuàn wǔlóng shénzhòu jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Dragon Deity Spells of the Dragon King’s Vow). Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng):

one fascicle of the *Wǔlóng zhòujīng* (Sūtra of the Five Dragon Spells), from the *Zhēnjì sì lù* (Record of Zhēnjì Monastery). The above seventeen sūtras are from the *Shàngdà guǎngdìng jīng* (Great Universal Empowerment Sūtra).

The *Jízhòngdé sānmèijīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Accumulating All Virtues) in one part, either two or three fascicles, also known as the *Jíyíqiè fúdé sānmèijīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Gathering All Merit and Virtue), consisting of fifty-seven sheets. Translated by Zhú Fáhù of the Jin Dynasty.
*Equi-jì-sānmèi-jīng* (Sūtra on the Equal Collection of Samādhis), one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bó Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng-lù*.

The *Sarvapuṇyasamuccaya-samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle in three volumes, extracted from the *Samantabhadrotsāhana-samādhi Sūtra*, totaling fifty-eight pages. Translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.
In the *Jianzhenji si lu* (Record of the Jianzhen Temple), the upper section lists three sūtras that share the same original text but have different translations.

The first is the *Dundubhitarasvabhāva-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one volume in two fascicles or three fascicles, also titled the *Dundubhitarasvabhāva-sūtra*. It originally consisted of fifty-seven sheets. It was translated at Luoyang during the Jianning era of the Later Han dynasty by Zhi Chen.
This is found in the *Chángfáng lù* and the *Nèidiǎn lù*.

The *Dàshù jīnnáluowáng suowèn jīng*, one fascicle in four rolls, the second edition, consisting of seventy-eight pages, was translated by Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān during the Hóngshí era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Having consulted the *Chángfáng lù*, it is seen that the above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Fǎjìng jīng* (Dharmādarśa-sūtra), one fascicle in two volumes, or one volume in twenty-six pages. Translated during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han by the lay practitioner An Xuan, together with Yan Fotiao, in Luoyang.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
One fascicle, or two fascicles, totaling twenty-six sheets, of the *Fǎjìng jīng* (Dharmadarśana-sūtra), translated during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty by the lay practitioner (upāsaka) Zhīqián.
From the *Chángfáng lù*. The two sūtras above are the same original text, translated separately.

*Yugāra-vai-pṛcchā-bodhisattva-caryā-sūtra*, one fascicle (or two fascicles), the third translation; also known as the *Yugāra-gṛhapati-sūtra*. It is the same text as those translated by Kang Sengkai of the Wei dynasty and Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty, differing only slightly in length. Thirty sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty during the reign of Emperor Wu.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle, or two fascicles, of the *Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra*; the second translation, thirty sheets. Translated by Saṃghavarman at the Baima Monastery in Luoyang during the Jiaping era of Emperor Qi of the Former Wei.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Ugraparipṛcchā-sūtra*, in two fascicles or one; the second extraction above was translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Shorter Sūtra of Ugga* (1 fascicle). This is distinct from the *Sūtra of the Elder Ugga*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;
recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Questions of Uggarāva on Bodhisattvas* (1 fascicle). Translated by Bai Fazǔ during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Questions of the Householder Ugga*. The above was translated during the Yuánjiā era of the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra from Jibin (Kashmir), whose Chinese name was Fǎxiù.
Translated at the Jetavana Monastery.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Dharmafang). The six scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*Yuè míng tóng zǐ jīng* (Sūtra of the Moon-Bright Boy), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Yuè míng tóng nán jīng* (Sūtra of the Moon-Bright Boy) or *Yuè míng púsà sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra of the Moon-Bright Bodhisattva’s Samādhi), seven sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wucheng era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded from the *Chenziji si lu*.

One fascicle of the *Candraprabha-kumāra-sūtra*; it is a different translation of the same text as the *Shenri jing*, *Shenri dou jing*, and *Shiliyue jing*—these three sūtras being of the same original. Also titled the *Yueming tongzi jing*. Ten sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
*The Original Scripture on the Son of Shenri*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra at the Jetavana Monastery during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture of the Elder Śrīgupta*, one fascicle in two volumes; also known as *The Scripture of the Elder Śrīguṇa*. It is a different translation of the same text as the *Scripture of the Layman Sunakṣatra* and the *Scripture of the Youth Candraprabha*. Twenty-six pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Narendrayaśas at Chang’an during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.

Consulting the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog), there is one fascicle of the *Śrīlaulya-sūtra*, which appears in Sengyou’s catalog; the five sūtras listed above are thus different translations of the same original text.
There is also one fascicle of the *Daśadharma-sūtra*, translated by Buddhayaśas at Luoyang and Ye during the Later Wei dynasty.
*Shīfǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Dharmas), one fascicle, twenty sheets. Translated by Saṃghavarman at the capital of Yangdu during the Putong era of the Liang dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding sutras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sutra of the Hundred Treasures Stored Within* (Nèizàng Bǎibǎo jīng), one fascicle, also titled *The Sutra of the Hundred Items Stored Within* (Nèizàng Bǎipǐn jīng), consists of eight sheets. It was translated by An Shigao in Luoyang during the second year of the Yuanjia era of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Nèizàng bǎibǎo jīng* (Sūtra of the Inner Treasury of a Hundred Jewels), one fascicle, ten sheets. Translated by Zhi Chen during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*. The two sūtras above are translations of the same original text.

*Yandaosuye jing* (Sutra on the Exposition of the Deeds of the Laity and the Clergy), one fascicle; also known as *Wuye* (Without the Character "Deed"). Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty during the right [era].

Appears in the Chángfáng Record. *Yandaosuye jing*, one fascicle; the second version, which differs slightly from the one translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu period, consists of ten sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Shèngjiān of the Western Qin at the State of Hénán.
Some call him Fajian;
others call him Jian Gong.
Both entries are found in the Changfang lu.
The two sutras above are translations of the same original text.
*Ratnajāla-sūtra*, one fascicle, also known as the *Ratnajāla-kumāra-sūtra*, thirty-two sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Baowang jing* (Jewel Net Sūtra), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two sutras above are translations of the same original text.

*Mañjuśrīparipṛcchābodhicittabhūmi-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Bodhicitta-sūtra*, the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra*, or the *Bodhicittācaryā-sūtra*—eight sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān during the Hongshí era of the Later Qín dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra*, second translation, eleven pages. Translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xiàngtóu jīngshè jīng* (Sūtra on the Elephant Head Monastery), third extraction, nine sheets. Translated by Vinītāruci at Xingshān Temple during the second year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Bodhi wúxíng jīng* (Sūtra on Non-Action of Bodhi), seven pages; one fascicle of the *Dàchéng jiāyeshān dǐng jīng* (Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Summit of Mount Gayā), ten pages. Both were translated by Bodhiruci at the Eastern Temple of the Great Zhou in the second year of the Chángshòu era of the Great Zhou.
Newly included in the catalog.
The five scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*Wencheng Shí'èr yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination Spoken by Wencheng), one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by An Shigao, Prince of the Parthian Kingdom, during the Jianchu era of Emperor Huan of the Later Han.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Kāishéng shí'èr yīnluán jīng* (Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination from the Kāishéng Era), one fascicle; the second translation. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhīyào in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Zhìfáng).

*Bēitu shùxià sīwéi shí'èr yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination under the Pāṭala Tree), one fascicle; second translation. Translated by Zhīqiān during the Huángwǔ era of the Wú dynasty.

*The Sutra on Contemplating the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination under the Pippala Tree*, one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. Appears in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng) and the *Nèidiǎn lù* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures).
*Śālistamba-sūtra* (Twelve Links of Dependent Origination), one fascicle; fourth translation, four pages. Translated by Guṇavidi at Yangzhou during the Yongming era of the Southern Qi dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The five sūtras above are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra on the Secret Retention of the Immeasurable Gate* (1 fascicle, 8 pages), translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù.

The *Ānandamukha-sūtra*, one fascicle, is identical to the *Vimala-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. It was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master An Faqin of the Western Jin dynasty during the reign of Emperor Hui at Luoyang.
It appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sutra of the Dharani for the Infinite Destruction of Māra*, one fascicle, twelve pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bai Fazang of Henei during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sūtra of the New Subtle and Secret Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; the second [recension] issued [from this]. Also titled *The Sūtra on Attaining the Way, Subduing Māras, and Obtaining All-Knowledge*. Translated by Buddhabhadra at Mount Lu in the second year of the Long’an era (398 CE) of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, eight sheets, titled *Chūshēng wúliàngmén chí jīng* (Sutra on the Dharani of the Gate of Producing Immeasurable Doors). Translated by Buddhabhadra at Mount Lu and in Yangzhou during the Yuánxī era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Ānán mùqié níhélí tuóluóní jīng* (The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of Ānanda Mukhanirhāra), one fascicle, twelve sheets; also known as *Wúliàng wēimì chí jīng* (The Sūtra of the Immeasurable Secret Retention), *Bátuóluó wúliàngmén chí jīng* (The Sūtra of Bhadra’s Immeasurable Gate Retention), or *Gōngdé zhípò mó tuóluóní jīng* (The Sūtra of the Merit that Directly Shatters Māra’s Dhāraṇī). Translated during the Northern Wei dynasty by Buddhayaśas at Baima Monastery in Luoyang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Wúliàngmén pómó tuólóní jīng* (12 sheets). Translated by Guǒdézhí of the Dàmíng era of the Song dynasty at Jīngzhōu.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Ānàndamukha-nihārida-jīng*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Chū-muryō-ji-mon-kyō* (Sutra on the Gate of Immeasurable Retentions), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra (translated into Chinese as Gōngdéxián) during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty at Jīhuán Temple in Yangdu in the twelfth year of the Yuánjiā era.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Śāriputra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, nine pages. Translated by the Śramaṇa Saṃghabhadra of Fúshā during the Liáng dynasty at the Shòuguāng Palace in Yángdū.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Yīxiàng chūshēng púsà jīng* (Sūtra on the Sole Path to the Birth of Bodhisattvas), one fascicle, twelve pages. Translated at Dàxīngshàn Temple by Jñānagupta in the fifteenth year of the Kāiyuáng era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The eleven scriptures above are translations of the same original text with different translations.

*Zhǎngzhězǐ zhì jīng* (The Scripture on the Elder’s Son’s Regulation), one scroll; also known as *Zhì jīng*, six sheets. Translated by An Shigao, Prince of the Parthian Kingdom, during the Later Han dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang:
*The Scripture on the Departed* (one fascicle), also known as the *Scripture on the Departed Youth*. Translated by Bai Fazang during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.

*The Scripture on the Departure of the Youth*, one fascicle; the second [entry]. Also titled *The Scripture on the Elder’s Regulation*, or simply *The Scripture on Regulation*; it is also called *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Departure*, or simply *The Scripture on Departure*. Two sheets. Translated by Zhi Fadu in the first year of the Yongning era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of four sheets of the *Púsà shì jīng* (Sūtra on the Departure of the Bodhisattva). Translated by Ānyáng Hóu Jīngshēng, the younger brother of Zhūqú Méngxùn, the Prince of Hēxī, during the Northern Liáng period.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Zhìjīng* (Scripture on Regulation), from Zhēnjì Temple and the *Chángfáng lù*. The five scriptures above are the same text with different translations.
The *Dúzǐ jīng* (Gavāṃpati Sūtra), one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Zhīqián during the Huángwǔ era of the Wù dynasty.
The *Gavāṃpati-sūtra* (one fascicle), also known as the *Vatsa-sūtra*, translated by Dharmaruci of the Eastern Jin dynasty; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
It is found in the *Dànmó yùduōluò lù*.

*Fuguang jing* (Sutra of Floating Light), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Ruguang jing* (Sutra of Milk Light). Translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Qiduomi. Appears in the *Changfang lu*. *Ruguang fo jing* (Sutra of the Buddha Milk Light), one fascicle;
the same original text as the *Duzi jing* (Sutra of the Vatsiputriya), translated separately in seven sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
*Fujōkyō* (The Scripture on the Unadorned Woman), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Garbhakośa-sūtra*, one fascicle; second translation, four pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Vimaladattā-bhaginī-sūtra*, one fascicle. The *Chángfáng lù* states it is the *Rìgòu shīnǚ jīng* (Sūtra of the Daughter Vimaladattā), three pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Nie Daozhen.
*The Woman in the Belly Listening to the Sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *The Unadorned and Uncorrected Woman’s Sūtra*, three sheets. Translated by the Northern Liang śramaṇa Dharmakṣema.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
One fascicle of the *Zhǎnnǚshēn jīng* (Sūtra on Transforming the Female Body), twenty sheets. To the right:
translated during the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmamitra.
Translated at Jetavana Monastery.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. One fascicle:
*The Daughter in the Womb Listens to the Sūtra*. Second appearance; identical in substance to the *Bùzhuāngjiào nǚ jīng*. Dated the first year of the Yongping era of the Southern Qi dynasty.
Recited by the śramaṇa Shi Faha.
This is identical to the *Pusa yingluo benye jing* (Sūtra on the Original Acts of the Bodhisattva’s Garland) translated by Dharmakṣema, though without the ornate embellishments.
Recorded from the Zhenji Temple catalog. The ten sūtras above are translations of the same original text.
*Mahāvaipulya-sūtra-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; second translation; three pages. Translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Zhuan you jing* (Sūtra on the Transformation of Existence), one fascicle, two pages; translated by Buddhayaśas during the Wei dynasty.
It appears in the *Dharmoktara lu*. The two sūtras above are translations of the same original text.

*Maitreya-buddha-jāta-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Maitreya-āgami-avataraṇa-sūtra*. First translation; seventeen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taian era of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).

The *Mile chengfo jing* (Sūtra on Maitreya’s Attainment of Buddhahood), one fascicle, is the second translation; it is largely identical with minor variations to the version translated by Dharmarakṣa. It consists of nineteen sheets. This was translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the fourth year of the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.

In the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng), there is one fascicle of eight sheets titled *Mílè zuò fó shíshì jīng* (Sūtra on the Events of Maitreya’s Attaining Buddhahood); the above is from the *Bǎochàng lù* (Record of Bǎochàng).
There is one fascicle of three sheets titled *Mílè lái shí jīng* (Sūtra on Maitreya’s Coming); the above is from the *Dámó yùduōluò lù* (Record of Dhamayuttara).
*Maitreya Bodhisattva’s Original Vow to Await the Time for Attaining Buddhahood*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty;
appears in the Changfang Record.

*Maitreya’s Descent to Be Reborn*, one fascicle, also titled *Maitreya’s Reception of the Prediction*, seven sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.
It appears in the *Chū innenroku* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures) and the *Chōbōroku*.

*Guān Mílé púsà shàngshēng Dōushuì tiān jīng* (Sutra on the Visualization of Bodhisattva Maitreya’s Rebirth in Tuṣita Heaven), one fascicle; also known as the *Mílé shàngshēng jīng*. Translated by Jūgoku Kyōshō during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mílè chéngfó jīng* (Sūtra on Maitreya’s Attainment of Buddhahood), the third extraction; it is also called the *Xiàshēng jīng* (Sūtra on the Descent). The preface states: "The Great Wise Śāriputra. Translated by the Qi dynasty monk Shì Dàobiāo.
Re-edited by the śramaṇa Daozheng of Jiangzhou;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù.
*Mílè xiàshēng jīng* (Sūtra on Maitreya’s Descent), one fascicle; the third translation. [Compiled] during the third year of the Chéngshèng era of Emperor Wŭ of the Liáng dynasty.
Translated by Paramārtha at Baotian Monastery in Yuzhang County;
recorded in the Chángfáng Lù.
The eleven sūtras listed above are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Aśoka’s Crown Prince Losing His Eyes*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Chen at Luoyang during the Jianhe to Zhongping years of Emperor Huan of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *A-yù-wáng-tài-zǐ huài-mù yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Prince Aśoka’s Blinding), also titled the *Wángzǐ fǎyì huài-mù yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Prince Dharmavardhana’s Blinding). Translated on the eighth day of the sixth month in the second year of the Jiānchū era during the Former Qín dynasty.
Dharmalan-di, together with Fonian,
translated [this] for Yao Min, the Minister of State, in the city of Chang'an.
One manuscript lacks the word "sūtra."
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Prinaprabha-rājakumāra-cakṣur-vināśa-hetupratyaya-sūtra*, the second translation. Translated by Zhu Fonian during the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin.
The above three scriptures, recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*, are different translations of the same original text.

*The Essential Collection of All Buddhas* (諸佛要集經), one fascicle in two volumes, also titled *The Essential Collection Sūtra* (要集經), consisting of forty-nine sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng):
*The Essential Collection of All Buddhas Sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes. Translated by Nie Dàozhēn during the Tàikāng era of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*. The two sūtras above are the same original text translated separately.

*The Scripture of the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture on the Eradication of Transgressions and Birth-and-Death*, or *The Scripture of the Original Vows of the Medicine Master Lapis Lazuli Light*. Thirteen sheets. Translated by Huìjiǎn of Lùnyè Monastery in the capital during the Dà míng era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
*Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabhāsa-pūrvapraṇidhāna-sūtra*, one fascicle, twelve sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta at the Shanglin Garden in the Eastern Capital during the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.

Extracted from the *Lù dìng nèi diǎn lù* (Catalogue of the Definitive Inner Scriptures). *The Scripture on the Merit of the Fundamental Vows of Bhaisajyaguru Tathāgata*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated by Xuanzang at Ci'en Monastery in the capital during the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Extracted from the *Chūn-ien-lu* (Record of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
The three sutras above are different translations of the same original text.
*Mahāyāna-ratnamegha-sūtra*, one fascicle in eight volumes: translated by the Śramaṇa Subhūti of Funan during the Chen dynasty.
Translated at Zhijing Monastery within the capital city of Yangdu.
Recorded in the Changfang Catalogue.
One fascicle of the *Ratnamegha-sūtra* in seven rolls; the first portion, consisting of one hundred and twenty sheets, was produced during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
The *Tripiṭaka-maṇḍala-sūtra* and others were translated in the capital of Yangdu;
this appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Ratnamegha-sūtra*, one fascicle in ten rolls and one hundred eighty-six pages: the above was translated at Foshouji Monastery by the Tripiṭaka Master Varmasena in the second year of the Chángshòu era of the Great Zhou dynasty.
Newly included.
The above three sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Sarvadharmavīrarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-one sheets; translated by Lokakṣema of the Later Han dynasty.
The *Dharmavīrarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, translated during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Dharmamitra; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
It appears in the *Dàmó yùduōluò lù*.
The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, eleven pages; both [texts] concerning its efficacy were translated by Yaśakṛta during the Later Zhou dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Shíyīmiàn Guānshìyīn Shénzhòu Jīng* (The Divine Incantation Sūtra of the Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara). Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuánzàng of the Great Táng within the Jīnbāo Gate of the Northern Palace.
Extracted from the *Lù* (Catalogues) of Inner and Outer Scriptures.
The above two sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra of the Buddha-Usnīsa Dhāraṇī and its Efficacy*, one fascicle: translated in the fourth year of the Baoding era of Emperor Wu of the Zhou dynasty by Jñānayaśas and others at the Four Heavenly Kings Temple in the Old City of Chang’an.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fóding zūnshèng tuólóní jīng*, one fascicle, eight pages. Translated by Buddhāpālita during the second year of the Yongchun era of the Great Tang.
Newly included in the catalog:

*The Sūtra of the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle, eight pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara at Dongtaiyuan Temple in the Eastern Capital during the first year of the Yonglong era of the Great Tang.
On the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month of the first year of the Tiān-cè Wàn-suì era, these were received by imperial decree and entered into the records for implementation.
The three aforementioned sūtras share the same original text but are distinct translations.

*Mahāyāna-samatā-nirdeśa-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes (also in four volumes), also titled *Buddha-daśabhūmi-sūtra* or *Sarva-buddha-caryā-praveśa-jñāna-vairocana-kośa-sūtra*, forty sheets. Translated during the fifth year of the Tiānhé era of the Later Zhou dynasty by Jñānayaśas, Kujūta, and others.
Translated at the Four Heavenly Kings Temple (Sìtiānwáng Sì) in the Old City of Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

One fascicle, two scrolls, thirty-nine sheets: the *Zhèngqì Dàchéng Jīng* (Sūtra on the Seal of Accord with the Mahāyāna). Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara in the first year of the Yǒnglóng era of the Great Táng.
Translated at the Eastern Taiyuan Temple;
newly included in the compilation.
The two aforementioned sutras are different translations of the same original text.

*Yishi jing* (Sutra on the Transference of Consciousness), one fascicle in two volumes, forty-three pages. Translated by Jñānagupta and others at Daxingshan Monastery in Chang’an during the eleventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahāyāna-vijñapti-prakāśana-sūtra*, consisting of two scrolls and twenty-five sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara at the Eastern Taiyuán Monastery during the first year of the Yǒnglóng era of the Great Táng.
Newly included.
The two scriptures above are different translations of the same text.
One fascicle of the *Śūramgama-pradīpa-sūtra* (Shǔ Pǔyào jīng) in eight rolls; the right-hand [text] was first produced.

The *Puyao jing* (Sutra of Universal Radiance), one volume in eight fascicles, also known as the *Fangdeng benqi jing* (Sutra of the Origin of the Vaipulya), second translation; one hundred eighty-two pages. Translated by Zhu Fahu at Tianshui Temple in the second year of the Yongjia era of Emperor Huai of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Puyao jing* (Sūtra of Universal Radiance), in eight or six rolls; the third translation. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhìyán and Bǎoyún and others during the fourth year of the Yuánjiā era of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*The Scripture on the Ten Abodes and the Severing of Bonds*, one fascicle in eight volumes (or four volumes). Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa at the Baima Monastery in Luoyang during the Yongping era of the Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, ten scrolls, the second edition of the *Shízhù duànjié jīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Stages and Severing the Bonds). Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhú Fóniàn of Liangzhou during the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture on the Ten Abodes and the Severing of Bonds*, one fascicle, fourteen (or eleven) rolls, totaling two hundred fifty-four pages. Translated by Zhu Fonian together with Dharma Master Dao’an during the eleventh year of the Jianyuan era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Ji guo si lu* and the *Seng you lu*.
The three aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Wu zi bao qie jing*, one fascicle, six sheets; translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sutra of the Jewel Casket Without Letters*, one fascicle; second translation. Translated by Buddhayaśas at the Baima Monastery in Luoyang and the Jinhua Monastery in Ye between the sixth year of the Zhengguang era and the Yuangxiang era of the Northern Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù.
*Mahāvaipulya-ratnakaraṇḍa-sūtra*, one fascicle, in two or three rolls, forty-nine sheets. [Compiled] during the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Translated by Guṇabhadra at Xinsi Monastery in Jingzhou;
recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.

*Mahāyāna-akṣara-vimukta-samantaprabhā-garbha-sūtra*, one fascicle, six sheets. [This] was translated by Divākara at Taoyuan Monastery in the Western Capital during the second year of the Yongchun era of the Great Tang.
Newly included.
The above four sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-vyūha-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; also known as *Buddhakṣetra-vyūha-sūtra* or *Vyūha-śuddha-buddhakṣetra-sūtra*; forty sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa at Luoyang during the Taixi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Foshuo pusa sanfa jing*, one fascicle.
The above was translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty;
it appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Pusa fengshi yita zuo yuan nian jing* (The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Offering and Making Vows at a Stūpa), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Zhu zi* (Various Characters). Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Questions of the Elder Prāhārika Concerning the Dharma of Bodhisattvas*, one fascicle. The above was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
this is recorded in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

*The Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Siṃhakrama-raja Concerning the Arousing of the Mind [by Mañjuśrī]*, one fascicle. The above was translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Siṃhagāmin-Garjitasvara Regarding Mañjuśrī’s Attainment of Buddhahood*, along with the preceding five sūtras, is an offshoot of the *Mañjuśrī-buddhakṣetra-vyūha-sūtra*.

*Xiánjié sānmèijīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Bhadrakalpa), one fascicle, ten scrolls; *Xiánjié jīng* (Sūtra of the Bhadrakalpa), one fascicle, thirteen scrolls, or ten scrolls, totaling two hundred and seventeen sheets. Both were translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Fahu at Chang’an during the Yuankang era of the Western Jin dynasty.

Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Bātuójié sānmèijīng* (Bhadrapāla-samādhi Sūtra), one volume in seven fascicles; translated by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the Yuánkāng era of the Western Jìn dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfánglù*.

*Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Bhadrakalpa-sūtra*. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin.

Recorded in the *Changfang lu*. *Bhadrakalpa-sūtra*, one work in ten fascicles; also titled *Bhadrakalpa-samādhi-sūtra* and *Bhadrakalpa-dhyāna-sūtra*. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an in the fourth year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin. Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
The above five sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Sāgaranāgarājaparipṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle in four volumes (or three volumes), first translation; translated by Dharmarakṣa in the sixth year of the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The New Sūtra of the Dragon King of the Ocean*, one fascicle in four rolls, second translation, eighty-five pages. Translated by Dharmakṣema at Guzang in the seventh year of Xuanshi during the Northern Liang dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two sūtras above are different translations of the same original text.
*Dà zhōu kān dìng zhòng jīng mùlù*, Scroll Four.
The Great Zhou Catalogue of All Scriptures, Volume Five, compiled by order of the Empress of the Great Tang by the śramaṇa Mingquan and others at the Foshouji Monastery.
Volume Four: The Catalogue of Mahāyāna Scriptures Translated More Than Once. Volume Four: One Hundred and Sixty-eight Works in Three Hundred and Sixty-five Volumes.
The *Śūraṅgama-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; first appeared, translated by Zhi Loujiachan at Luoyang in the third year of the Zhongping era (186 CE) of Emperor Ling of the Later Han.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Śūraṅgama-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; second translation. Translated by Bo Yan at Baima Monastery in Luoyang during the Gānlù era of the Cao Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, third translation; translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śūraṅgama-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Yǒngfú dìngjīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Courageous Submission), in two scrolls; the fourth version listed above, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Yuánkāng era of the Jìn dynasty.
It shares the same title as the versions of the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi* produced by Zhīqiān, Zhīchèn, and Bóyán, though the wording differs slightly.

The *Śūraṅgama-samādhi Sūtra*, one volume in eight fascicles, the sixth edition; compiled to the right by Zhi Mindu during the Yongning era of the Western Jin dynasty, combining two versions by Zhi [Qian], two by Zhu [Fahu], and one by Bo [Yicheng] into a single work.
I consulted Zhi Mindu’s Catalogue.

The *Śūraṅgama-sūtra*, one volume in two fascicles, the fifth translation, consisting of thirty-six sheets. It was translated by Zhu Shulan in Luoyang during the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

*Śūraṃgama-samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle in three volumes; alternatively called the *Śūraṃgama Sūtra*, the seventh translation, consisting of fifty-eight sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.
One fascicle of the *Śūraṃgama-sūtra* in two scrolls; translated during the reign of Emperor Qi of the Wei dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.
The *Śūraṃgama-sūtra*, one volume in two fascicles, translated during the reign of Emperor Qi of the Later Wei;
recorded in the *Chángfáng-lù*.
The ten preceding sūtras are of the same original text but different translations.

The *Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Śūnyatāpraśānta*, one fascicle; also titled the *Sūtra on the Extinction of the Dharma* or the *Sūtra on the Disappearance of the Dharma*. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
The *Dharmakṣaya-sūtra*, one fascicle, first appearing in the *Chángfáng lù*;

a third appearance, also called the *Fǎmòjìn jīng* or the *Kōngjì púsà suowèn jīng*, which is identical to the version translated by Zhīqiān during the Wú period. The above was translated by Zhú Fǎhù of the Jìn dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Extinction of the Lesser Dharma*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Famojin jing* (Sūtra on the Extinction of the Dharma), one fascicle; the second appearance. Translated by Jñātāmitra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The preceding four sūtras are of the same original text with different translations.

The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra, one fascicle; also known as the Buddhadhātu Vaipulya Sūtra; twenty sheets. Translated in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty by Dharmakṣema and Dharmayaśas.
Extracted from the *Huàdù lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya-tathāgatagarbha-sūtra*, second extraction. Translated by Buddhabhadra at the capital of Yang and Mount Lu during the Yixi era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Dharmafang).
One fascicle of the *Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgata-rahasya-garbha Sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, twenty-four sheets; this is a different translation of the same text as the four preceding sūtras.

*Siddhārthaprabhāsa-samādhi Sūtra*, one fascicle (also known as the *Siddhārthaprabhāsa Sūtra* or the *Siddhārthaprabhāsa-samādhi Sūtra*), twenty-six sheets. Translated by Zhi Yao at Luoyang in the second year of the Guanghe era of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty.
*Chengju guangming sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Fulfillment of Radiance), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Chen of the Later Han;
recorded in the *Changfang lu* and the *Wu lu*, as well as the *Sanzang ji*.
*Chenyang zhufu gongde jing* (Sūtra of the Praise of the Merits of All Buddhas), one work in three fascicles, sixty-seven sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Dharma-rooms).

The *Chēngyáng zhūfó gōngdé jīng* (Sutra on Praising the Merits of All Buddhas), one fascicle, three rolls; also titled *Fóhuā jīng* (Buddha-flower Sutra), *Jíhuā jīng* (Collected Flower Sutra), *Jiànzài fó míng jīng* (Sutra of the Names of Buddhas Present), or *Zhūfó huā jīng* (Flower Sutra of All Buddhas). Third translation. Translated by the Northern Wei śramaṇa Jikaya at Beitaishan.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Chēngyáng zhūfó gōngdé jīng* (Sutra on Praising the Merits of All Buddhas), also titled the *Jíhuā jīng* (Sutra of Collected Flowers), in three volumes and sixty-seven sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the seventh year of the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Fómiàng jīng* (Sūtra of the Names of the Present Buddhas), one fascicle in three rolls; also titled the *Huāfū jīng* (Flower-Blossoming Sūtra). Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra at Jingzhou during the twenty-ninth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Baochang lu*:
The first six sūtras are the same original text translated separately.
*Aṅgulimālīya-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Aṅgulimāla-sūtra* or the *Aṅgulimālaka-sūtra*. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty under Emperor Wu.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Aṅgulimāla-āpatti-pratideśana-sūtra*. The aforementioned was stated by Dao’an to have been translated by Dharmarakṣa.
Recorded in the *Sēngyòu lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Aṅgulimāla’s Mother*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Sūtra on the Land of Immeasurable Bliss*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu.
*The Scripture on the Dharma Robe Offered by Śakra Devendra to Aṅgulimāla*, one fascicle. The above was translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa; so says Dao’an.
It appears in Sengyou’s Catalogue.

*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Subduing of Aṅgulimāla and the People’s Joy*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Aṅgulimāla’s Conversion*, one fascicle—also titled *The Sūtra on the Death of Aṅgulimāla’s Wife*. Both were translated by Dharmākara and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng Lù (Catalogue of Longfang).
*Aṅgulimālīya-sūtra*, one fascicle, four rolls, ninety-two sheets. Translated at Dàochǎng Sī Monastery by Guṇabhadra during the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first eight scriptures are translations of the same original text.
The *Sūrala-sūtra*, one fascicle, was the first to appear; it was translated by Bó Yán at Bǎimǎ Temple in Luòyáng during the early Wèi dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sūrala-sūtra*, the second translation; alternatively titled the *Sūrala-bodhisattva-sūtra*, twenty sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra of Prince Guṇaprabha*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra of the Questions of Sulā on Prince Guṇaprabha*, or *The Sūtra of the Questions of Rāṣṭrapāla on Prince Guṇaprabha*; nineteen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa in the sixth year of the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture of the Poor Son Susthitamati*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first four sutras were originally the same text translated separately.

The *Huiyin sanmei jing* (Sutra on the Samādhi of the Seal of Wisdom), one fascicle—also titled the *Huiyin jing*, or the *Shifang xianzai fo xi zai qianli ding jing*, or the *Baotian huiyin sanmei jing*—consists of twenty-three sheets. It was translated by Zhi Qian during the Jianxing to Huangwu years of the Wu dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
*Rúlái zhìyìn jīng* (Tathāgata-jñāna-mudrā-sūtra), one fascicle, nineteen sheets. The two sūtras above are the same text translated differently.

*Xūzhēn tiānzǐ jīng* (Sūtra of the Devaputra Susīma), one work in two fascicles, also titled *Xūzhēn tiānzǐ wèn sìshì jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Devaputra Susīma on Four Matters). Translated by Dharmarakṣa at Baima Monastery in the second year of the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xiūzhēn tiānzǐ jīng* is found in the *Wú lù*, which also states it was translated by Kumārajīva as a re-translation; however, this was actually translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liáng period.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
The first two scriptures are translations of the same original text.
*Yuedeng sanmei jing* (Moon Lamp Samādhi Sūtra), one fascicle; extracted from the *Dayuedeng sanmei jing*. Translated by An Shigao of the Han Dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yuedēng sānmèi jīng* (Moon-Lamp Samādhi Sūtra), one fascicle; also known as *Wénshūshīlì shíshì xíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Deeds of Mañjuśrī) or *Jiànhuì sānmèi jīng* (Samādhi of Established Wisdom). Ten sheets. Translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Xiāngōng.
Recorded in Changfang’s Catalogue.

*Candrapradīpa-samādhi-sūtra*, one volume in eleven (or ten) fascicles, totaling two hundred and two sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Yeśas together with Fazhi at Xiangzhou during the eighth year of the Tianbao era of the Northern Qi dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three scriptures are translations of the same original text.
*Dàoshù jīng zhùjiě* (Commentary on the Sūtra of the Tree of the Path), one fascicle, including preface; translated by Kang Senghui during the Zhengshi era of Emperor Qi of the Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Dàoshǔ sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Bodhi-tree Samādhi), one fascicle; also known as the *Sīhémò jīng* or the *Púsà dàoshǔ jīng*; eleven pages. Translated by Zhīqiān during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
From the *Baoshang lu*:
One fascicle of the *Daoshu sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Bodhi Tree) in two scrolls. The above appears in the catalogues of Shi Dao’an and Zhi Mindu;
these six preceding sūtras are translations of the same original text.
*Zhàomíng sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Illumination), one fascicle, seven pages. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Zhàomíng sānmèi jīng*, one fascicle, ten pages. Second translation. Translated by Qiduomi during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures are the same original text translated separately.

*Chāorìmíng sānmèijīng*, one fascicle in two volumes; also known as *Chāorìmíng jīng*, or in three volumes; the initial translation consists of fifty-five sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa in the seventh year of the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of two scrolls, the *Chāorìyuè jīng* (Sūtra of Surpassing the Sun and Moon), second translation; on the right, it was re-edited by Nie Chéngyuǎn of the Jin dynasty.
This is a different translation from the same original text as the *Chāorìmíng jīng* (Sūtra of the Radiance of Surpassing the Sun) produced by Dharmarakṣa.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
The first two scriptures are the same original text with different translations.
*Kǒngquèwáng záshénzhòu jīng* (The Scripture of the Miscellaneous Divine Incantations of the Peacock King), one fascicle; translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Bo Shìlìmíduō.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Peacock King Divine Incantation Sūtra* (in two fascicles or one fascicle). Translated by the Śramaṇa Śrīmitra during the Xiánkāng era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Peacock King Dhāraṇī Sūtra* (different from the previous translation by Jiaye); this is the second edition, translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin by Dharmaruci.

*The Great Golden-Colored Peacock King Sūtra*, one fascicle, together with the *Method for Delimiting the Ritual Boundary*, complete. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty at the Xiaoyao Garden in Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, thirty-seven pages. Translated by Saṃghavarman at the Zhanyun Hall and Zhi guan Monastery in the capital of Yangdu during the fifteenth year of the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first five scriptures share the same original but have different translations.
*Qǐng guānshìyīn jīng* (one fascicle), also titled *Qǐng guānshìyīn xiāofú dúhài tuólóní zhòu jīng*, recorded in the *Bǎochàng lù*. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin.
Translated at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an. Recorded in the Chángfáng Lù (Catalogue of Changfang).

*Qǐng Guānshìyīn Xiāofú Dúhài Jīng* (Sutra on Entreaty to Avalokiteśvara to Eliminate and Subdue Poisonous Harm), one fascicle; the second edition, fourteen sheets. Translated by Zhú Nántí during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Lù* (Catalogues) of the Inner and Outer Scriptures. The first two scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Dà jìng fǎmén jīng*, one fascicle; also titled *Shàngjīn guāngshǒu nǚ suowèn rúshǒu tóngzhēn suowèn kāihuà jīng* or *Jìng fǎmén jīng*; twenty-nine sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa in the first year of the Jiànxīng era of the Western Jìn dynasty.
From the *Chūnadi-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures):

One fascicle of two rolls of the *Mahāvyūha-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*, a separate translation of the same text as the *Mañjuśrī-prabhāva-sūtra*, the *Suvarṇavarṇābhā-kanyā-guṇa-sūtra*, and the *Mahāviśuddha-dharmaparyāya-sūtra*, totaling twenty-six pages. Dated the third year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas from Udyāna in Northern India at Daxingshan Temple;
recorded in the Neidian lu (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures).
The aforementioned two sūtras are different translations of the same original text:

*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Śyāma* (菩薩睒子經), one fascicle, five sheets; and *The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Śyāma* (佛說睒經), one fascicle, also titled *The Sūtra on the Origin of Śyāma* (睒本起經). Both were translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Śyāma-putra Sūtra* (also known as the *Sūtra on the Filial Son Śyāma*, the *Bodhisattva Śyāma Sūtra*, the *Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Śyāma*, the *Sūtra on the Hidden Filial Son*, and the *Root Sūtra of Śyāma*). Second translation; seven sheets. Translated by Dharmayaśas of the Western Qin.
Translated by Qifu Qiangui at Henan Commandery.
Recorded in the Changfang Catalogue.
*Śyāma-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty at the Xiaoyao Garden in Chang’an.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xiǎozǐ shǎnzǐ jīng* (Sūtra of the Filial Son Śyāma), also known by five other titles: *Xiǎoshǎn jīng*, *Púsà shǎn jīng*, *Fóshuō shǎn jīng*, *Shǎnběn jīng*, and *Xiǎozǐ dé jīng*—thus totaling six names. This second edition differs slightly from the translation by Kumārajīva. It was translated by Dharmabuddhin of the Western Qin dynasty in the state of Hénán.
From the Record of Changfang.
The first five scriptures are different translations of the same original text.
*The Scripture on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Yuankang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Guanshiyin shouji jing* (The Scripture on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sūtra on Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Receiving the Prediction*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra on Avalokiteśvara Receiving the Decision*. Translated from the *Baochang lu* (Record of Baochang), this is a re-translation. It was translated by Dharmakṣema in Yangzhou during the first year of the Yongchu era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three sutras are the same text with different translations:

*Púsà xiūxíng jīng* (One fascicle), also titled *Wēishī zhǎngzhě suowèn púsà jīng*, or alternatively *Zhǎngzhě xiūxíng jīng*. Seven sheets. Translated by Bóyán in Luoyang during the Gānlù era of the Former Wei.
*Pusa xiuxing jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Practice), one fascicle. The above was translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
It appears in the Changfang lu.

*The Scripture on the Practice of the Elder* (Chángzhě xiūxíng jīng), one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva Practice Asked by the Elder Vaiśya* (Wēishī chángzhě suowèn púsà xiūxíng jīng) or simply *The Scripture on Bodhisattva Practice*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bái Fǎzǔ of Hénèi during the Jìn dynasty, under Emperor Huìdì.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three scriptures are the same original text with different translations.

*Bodhisattvapūrvacaryā-sūtra*, one fascicle in three volumes, fifty-two pages; *Bodhisattvapūrvacaryā-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
From the Record of Changfang.
The first two scriptures are the same original translated separately.
*Bodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra*, one volume in three fascicles; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra* in three rolls; also known as the *Pūrṇaparipṛcchā-sūtra* or the *Mahākaruṇācitta-sūtra*, or [alternatively] in two rolls and seventy-three sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva in Cháng'ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahābodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra*, twenty scrolls, four hundred and ten sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at Hongfu Monastery in the Western Capital during the nineteenth year of the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty.

The *Jùshàngēn jīng* (Sūtra on the Accumulation of Roots of Goodness), one fascicle, appears in the lower volume of the *Púsà zàng* (Bodhisattva Piṭaka). Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
It appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.
The first four scriptures were translated separately from the same original text.
*Púsà xíng wǔshí yuánshēn jīng* (One fascicle), also called *Wǔshí yuánshēn jīng* or *Púsà yuánshēn wǔshí shì jīng* (Seven sheets); translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bōsà yuánshēn wǔshí shì jīng* (Sūtra on the Fifty Matters of the Bodhisattva’s Past Lives), which is largely identical with minor differences to the *Wǔshí yuánxíng jīng*; translated by Niè Dàozhēn during the Tàikāng era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures are the same original text with different translations.
*Zhūdé fútián jīng*, one fascicle; its initial appearance simply titled it *Fútián jīng*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Fǎlì of the Western Jin, during the reign of Emperor Huì.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fútián jīng* (Sūtra on Fields of Merit); also known as the *Zhūdé fútián jīng* (Sūtra on the Fields of Merit for All Virtuous Ones), or alternatively titled the *Fútián dì jīng* (Sūtra on the Grounds of the Field of Merit). Second, six pages long; translated by Zhu Faju of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Zhìchángfáng).

One fascicle, titled *Fútián jīng* (Sūtra on the Field of Merit), also known as the *Jūsì qǐngsēng fútián jīng* (Sūtra on the Householder Inviting Monks to the Field of Merit). Translated by Dharmakṣema during the reign of Emperor An of the Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three scriptures share the same original text but were produced separately.
*Taizi mupo jing* (one fascicle), translated by An Shigao of the Later Han;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù.
*Taizi mumo jing* (The Scripture on the Prince’s Dream-Omen), one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin; this is the second translation.
It appears in the *Changfang lu*.
Since the previous two scriptures are translations of the same original text, they are grouped together.
*The Scripture on Prince Andhaka*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty;
recorded in the *Catalogue of Dharma-uttara*.
*The Scripture on Prince Śūradatta*, one fascicle, five sheets. Dao’an states that it was translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
Recorded in Sengyou’s Catalogue (*Chu sanzang jiji*).
The first two scriptures share the same original text.
*The Great Aśoka-rāja Sūtra*, one volume in five fascicles. Translated by the Anxi śramaṇa An Faqin during the Guangxi era of the Western Jin dynasty, under Emperor Hui.
Translated in Luoyang.

*The Great Aśoka Sūtra*, one volume in ten fascicles (sometimes without the character "Da" [Great]). Right: During the eleventh year of the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty, the śramaṇa Saṃghavarman.
In the Shouguang Hall at the capital of Yangdu, the Emperor himself took up the pen to translate it.
This is recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
It is noted that the previous two sutras are alternative translations of the same original text.
The Mahāmāyā-sūtra, one work in two fascicles (or one fascicle). Translated by Zhi Yao in Luoyang during the Zhongping era of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*Mahāmāyā-sūtra*, one fascicle (or two fascicles), twenty-five sheets. Translated by Tánjǐng at Yángdū during the Southern Qí dynasty. It appears in the *Nèidiǎnlù*.
Since this and the previous two sūtras are different translations of the same original text, they are listed here together.

*Qīfó shénzhòu jīng* (The Scripture on the Divine Incantations of the Seven Buddhas), one fascicle; "Jielü" (Knotting Thread) is an alternative title, though some versions lack the word "jīng" (scripture). Translated during the Wu dynasty by Zhi Qian.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture on the Divine Incantations of the Seven Buddhas*, one fascicle in four volumes, seventy-one pages; this is a separate translation of the same original text as the two preceding scriptures.

*The Scripture on the Merit of Erecting Images*, one fascicle in two pages. *The Mahāyāna Scripture on the Merit of Creating Images*, one part in two fascicles, or alternatively one fascicle in twenty-two pages. The above was translated by Divākara at Dazhou Dongsi in the second year of the Tiānshòu era of the Great Zhou dynasty.
The aforementioned two sutras share the same original text.
*Dharmadhātuprakṛtyasambhedanirdeśa-sūtra*, one fascicle, two volumes, thirty-one pages. Translated by Saṃghamitrā at the capital of Yangdu during the Tianjian era.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle, two scrolls, thirty-six sheets; the aforementioned single copy was translated by Kumārajīva.
Recorded in the *Dámó yùduōluò lù*.
The two aforementioned sutras were originally the same text translated separately.
The *Adbhutadharmaparyāya-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes and forty-eight pages, was translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Dharmottara* record:

*The Scripture on Unprecedented Causes and Conditions*, one fascicle in two volumes, also titled *The Scripture on the Causes and Effects of the Unprecedented*, forty-eight pages. Translated by Tanying of the Southern Qi dynasty at Yangdu.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two sutras are the same original text translated separately.
*Sì bùkědé jīng* (The Sutra on the Four Unobtainables), one fascicle; translated by An Shigao, Prince of the Parthian Kingdom, during the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sì bùkědé jīng* (The Scripture on the Four Unobtainables), second edition, six sheets. Translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa;
identical to the version translated by An Shigao.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
The first two sutras are considered different translations of the same original text.
*The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Śūraṅgama* (also known as *The Sutra on Resolving All Dharmas as Being Like Illusions and Samādhi*), one fascicle, thirty-two pages; translated during the Han dynasty.

*The Scripture of the Peerless Pure Alms-Gathering of the Bodhisattva Sumati*, one volume in two fascicles; also titled *The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Definitive Realization that All Dharmas are Like Illusions*, thirty-two pages. Translated at Luoyang by the lay believer Yan Fotiao of Qingxin during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Rúshǒu púsà wúshàng qīngjìng fēnwéi jīng* (The Sutra of the Supreme Pure Alms-Gathering of Bodhisattva Lokeśvara-rāja), also known as the *Juélìo zhūfǎ rúhuàn sānmèi jīng* (The Sutra on the Samādhi of Resolving that All Dharmas are Like Illusions), consisting of thirty-three pages. Translated by Master Xiáng of the Song Dynasty in the Nanhai Commandery.
This is recorded in the *Chūnēidiǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). The first three scriptures share the same original text but were translated separately.
Excluding the one fascicle, fifteen sheets of the *Kǒngzāihuàn jīng*, which was translated by Bó Yán during the Wei dynasty.
*Chūkōngtsāihuàn jīng* (Sūtra on Eliminating Fear of Calamities and Afflictions), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Shengjian during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Western Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sutras were originally the same text translated separately.
The *Yìyì jīng* (Sūtra on Increasing Benefit), one fascicle in three volumes, is the second translation; it was translated by Kang Daohé at the end of the Taiyuan era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Zhudaozu lu:

*Yiyi jing* (Scripture on Increasing Intent), one fascicle, also titled *Siyi jing* (Scripture on Contemplating Intent). Translated by the lay devotee Yan Fotiao of Qingxin in Linhuai during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle, two scrolls, titled *Yìyì jīng* (Sūtra on Increasing the Intention), translated by the monk Fǎní;
recorded in Zhū Shíxíng’s *Hàn lù*.
The first three sūtras were originally the same text translated separately.
*Śirīmatī-brāhmaṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as *Brahmaṇī-śirīmatī-sūtra*, six pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Fannü Shòuyì jīng* (Sūtra of the Brahmin Girl Śrīmatī), one fascicle. Translated by the Sòng dynasty śramaṇa Shi Yǒng.
Appears in the Chángfáng lù.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Original Sūtra of Pai* (Pai ben jing), one fascicle in two volumes, the first translation; translated by the Han dynasty śramaṇa Zhi Chen.
*The Sūtra of Pai* (Pai jing), one fascicle in two volumes, the second edition; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Pai jing* (The Scripture of Pai), one fascicle.
Translated by the śramaṇa Shengjian of the Western Qin at Henan for Qifu Qiangui.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three scriptures share the same original text but were produced separately.
*Wúliàngyì jīng* (One Fascicle), translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Wúliàngyì jīng* (Sūtra of Immeasurable Meanings), twenty-one pages. Translated by Dharmagatayaśas at Cháo廷 Temple in Guangzhou during the Jiānyuán era of the Southern Qi dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures are translations of the same original text.
*Jìngdù sānmèi jīng*, one fascicle; translated by the monk Tanyao during the third year of the Héping era of the Later Wei dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Jìngdù sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Pure Deliverance). Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìyán in the fourth year of the Yuánjiā era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jingdu sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Pure Deliverance), one fascicle in two volumes. Translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Baoyun at Yangzhou;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jingdu sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Pure Deliverance), one fascicle in three volumes. Translated by Guṇabhadra of the Song dynasty.
This is recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first four scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

The subsequent *Āmítuó jì* (Verses on Amitābha), one fascicle, one sheet, and the *Āmítuófó jì* (Verses on Amitābha Buddha), one fascicle, are separate editions of the same original text as the preceding two scriptures.

The *Mahā-kṣudraka-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes; the *Guanfo jing* (Sūtra on Contemplating the Buddha), one volume. These are largely identical with minor differences from the *Kṣudraka-sūtra*. Both were translated by the Śramaṇa Shengjian of the Western Qin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Guānjīng* (Sutra on the Consecration), also titled *Sìyuèbārì guānjīng* (Consecration Sutra of the Eighth Day of the Fourth Month). Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì of the Western Jin dynasty during the reign of Emperor Huì.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first three scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.
*Fó běnxíng jīng*, one fascicle; Master Sēngyòu of the Liáng dynasty’s catalog states that this is a "classical scripture."
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fó běnxíng jīng* (The Scripture on the Original Deeds of the Buddha), one volume in five fascicles; the second edition, translated by Dharmakṣema of Liangzhou during the Juqú regime of Northern Liang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sutra of the Buddha’s Original Deeds* (Buddha-benxing-jing), one volume in seven fascicles, totaling one hundred fourteen pages. Translated by the monk Baoyun at Yangdu during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

The *Buddhacarita-saṃgraha-sūtra*, one volume consisting of sixty fascicles and eight hundred and sixty-two sheets. Translated by Jñānagupta at the capital during the seventh year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
The first four scriptures were translated from the same original source but separately.
*Dharmapada* (Faju jing), one volume in four fascicles; translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue (*Chángfáng lù*).

The *Dharmapada-sūtra*, one work in two fascicles; the initial translation is recorded in the *Wu lu* (Records of Wu) as being five fascicles. During the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty, only Śrīnanda translated it at Wuchang Commandery.
This appears in the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The *Dharmapada-sūtra*, one work in two fascicles; the second translation. [Recorded in] the *Bielu* and the *Sanbaolu*. Translated by the lay devotee (upāsaka) Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Fǎjù jīng* (Dharmapada-sūtra), one fascicle. Translated by Zhìqiān together with Qínán during the Wú dynasty;
recorded in Sēngyòu’s catalog.

*Dharmapada-avadāna-sūtra*, one work in four fascicles, or five or six fascicles. Also titled *Fǎjù běnmò jīng* (Dharmapada-mūla-prakaraṇa-sūtra) or *Fǎjù pìjīng* (Dharmapada-dṛṣṭānta-sūtra). Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjǔ and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jìn dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
