The first five scriptures are different translations of the same original text.
*Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana Wander through the Four Crossroads*, one fascicle. Translated by Kāṅ Mèngxiáng in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Xiàn of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle: *The Scripture on Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana Wandering through the Four Crossroads*, also titled *The Scripture on Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana Wandering through Various Kingdoms*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures are the same original translated separately.

One fascicle of the *Zìshì sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Self-Vow) contains an internal title stating "Chapter Four: Independent Realization," which appears within the *Bǐqiū jìngxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Pure Conduct of Bhikṣus). Its initial appearance is largely identical with slight variations to that produced by Hù. It was translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.

*The Scripture on the Samādhi of Solemn Self-Vow of Solitary Realization* (also known as *The Scripture on the Samādhi of the Tathāgata’s Solemn Self-Vow*), one fascicle; the second translation, recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù* as eight pages. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty; recorded in the *Nèidiǎn Lù*.
*The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Past Lives*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty, under Emperor Hui.
Included in the *Changfang Lu*.
*The Sutra on the Tathāgata’s Sole Realization of the Samādhi of Self-Vow*, one fascicle. Second edition. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jīvaka from the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
The first four scriptures are translations of the same original text.

One work in eight fascicles, totaling one hundred and forty-five sheets, titled the *Liùdù jí jīng* (Compendium of the Six Perfections), also known as the *Liùdù wújí jīng* (Sutra on the Infinite Six Perfections), the *Dù wújí jīng* (Sutra on the Infinite Deliverance), or the *Zá wújí jīng* (Miscellaneous Sutra on the Infinite). This was translated during the Wu dynasty by the monk Kang Sēnghuì at Wuchang.

Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). One fascicle of the *Chāmí Wángjīng* (Sūtra of King Chāmí), appearing in the eighth fascicle; translated by Kang Senghui of the Wu [Dynasty].
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Fanhuang jing* (Sūtra on the Brahmā King), one fascicle; also known as the *Fanhuangwang jing* (Sūtra on the Brahmā King). It appears in the eighth fascicle [of the *Zhongjing mulu*]. Translated by the śramaṇa Kang Senghui during the Zhengshi era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Ānanda-nimi Sūtra*, one fascicle; also called *Ānanda-āśaya Sūtra*. Translated by Kang Senghui during the Zhengshi era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Zhongxin zhengxing jing* (Sūtra on the Correct Practice of the Central Mind), one fascicle; also known as *Landa Wang Jing* or *Maudgalyāyana Puṇya Sūtra*. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*Ānanda-niyama-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Taken from the eighth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Taken from the *Changfang lu*.
*The Scripture on the King of the Deva-Heaven*, one fascicle; extracted from the fifth fascicle [of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*].
Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mílán jīng* (also titled *Mílián jīng*); translated by Zhu Tánwúlán at Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiào Wǔ of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
The *Módiào wáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Māndhātṛ), one fascicle, listed in the *Chángfáng lù*. Second edition. Translated by Zhú Fǎhù of the Western Jìn dynasty.
It is largely identical with, yet slightly different from, the version translated by Zhī Qián.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Qiányíwáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Qiányí). The aforementioned was translated by Zhú Fǎhù during the Jìn dynasty;
this is recorded in Sēngyòu’s catalog.
*The Bodhisattva’s Sutra on Being Free from a Ghost Wife*, one fascicle; appears in the eighth fascicle. Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.

*The Sutra of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta*, one fascicle; appears in the eighth fascicle. It was translated by Nie Daozhen in the first year of the Taikang era (280 CE) during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Tiāodá jiàorén wéiè jīng* (Sūtra on Tiāodá Teaching Others to Commit Evil), appearing in the sixth volume; translated by Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Jīngīn tàishān shúzuò jīng* (Sutra on Offering Gold to Mount Tai to Expiate Sins), also known as the *Mílán jīng* or the *Mílián jīng*. Translated by the Śramaṇas Fǎjǔ and Fǎlì of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the King of Sparrows Spoken by the Buddha*, one fascicle. Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin dynasty;
recorded in the fifth fascicle of the aforementioned catalog.
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Becoming a King of Pigeons*, one fascicle. Extracted from the sixth fascicle; translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of King Samantaprabha*, one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang, during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.

*The Scripture on Sacrificing One’s Life to Rescue a Merchant*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Chángfáng lù*. The above [scripture] is from the fifth fascicle; it was translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Shi Huìjiǎn.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Shìjiā bìzuì jīng* (Sūtra on the Expiation of Sins by Śramaṇas), found in the fifth fascicle of the *Chūshēng jīng* (Sūtra on the Emergence). Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Candanagāthā-sūtra*, also titled the *Candanamūlanta-sūtra*, appears in the eighth fascicle; translated by the Sòng dynasty śramaṇa Śākya Yonggong.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Kōngjìng tiān gǎnyìng sānmèi jīng* (The Sutra on the Samādhi of the Response and Manifestation of the Heaven of Emptiness and Purity), one fascicle; also titled *Kōngjìng sānmèi jīng*. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Kōngjìng sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Emptiness and Purity), also known as the *Kōngjìng dàgǎnyìng jīng* (Sūtra of the Great Miraculous Response of Emptiness and Purity). Translated by the Sòng dynasty śramaṇa Shi Yǒnggōng.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Lánběn jīng* (Blue-Text Sūtra) is extracted from the third fascicle; one fascicle of the *Zhēluó guówáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Cera) is extracted from the eighth fascicle;

one fascicle of the *Jièdù wújí jīng* (Sūtra on the Perfection of Precepts) and one fascicle of the *Sàhétán jīng* (Sūtra of Sahetana) are extracted from the second fascicle of the *Rěndù wújí* (Perfection of Patience).

*Ji-jing* (Sutra on the Ultimate), one fascicle; *Chan-du wu-ji jing* (Sutra on the Perfection of Dhyāna), one fascicle; *Xiao-er wen fa ji jie jing* (Sutra on the Child Who Understands the Dharma Upon Hearing It), one fascicle—these appear in fascicle six.
*Pan-da longwang jing* (Sutra of the Dragon King Pan-da), one fascicle—appears in fascicle five. *Bo-ye wang jing* (Sutra of King Bo-ye), one fascicle—appears in fascicle two.
*Shi-he-bian wang jing* (Sutra of King Shihebian), one fascicle—appears in fascicle eight. *Pusa wei yu* (The Bodhisattva as a Fish).
*The Sūtra of the King*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Prince’s Dharma-Giving*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Buddha Laughing for Three Reasons*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of Kṣāntivādin*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Perfection of Giving*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Honeybee King*, appearing in the first fascicle, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Rishi’s Praise*, appearing in the sixth fascicle, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Past Deeds of the Bodhisattva as a Tortoise*, one fascicle.
The thirty-nine scriptures on the right of this volume are extracted from the *Ṣaṭpāramitā-samuccaya-sūtra* (*Liudu ji jing*).

According to the fifth volume of the *Dazhou kanding zhongjing mulu*, the *Mañjuśrī-kumārabhūta-bodhisattva-sūtra* in one fascicle is appended here; it is recorded as being extracted from the eighth volume in the *Bie lu*.
Translated by Nie Daozhen during the first year of the Taishi era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the Changfang lu.

*Zhongben qijing* (Sutra on the Middle Account of the Origin), two fascicles; *Diaotuo jiaoren wei’e jing* (Sutra on Devadatta Teaching Others to Do Evil), one fascicle; both appear in the sixth fascicle. The above are from the *Zalu* (Miscellaneous Records).
Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Chángfáng’s Catalogue).

*Xingqixing jīng* (Sūtra on the Arising of Practice), two fascicles; *Jīngīn tàishān shúzuò jīng* (Sūtra on Offering Gold to Mount Tai to Expiate Sins), one fascicle—also titled *Mílán jīng* or *Mílián jīng*; the latter is also known as the *Shíyuán* (Ten Conditions).
*Wu lu* (Records of Wu).
The imperial era and the translators are the same as above.
*Catuḥsatya-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Buddhabhāṣita-śakuntarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle. These appear in the fifth fascicle. The above works are found in the *Wu lu*.
Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Xiūxíng běnqǐ jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Arising of Practice) in two fascicles and the *Púsà shēnwéi gèiwáng jīng* (Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Body as a Pigeon King) in one fascicle appear in the fifth fascicle. The aforementioned one sūtra in two fascicles was translated by various translators, as previously noted.
The *Hu-ben-jing* in four fascicles and the *Pu-ming-jing* in one fascicle; these two appear in the *Wu-lu*.
They were translated by Juqu Jingsheng of Northern Liang during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
[Recorded in] the *Changfang-lu*.

*The Sutra on Transformations During the Thousand Years After the Parinirvāṇa*, four fascicles; *The Sutra on Saving Oneself and Rescuing Merchants*, one fascicle. These two appear in the fifth fascicle of the *Chū-sō-moku-roku* (Separate Record).
*The Combined Sutra on the Divine Footsteps of the Way*, two fascicles, translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Shi Huijian.
Recorded in Changfang’s Catalogue; the former title is *The Scripture on Ultimate Transformations*.

*The Scripture on Śākyamuni’s Exhaustion of Karmic Offenses*, one fascicle. Recorded in the fifth fascicle. *The Names of All Buddhas in the Various Scriptures*, two fascicles; the former title is *The Scripture on the Names of Buddhas*.
The imperial-era translators are the same as before.

*Jiù pìyù jīng* (Old Avadāna Sūtra), two fascicles; *Chénì jīng* (Sūtra of Chanda), one fascicle—also titled *Chénì běnmò jīng* (Sūtra on the Origins of Chanda)—appears in the eighth fascicle [of the *Dà zàng jīng*]. The latter is also known as the *Pìyù jīng*.
Translated by the Song Dynasty śramaṇa Shi Yong;
recorded in the Changfang lu.

*The Sūtra on Contemplating Immeasurable Life*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Response and Manifestation of the Emptiness-Purity Heaven*, also called the *Sūtra on the Samādhi of Emptiness-Purity*. The above is from the *Collection of Single Sūtras*; translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
From the *Chángfáng lù*:

*Lóngzhǒng zūn guó biànhuà jīng* (Sūtra on the Transformation of the Honored Land of Dragon Seed), two fascicles; *Kōngjìng sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Emptiness and Purity), one fascicle—also titled *Kōngjìng dà gǎnyìng jīng* (Sūtra of the Great Miraculous Response of Emptiness and Purity). The above are from the *Bié lù* (Separate Record).
*The Buddha Seeing the Cowherd Showing the Way Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Song dynasty śramaṇa Shi Yonggong.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Names of Three Thousand Buddhas*, one fascicle; recorded in the third fascicle of the *Zhālǎ Guówáng Jīng*. *The Sūtra of King Zhālǎ*, one fascicle.

Extracted from Volume Eight: *The Sutra of the Names of Fifty-three Buddhas*, one scroll; *The Sutra on the Perfection of Precepts*, one scroll; *The Sāvadha-sūtra*, one scroll. Extracted from Volume Two:
*The Sutra of the Names of Buddhas in the Southern Quarter*, one scroll; *The Perfection of Dhyāna*, one scroll;

*The Sutra on Children Understanding the Dharma Upon Hearing It*, one scroll. Extracted from Volume Six: *The Sutra of the One Buddha of City-Governing Temple*, one scroll; *The Perfection of Forbearance*.

*Wujijing* (Sutra on the Ultimate), one fascicle; *Panda Longwangjing* (Sutra of the Dragon King Pandara), one fascicle; from the fifth fascicle: *Miezuodefujing* (Sutra on the Extinction of Sin and Attainment of Merit);

*Guanshiyin Suoshuo Xingfajing* (Sutra on the Methods of Practice Spoken by Avalokiteśvara); *Boyewangjing* (Sutra of King Pāyāsa), one fascicle; from the second fascicle: *Mile Wei Nushenjing* (Sutra of Maitreya Taking Female Form);
*Shihabianwangjing* (Sutra of King Śikhaṇḍin), one fascicle; from the eighth fascicle: *Jitiaoyisuo...* (The [Sutra] Spoken by the One of Tranquil and Harmonious Mind).
*The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva as the Fish King*, one fascicle; *The Illustrated Record of the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita Seeking the Profound Prajñā*;
*The Sūtra on the Birthplace of the Bodhisattva*; *The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Constantly Practicing the Path Six Times Day and Night from the First Arising of the Resolve*;
*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions for Gathering All Streams*; *The Sūtra on the Prince’s Dharma-Giving*, one fascicle; *The Buddha [Teaching] by Means of Three Matters*.

*Xiāojīng* (Sūtra on Laughter), one fascicle; *Chàntíhéjīng* (Sūtra of Kṣāntivādin), one fascicle; *Bǔshìdùwújīng* (Sūtra on the Perfection of Dāna), one fascicle; *Mìfēngwángjīng* (Sūtra of the Honeybee King), one fascicle;
*Xiāntànjīng* (Sūtra of the Rishi’s Lament), one fascicle; *Púsàzuòguīběnshījīng* (Sūtra on the Past Deed of the Bodhisattva as a Tortoise), one fascicle.
The above thirty-nine sūtras are extracted from the *Liùdùjíjīng* (Saṃyukta-Ṣaṭpāramitā-sūtra).
Now, based on the manuscript from India (Zhudong), twenty-one additional sūtras have been inserted;
they are not included within the original list.
This was collated by the Dharma Master Zhutang.
The Fifth Volume of the *Catalogue of All Scriptures Compiled and Verified by Emperor Wu*;
the Sixth Volume of the *Catalogue of All Scriptures Compiled and Verified by Emperor Wu*.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Mingquan and others at the Foshouji Monastery by Imperial Decree of the Great Tang Empress.
The catalog of Mahāyāna Vinaya and Mahāyāna Śāstras, combined into one fascicle, consists of one hundred and fifty-two works totaling seven hundred and sixteen fascicles.
As for the Bodhisattva Precepts, "bodhisattva" (pú-sà) means "to awaken" (jǐng).
Restrain! Restrain body and mind to give rise to the great resolve;
riding upon the great vow, proceed toward the great fruit.
Extensively delivering sentient beings and proclaiming the great stations of learning,
I have excerpted and recorded them herein.

Mahāyāna Vinaya texts: fifty-four works. *Buddhapiṭaka-sūtra*, one work in four fascicles (or three), also titled *Viveka-dharma-sūtra*. Translated by Kumārajīva in the seventh year of the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty.
It appears in the *Dharmottara-lu* and the *Chángfáng-lu*.
The *Bucáng Dàfǎngjīng* (Buddha-treasury Mahāvaipulya Sūtra), one fascicle, also titled *Wènmíngxiǎn jīng* (Sūtra of the Manifestation of Inquiry), was translated by the Song dynasty monk Shi Dàoyán.
*Fó huìguò jīng* (Sūtra on the Buddha’s Repentance), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Mañjuśrī-paścāttāpa-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled the *Mañjuśrī-pañcāṅga-paścāttāpa-sūtra*, twenty-four sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Jin Dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Wénshūshīlì jìnglǜ jīng* (Mañjuśrī-vimala-śīla-sūtra), one fascicle; also known as the *Jìnglǜ jīng*, fifteen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa at Baima Monastery during the Western Jin dynasty.
It appears in the *Dharmottara-lu* and the *Chángfáng-lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mañjuśrī-viśuddha-śīla-sūtra*; the second edition differs slightly from that translated by Dharmarakṣa. It was translated by Nie Daozhen during the Yuankang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Wenshushili huiguo jing* (The Sutra of Mañjuśrī’s Repentance), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one volume in twenty fascicles. According to the records of Sengchang and Zhudaozu, it was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇavarman from Kaśmīra—whose name means "Armor of Merit" in the Song language.
It arrived at Jianye during the Yuanjia era.
It was the second time it was produced at Qihuan Temple;
its translation differs slightly from that of Zhi Chen’s eight-fascicle version.
According to the *Zhudaozu lu* and the *Biographies of Eminent Monks*,
later disciples at Dinglin Temple further produced two additional sections,
completing the work in thirty fascicles.

The *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra* (Pusa shanjie jing), one fascicle, ten scrolls, totaling one hundred and sixty-four sheets. According to the records of Baochang and Sengyou, it was [translated] by the monk Huiyi of Qiyuan Temple.
On the twenty-first day of the second month in the eighth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty,
the Kapiśa śramaṇa Guṇavarman was invited to the monastery to perform the translation,
with Huìyì acting as the scribe.
With two fascicles remaining, he moved to the Xia-zi (Summer Retreat) at Dinglin Temple and commissioned his younger brother,
Saṃghavarman, to complete the work. Before the transcription was finished,
he lost the *Sūtra on the Sequence of Practice* (*Xiuxing pin*).
Later, when Guṇavarman entered nirvāṇa, [the text] was transcribed in eight fascicles;
it was titled the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra* and also the *Bodhisattva-bhūmi-sūtra*.
At that time, Dharmakṣema of Jetavana Monastery composed the "Postscript to the Sūtra," which states:
Shi Faming of the same monastery initially collaborated with Huiyi in the commentary; however,
because he received the version translated by Ming, the detailed and finalized text was subsequently abridged.
He further consulted the original manuscript and again made his own editorial adjustments,
producing another eight fascicles titled the *Dichí* (Bhūmisaṃgraha).
The addition of one verse at the beginning resembles the Sāṃkhya school.
Mahāyāna died. Suspecting this, the Vinaya Master searched for and recovered the "Introductory Chapter" (Nidāna-varga) and the "Chapter on Precepts" (Śīla-varga).
The latter portion was copied out to form ten fascicles;
based on the text of the Entrustment,
it is titled the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*.
Before it could be arranged in order, there were doubts regarding its loss.
In the tenth year of the Tianjian era, by imperial decree, Baochang was commissioned to compose a preface and to compile and determine the sequence of the various chapters.
This was extracted from Zhu Daozu’s *Miscellaneous Records of the Jin Dynasty*.
One hundred and thirteen sheets.
One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra* in eight rolls, also known as the *Bodhisattvabhūmi-sūtra*. Translated by Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang dynasty at Guzang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Bodhisattvabhūmiviniścaya-sūtra*, in eight or four fascicles.
According to the *Sēngyòu lù*, Dharmakṣema brought the Sanskrit original from India.
He arrived at Xiliangzhou and translated [the text] for Juqu Mengxun, the Great King of Hexi.
This was recorded in Zhu Daozu’s *Hexi lu* (Record of Hexi).
Since it is unclear which of the two accounts is correct,
both records are preserved.
Sengyou states that this is the same scripture as the one previously translated by Guṇabhadra, issued here for a second time.
It is largely the same with minor differences.
*The Bodhisattva’s Good Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated at the monastery by Guṇavarman in the eighth year of the Yuanjia era.
Recorded in the Baochang lu.
The *Jingtai Shilu* and the *Fulin Si Lu* both state that this was missing from their editions;
it was later obtained.
One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva-antarashī-sūtra*, twenty sheets. Translated by Guṇavarman during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
The *Bodhisattva-śīla-saṃgraha-sūtra* (Pusa jie yaoyi jing), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Yuankang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Ritual Text for the Sole Reception of the Bodhisattva Precepts*, one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Bodhisattva Fast Sūtra*, one fascicle, also titled *The Ritual for the Bodhisattva Fast of Worthy Head*; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Pusa shouzhai jing* (Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Receiving the Fasting Precepts), one fascicle. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Bodhisattva’s Method for Repentance*, one fascicle; a different recension of the same text translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.

Recorded in the *Changfang lu*. *Bodhisattva Huiguo Fa Jing* (The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Method for Repenting Transgressions), one fascicle; sometimes the character "jing" (sūtra) is omitted. A note below states it is from the *Ten Stages Treatise* (*Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra*) by Nāgārjuna. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin period.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Púsà zhāifǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Method for the Bodhisattva’s Fasting), one fascicle; also titled *Zhèngzhāi jīng* (Sūtra on the Correct Fasting) or *Chízhāi jīng* (Sūtra on Maintaining the Fast); eight sheets. Translated by Zhú Fáhù during the Jin dynasty.
*Pusa zhengzhai jing* (Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Correct Fasting), one fascicle. Translated by Jñātāmitra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Guzang during the reign of Juqu Mengxun of the Northern Liang.
*Chuyi Shansi lu* (Record from the Shanshi Temple).
One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva Precepts Upāsaka Ordination Altar Text*. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Huisong during the Northern Liang period.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle; a second version from a different manuscript. Translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Dharmakṣema, Huìsōng, and others.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*Bodhisattva-pratimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle. Brought by Dharmakṣema and translated at Gāochāng.
*Pusa zang jing* (Bodhisattvapitaka-sūtra), one fascicle. Translated by Saṃghavarman during the sixteenth year of the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
Recorded in the *Baoshang lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Fivefold Dharma of Bodhisattva Repentance*, one fascicle, two sheets. The record from Folin Monastery states:
"Later, I obtained this sūtra and vinaya.
*The Bodhisattva Karma*, one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at Cuimeng Palace during the twenty-third year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra*. Translated by Xuanzang at Cuifei Palace during the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Śāriputra-parivarta-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śāriputra-parivarta-sūtra*, one fascicle, also titled *Huìguò jīng* (Sūtra on Repenting of Faults), six sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Śāriputra-parivarta-sūtra* (The Sutra on Śāriputra’s Repentance), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty.
Appears in the *Dharmoktara-lu*.
The Text on the Precepts for Upāsakas and Upāsikās Free from Desire. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmaruci at Xie Zhenshi Temple during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the Changfang Catalogue.

The *Upāsaka-śīla Sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively ten, seven, six, or five fascicles; totaling one hundred and fifty-four pages. Translated by Dharmakṣema at the Xiányù Palace in Liangzhou during the first year of the Chéngxuán era of the Northern Liáng dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Líyù ōubāsē yōubāiyì jùxíng èrshí'èr jiè jīng* (Sūtra on the Twenty-two Precepts for the Full Practice of Laymen and Laywomen Free from Desire), also known as the *Sānguī ōubāsē jiè* (Precepts for the Three Refuges of Laymen) or the *Shànxìn èrshí'èr jiè* (Twenty-two Precepts of the Good Faith). Translated by Guṇavarman during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù.
*Upāsaka-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle. The above scripture is extracted from the *Upāsaka-śīla-sūtra*.
Recorded in the Zhēnjì sì lù.
*Fanwang jing* (Brahmajāla Sūtra), one work in two fascicles, or three fascicles; translated by the foreign śramaṇa Kang Mengxiang during the reign of Emperor Xian of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Fanwang jing*, one work in two fascicles, thirty-nine pages; translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
*The Scripture on the Definitive Vinaya*, one fascicle, twenty-two pages. Translated in Liangzhou during the Northern Liang dynasty at Dunhuang; the names of the translators are not recorded.

The *Sūtra of the Names of the Thirty-five Buddhas* in one fascicle is excerpted from the *Dharmottara Record*. The aforementioned *Sūtra on the Decisive Vinaya* states that Dao’an says it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
Appearing in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*:

*The Bodhisattva’s Method for Almsgiving and Repentance*, one fascicle; excerpted from the *Vinayaviniścaya-sūtra*. Translated by Nie Daozhen during the Taikang era of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Fayue sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Dharma and Vinaya), one fascicle, eight sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
Appears in the *Dafanglu* and the *Damoyuduo lu*.
*Fǎlǜ sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Dharma and Discipline), one fascicle; also known as the *Fǎlǜ jīng*. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Sengcháng).
*Jìng yèzhàng jīng* (Sūtra on Purifying Karmic Obstructions), one fascicle, eighteen sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty.
The *Qingjing pinifangguang jing* (Sūtra on the Vast and Extensive Vinaya of Purification), one fascicle, twenty sheets; translated by Kumārajīva of the Qin dynasty.
It appears in the *Dharmottara-lu*.
*Daśadig-vistara-tri-śīla-sūtra*, one fascicle, three volumes, fifty-four pages; translated by Dharmakṣema during the Northern Liang dynasty.
Included in the *Dharmôttarīya-lu*.
The Ratnarāśi Sūtra, one fascicle in two volumes, forty-four pages; translated by Dao Gong during the Northern Liang dynasty.
It appears in the Da Mo Yu tuo luo lu (Dharmottara’s Catalogue) and also in the Chang fang lu (Zhi Changfang’s Catalogue).
The *Kāśyapa-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, forty-five pages. Translated by Dharmapūrṇa at Ye-du (Yecheng) in the second month of the second year of the Xinghe era of the Northern Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Questions of Śāntasvarā*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture on the Pure Subjugation Spoken by the Tathāgata*, twenty-one pages. Translated during the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Fǎhǎi.
Extracted from the *Dharmottara-lu* and the *Chángfáng-lù*.
*Mahāyāna-triskandha-pratideśana-sūtra*, one fascicle, thirteen sheets. Translated at Xingshan Monastery during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty by Jñānagupta and Dharmagupta.

Record from the Fulin Monastery Catalogue: *The Bodhisattva Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Householder Bodhisattva Precepts*, one fascicle; *The Householder Vinaya*, one fascicle; Mahāyāna Treatises: one hundred and eight works totaling six hundred and sixty-one fascicles. *The Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, one work in one hundred fascicles (alternatively one hundred ten fascicles or seventy fascicles), comprising two thousand three hundred and ninety-eight sheets; composed by the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna. Translated in the Hongshi era of the Qin dynasty by Kumārajīva in Chang’an.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Yúqié shīdì lùn* (Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra), consisting of one hundred scrolls and one thousand eight hundred and forty-eight pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng at Dàcí'ēn Monastery during the twentieth year of the Zhèngguān era of the Great Táng.
*Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra-vyākhyā*, one fascicle, composed by Bodhisattva Jinabhadra; translated by the Great Tang Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

The *Xianyang shengjiao lun* (Treatise on the Manifestation of the Holy Teachings), one volume in twenty fascicles, totaling three hundred and twenty-six sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at Hongfu Monastery during the nineteenth year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Xianyang shengjiao lun song* (Verses of the Treatise on Manifesting the Holy Teachings). Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

The Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā, one volume in sixteen fascicles, totaling two hundred and fifty-five pages; translated at Hongfu Monastery by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang during the nineteenth year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures:

*Abhidharmasamuccaya* (Compendium of Abhidharma), one work in seven fascicles, totaling one hundred and eight pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang during the Xianqing era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

*Prajñāpradīpa-śāstra*, one volume, either fifteen or thirteen fascicles, totaling two hundred and forty-three pages. Translated by Prajñāruci at Śrīkumāra Monastery during the third year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.

Extracted from the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Mahāvyūha-śāstra*, one volume in fifteen fascicles (or ten fascicles), totaling two hundred thirty-three pages; composed by Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa; translated during the Later Qin dynasty by Kumārajīva.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Mahāyānasūtrālaṃkāra-śāstra*, consisting of thirteen or fifteen rolls and two hundred sheets. Translated by Paramārtha at Shèngguāng Monastery during the fourth year of the Zhèngguān era of the Great Táng dynasty.

Extracted from the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures): *Daśabhūmivibhāṣā-śāstra*, one work in fifteen fascicles (or fourteen fascicles), totaling three hundred and ninety sheets; composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna; translated in Chang'an by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

One work in twelve fascicles, the *Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, first translated. [Note: This was subsequently translated by Ratnamati within the palace halls of Luoyang during the fifth year of the Zhengshi era of Emperor Wu of the Later Wei.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra* in twelve scrolls and two hundred eighty-four sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Bodhiruci at Luoyang during the Yongming era of Emperor Xuánwǔ of the Later Wèi dynasty.
The Emperor received it by dictation.
It appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Śāstra on the Mahāyānasaṃparigraha* in fifteen (or twelve) rolls, totaling three hundred and thirty sheets. Translated at Zhìzhǐ Temple in Guangzhou by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha in the fourth year of the Tiānjiā era of the Chen dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, twelve scrolls, totaling three hundred and forty-five sheets: the *She dàchéng shìlùn* (Commentary on the Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-śāstra), translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty at Guangzhou.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):

*Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-śāstra*, one fascicle, ten scrolls, one hundred and twenty-five sheets. Translated by Dharmagupta at the Shōrin-en Garden in the Eastern Capital during the fifth year of the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.

Extracted from the *Lidai Sanbao Ji* (Record of the Three Jewels Through the Ages). The *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya* in one volume and ten fascicles, composed by Vasubandhu, totaling one hundred and eighty sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang at the Northern Gate and the Great Ci'en Monastery.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):

*Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, one volume in ten fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Asvabhāva; two hundred and twenty sheets. Translated by Xuanzang at the Great Ci’en Monastery during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, comprising two scrolls and forty-four pages. [Compiled] by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhāśanta of North India during the first year of the Putai era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Translated at Baima Monastery in Luoyang and Jinhua Monastery in Ye-du.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Mahāyānasaṃparigraha-śāstra* (The Treatise on the Compendium of the Mahāyāna), one volume in three fascicles, fifty-eight pages. Translated by the Ceylonese (*Cīna*) monk Paramārtha at Wangyuan in Guangzhou during the Chen dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
*Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, one volume in three fascicles, sixty-one sheets. Translated by Xuanzang at Yuhua Palace during the twenty-second year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Chu neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Śatasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, twenty scrolls, four hundred sheets. Translated by Paramārtha (波羅頗蜜多羅) in the second year of the Taicheng era of the Liang dynasty.
From the *Dharmodgata-lu*:
one fascicle of the *Bodhisattvabhūmi-śīla-sūtra* (or eight fascicles), totaling two hundred and fifty sheets. Translated by the Northern Liang śramaṇa Dharmakṣema at Guzang.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Śata-śāstra*, ten scrolls, two hundred and two pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at Ci'en Monastery during the Xianqing era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Śata-śāstra-kārikā*, totaling sixteen sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the Cuiwei Palace during the imperial entourage in the twenty-first year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures):
*Śata-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Deva; forty-two sheets. Translated in Chang’an by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fódì jīnglùn* (Treatise on the Buddhabhūmi Sūtra), comprising seven rolls and one hundred and nineteen sheets; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng during the Yǒnghuī era of the Great Táng.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):

*Bodhipathapradīpa-śāstra* (Treatise on the Provisions for Enlightenment), one fascicle, six rolls, one hundred and sixty-seven pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmagupta at the Shanglin Garden in the Eastern Capital during the fifth year of the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):

One work in ten fascicles, or alternatively six or five fascicles, totaling one hundred and forty-five sheets, titled the *Mile pusa wen jing lun* (Sūtra and Treatise on the Questions of Maitreya Bodhisattva). Translated in Luoyang by Buddhabhadra (Bodhiruci) during the Later Wei dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra*, four scrolls, ninety-nine sheets; translated by Bodhiruci of the Later Wei dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Treatise on the Scripture of the Questions of Brahmā Viśeṣacinti* (勝思惟梵天所問經論), one work in four fascicles—or three fascicles—totaling sixty sheets. Translated in Luoyang by Bodhiruci in the first year of the Putai era of the Later Wei dynasty.
*Fóxìng lùn* (Treatise on Buddha-nature), one fascicle, four scrolls, eighty-two pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the Chen Dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Madhyamaka-śāstra*, one fascicle in four volumes, totaling one hundred and three pages; alternatively, eight volumes. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at Chang’an.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Ratnagotravibhāga-mahāyānottaratantra-śāstra*, one fascicle in five volumes, or four, or three, totaling ninety-eight pages. Also titled *Ratnagotra-vibhāga-mahāyāna-uttara-śāstra*. Translated by Ratnamati of the Later Wei.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ratnagotravibhāga-śāstra*, one fascicle in four or five rolls; translated by Bodhiruci of the Later Wei dynasty at Luoyang and Ye.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Prajñāpāramitā-ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā-śāstra*, one work in four fascicles. Translated by Ratnamati at the palace in Luoyang during the Later Wei dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Mahāyāna-mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-nirarthaka-vāda*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
*Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhicitta-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle, two volumes; also titled *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra-śāstra*, thirty-four pages. Translated by Bodhiruci of the Later Wei dynasty at Luoyang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle in two scrolls, *Dàzhàngfū lùn* (Treatise on the Great Man), composed by Bodhisattva Deva; forty sheets. Translated during the Northern Liáng dynasty by Dào Tái.
Recorded in the *Nèidiǎn lù*.
*Madhyāntavibhāga-śāstra*, one fascicle in two volumes, thirty-eight pages; translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya*, one fascicle in three volumes; translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog).
One fascicle of the *Madhyāntavibhāga-kārikā*. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu*.
*Madhyamaka-śāstra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Paramārtha during the Chengsheng era of the Liang dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Catalogue.
*Buddha-abhidharma-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles, forty-four sheets. Translated by the Śramaṇa Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūn-ien-lu*.
*Anupūrvasamādhi-śāstra* (順中論), one work in two fascicles; translated at Luoyang by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Ch’ang-fang-lu*.

*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, one fascicle in two volumes, twenty-eight pages. Translated by Jñānagupta at the Shōrin-en Garden in the Eastern Capital during the ninth year of the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Tri-svabhāva-nirdeśa-śāstra*, one fascicle, two scrolls, forty-four pages, or one scroll; translated by the Śramaṇa Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, one scroll; translated by Paramārtha at Wangyuan Temple in Zhizhi, Guangzhou, during the Chen dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra*, consisting of three rolls and fifty-five sheets. [Compiled] by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci during the second year of the Yongping era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Translated at the residence of Duke Wenxuan of Tai Shang;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù.

*The Treatise on Destroying Attachment to Grasping and Not Destroying Conventional Designations* (*Vajracchedikā-prajñāpāramitā-sūtra-grahaṇābhiniveśa-bhaṅga-prajñapti-anupaccheda-śāstra*), one fascicle, two rolls, thirty-nine sheets. On the fifteenth day of the ninth month of the second year of the Yongchun era of the Great Tang, by the Tripiṭaka Master Divākara.
Translated at the Guining Monastery of Xitaiyuan Temple in the Western Capital;
newly included in the catalog.
*Tattvasaṃgraha-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles, thirty-two sheets. Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang during the twenty-first year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Translated while accompanying the Emperor at Cuimigong;
recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

One fascicle, seventeen pages: *The Treatise on the Correct Principle of the King’s Law* (Wangfa zhengli lun). Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang during the twenty-first year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Translated while accompanying the Emperor at Cuīguōng Palace.
Recorded in the *Chūnèidiǎnlù*.
*Chéngyèlùn* (Treatise on the Establishment of Karma), one fascicle, seventeen sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng during the twenty-second year of the Zhēnguān era of the Great Táng.
*Yechengjiu lun* (Treatise on the Accomplishment of Karma), one fascicle, seventeen sheets. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).

*Cheng weishi lun* (Treatise on the Establishment of Consciousness-Only), one volume in ten fascicles, composed by Dharmapāla and other Bodhisattvas; translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Weishi lun* (Treatise on Consciousness-Only), one volume, nineteen sheets, concerning "Consciousness-Only Without External Objects"; translated by Gautama Prajñāruci of the Later Wei.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, titled *Xiū dào bù gòng tā* (The Path of Cultivation Not Shared with Others), which differs slightly from the version translated by Dharmaruci of the Northern Wei, consisting of eleven pages; translated during the Chen dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha.

Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Vimśatikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle; composed by the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu; nine sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Recorded in Jingmai’s *Jīngtú* (Illustrated Catalogue of Scriptures).
*Triṃśikā-vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Appears in Jingmai’s *Jingtu*.
*Tattvārtha-śāstra*, one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
From the *Jingmai Jingtu* (Catalogue of Scriptures by Jingmai):
*The Treatise on the Conditioned Object of Perception*, one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
From the *Jingmai Jingtu*.
*Sanju-zuron*, one fascicle, twenty sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci at Luoyang and Ye during the fifth year of the Zhengshi era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fahua jing lun* (Treatise on the Lotus Sūtra), one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Ratnamati (also known as Bodhi) from Central India at Luoyang in the fifth year of the Zhengshi era.
Initially, it was produced with the assistance of Bodhiruci;
later, they were translated separately. This is recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Repository).
The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra-śāstra*, one volume in two fascicles, twenty-nine sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci at Ye (Yecheng) during the Later Wei dynasty.
This is recorded in Jingmai’s *Jingtu*.

*Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*, one fascicle; *Hetuvidyānyāyamukha-śāstra*, one fascicle, composed by Bodhisattva Dignāga, twelve sheets. The above were translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang during the twenty-first year of the Zhenguan era of the Great Tang.
Translated while accompanying the Emperor at Cuīguōng Palace;
recorded in the *Chūnèidiǎnlù*.

*Yīnmíng rùzhènglǐmén lùn* (The Entrance Gate for Reasoning into Correct Principles), one fascicle, composed by Śaṅkarasvāmin; six sheets. Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng during the twenty-first year of the Zhēnguān era of the Great Táng.
Translated while accompanying the Emperor at Cuīguōng Palace. Recorded in the Chūnèidiǎnlù (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures).
*Mahāyānapañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, one fascicle, eight sheets. Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng during the twenty-first year of the Zhēnguān era of the Great Táng dynasty.
Translated while accompanying the Emperor at Cuimigong;
recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*Bai fa mingmen lun* (Treatise on the Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas), one fascicle, two pages. Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang in the twenty-first year of the Zhenguan era of the Tang dynasty.
*Chū kō saishui kyū* (Record of Works Brought from the Interior and Exterior Canons), translated at Saishui Palace.
*Jūnimon ron* (Twelve Gate Treatise), one fascicle, composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna; twenty-eight sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Shíbā kōng lùn* (Treatise on the Eighteen Emptinesses), comprising nineteen sheets; translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in Jingmai’s *Jīngtú* (Illustrations of the Scriptures).
*Mahāyānāvatāra-śāstra*, one fascicle in two volumes, composed by Bodhisattva Sthiramati; forty-seven pages. Translated during the Northern Liang dynasty by Dao Tai.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*Ratnagotravibhāga-mahāyānottaratantra-śāstra* (also known as *Ratnagotravibhāga-rāja-samyak-śāstra*), one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Zhou dynasty by the Tripitaka Master Paramārtha from Ujjayinī in Western India.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Fāngbiàn xīn lùn* (Treatise on the Mind of Expedient Means), consisting of seventeen sheets; translated during the Yánxīng era of the Later Wèi dynasty by Jíjiāyè and Tányào.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Treatise on Generating the Bodhicitta*, one fascicle in two volumes, thirty-two pages; composed by the Bodhisattva Vasubandhu. Translated in Chang’an by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.

*The Treatise on the Mind of Expedient Means*, one volume; [composed] during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master and Dhyāna Master Buddhabhadra from the country of North India.
The Jin-language version by Buddhabhadra was translated at Yangdu and Mount Lu; it is recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Yathābhūta-śāstra* (Ru shí lùn), one fascicle, twenty-two pages: translated by the Chen-dynasty śramaṇa Paramārtha.
Recorded in the *Chūn-ten-roku* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Pratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle, ten sheets.
Translated by Jñānagupta at the Shanglin Garden on the banks of the Luo River in the Eastern Capital during the tenth year of the Daye era of the Sui dynasty.
*Pratītyasamutpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle, nine pages. Translated by Bodhiruci of the Later Wei.
Appears in the *Neidian lu*.
*Śatākṣara-śāstra*, one fascicle, nine sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci of the Later Wei;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ekottaraka-śāstra*, one fascicle, also titled *Yīshūjiālùn*. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci of the Later Wei.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Niyatārthadharmaparyāya-śāstra* (Deciding Store Treatise) in two volumes, and one fascicle of the *Vigrahavyāvartanī* (Treatise on Turning Back Disputes) in twenty-five sheets; both were translated by Gautama Prajñāruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda-śāstra* (Dàchéng qǐxìn lùn), translated during the Liáng dynasty by Paramārtha;
recorded in the *Nèidiǎn lù*.
*Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-mūla-astitva-adhunābhāva-vāda*, one fascicle, six pages; translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle, eleven pages; translated by Dharmaruci.
*Zhuanfalun jing lun* (Treatise on the Sūtra of Turning the Wheel of Dharma), one fascicle, ten sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Included in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
*The Treatise on the Sūtra of the Four Dharmas of the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin*, one fascicle, twelve sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty;
recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*The Commentary on the Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*, one fascicle, eight sheets. Composed by Upatiṣya. Translated by Bodhiruci in the first year of the Putai era of the Later Wei dynasty.
*Chu neidian lu* (Record of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

*Zhuan shi lun* (Treatise on the Transformation of Consciousness), one fascicle; *Jie quan lun* (Treatise on Unfolding the Fist), one fascicle. Both were translated during the Chen dynasty by Paramārtha.
Included in the *Neidian lu*.

The Mahāyāna Extensive Treatise on the Five Aggregates, one fascicle, eighteen pages. On the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month in the first year of the Chuihong era of the Great Tang, the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra from Central India [translated this].
Translated at the Guining Monastery of Xitaiyuan Temple in the Western Capital (Chang’an).

*The Treatise on the Ten Stages* (*Daśabhūmika-vibhāṣā-śāstra*), one volume in ten fascicles, composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna; translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Shíqī dì lùn* (Seventeen Stages Treatise) in five rolls; translated by Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the fourth year of the Tàiqīng era of Emperor Wŭ of the Liáng dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Tri-sahasra-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, one fascicle. Translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Nirvāṇa-subhadra-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles (two sheets). *Śāstra on Refuting the Four Schools of Non-Buddhists*, one fascicle (two sheets). Both were translated by Bodhiruci during the Northern Wei dynasty.
*Pò wàidào nièpán lùn* (Treatise on Refuting the Nirvana of Non-Buddhists), one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Bodhiruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Pratipakṣa-śāstra* (Treatise on Counter-Arguments), one fascicle. Translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty;
listed in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Nigraha-sthāna-śāstra* (Treatise on Points of Defeat), one fascicle. *Lakṣaṇa-anusāriṇī-śāstra* (Treatise Following Characteristics), one fascicle. Both were translated by Paramārtha at Zhìzhǐ Wángyuán Temple during the Chen dynasty.
*Chengjiu san sheng lun* (Treatise on the Accomplishment of the Three Vehicles), one fascicle. Translated during the Chen dynasty by Paramārtha.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Yukti-prayoga-śāstra* (Treatise on the Exposition of Reasoning), one fascicle. Translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Citta-karman-śāstra* (Treatise on Mental Action), one fascicle. Translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang:
*The Treatise on Great Emptiness*, one volume in three fascicles; translated by Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang.

*Mahāyānopadeśa-śāstra*, one fascicle in five rolls; excerpted from various treatises, recorded in the catalog of Zhenji Temple. *Mahāyāna-Dharmadhātu-Abhedya-śāstra*, one roll, seven sheets. Dated the fourteenth day of the tenth month in the second year of the Tiānshòu era of the Great Zhou.
The Tripiṭaka Master Ti-yun Prajñā of Khotan translated [these works] at Dongsisi during the Great Zhou dynasty.

The *Pañcavidyā-śāstra* consists of five parts in one volume: 1. *Śabda-vidyā* (Grammar), 2. *Cikitsā-vidyā* (Medical Science), 3. *Śilpa-karma-sthāna-vidyā* (Arts and Crafts), 4. *Hetu-vidyā* (Logic and Sorcery), and 5. *Adhyātma-vidyā* (Inner Science/Seals and Symbols). [This was originally] from the era of Emperor Ming of the Liang dynasty, when the Tripiṭaka Master and Vinaya Master Saṃghabhadra of the country of Pāṭaliputra, together with Jñānayaśas, [translated them].
Translated at Bāgā Monastery in the Old City of Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Dà zhōu kān dìng zhòng jīng mù lù*, Volume Six.
The Seventh Volume of the Great Zhou Catalogue of Compiled Scriptures, compiled by order of the Empress of the Great Tang by the śramaṇa Mingquan and others at Foshouji Monastery.
List of Single-Translation Sūtras of the Hīnayāna: three hundred twenty-eight works in four hundred twenty-four fascicles.
*The Sūtra of the Buddha’s Previous Births*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Zhu Falan during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Dhyāna Sūtra*, one work in two fascicles. Translated by An Shigao during the reign of Emperor Huan of the Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Suffering Created by Oneself or Another*, spoken by the Buddha for Acelakāśyapa. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ānāpāna-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Wǔmén chányào yòngfǎ jīng*, one fascicle. First appearance: translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Fumoku piyu jing* (Sutra of the Parable of the Floating Wood), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Mahāyāna-Pratipatti-pāramitā-saṃgraha-pāpa-vipāka-parivarta Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Āṣṭamahāpuruṣa-vibhāga Sūtra*, one fascicle (two sheets). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Chū hōshōroku*. *Kaigōhōkyō*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chōbōroku*.
*Wǔfǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Dharmas), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Wǔxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Practices), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Sandu jing* (Sūtra on the Three Poisons), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Zhù yīn chí rù jīng* (Sūtra on Abiding in the Aggregates, Bases, and Entrances), one fascicle or two fascicles; also titled *Yīn chí rù jīng*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Zhengzhai jing* (Sūtra on the Righteous Fast), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Foshuo chuchu jing* (Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Various Places), one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
*Qingli youzui jing* (Sūtra on the Transgression of Emotional Attachment), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Chujia yuan jing* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions for Leaving Home), one fascicle, two sheets; also called *Chujia yinyuan jing* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions for Leaving Home). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty; listed in the *Changfang lu*.

*Ahan zhengxing jing* (Sutra on the Right Practice of the Āgama), one fascicle, four sheets; also titled *Foshuo zhengyi jing* (Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Right Intention). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Shíbā nílí jīng* (Sūtra on the Eighteen Nirayas), five sheets; also called the *Shíbā dìyù jīng* (Sūtra on the Eighteen Hells). Translated by An Shìgāo during the Later Han dynasty.
*Fashouchen jing* (Sutra on the Dharma Receiving Dust), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Found in the *Neidian lu* and the *Changfang lu*.
*Chánxíngfǎxiǎng jīng* (Sūtra on the Dharma-Contemplation of Zen Practice), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Neidian lu* and the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fóshuō sāndúshì jīng* (Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Matters of the Three Poisons), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Fenming zui fu jing* (One Scroll). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Yin chi ru jing* (Sūtra on the Bases of the Aggregates), one fascicle in two rolls, thirty-two pages; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Dà ān bān shǒu yì jīng* (Sūtra on the Great Ānāpāna-smṛti), one fascicle in either two or one roll, forty-five pages; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han period.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Ānāpāna Sūtra*, either in two fascicles or one fascicle, consisting of twenty sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Nèidiǎn lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Layman Nandika*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the Chángfáng Record.
*The Sūtra on Contemplation*, one fascicle, also known as the *Sūtra on the Essentials of Contemplation*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Abhidharma-duḥkha-prajñā-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Vibhāṣā-pañca-dharma-caryā-sūtra*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Chandeng fangbian cidi fa jing* (Sūtra on the Sequential Methods of the Expedient Means of Dhyāna), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Shuxi shijing* (Sūtra on the Practice of Counting the Breath), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Cana fajing* (Sūtra on the Methods of Dhyāna), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle (or two fascicles) of the *Jiānyì jīng* (Sūtra on Firm Resolve), also known as the *Jiānxīn zhèngyì jīng* (Sūtra on Firm Mind and Right Resolve) or the *Jiānxīn jīng* (Sūtra on Firm Mind). Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, four sheets: the *Jiǎochángzhězǐ àoǎo sānchù jīng* (Sūtra on the Elder’s Son’s Distress in Three Places), also titled the *Jiǎochángzhě àoǎo jīng* (Sūtra on the Elder’s Distress), or simply the *Sānchù nǎo jīng* (Sūtra on Distress in Three Places). Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
*Gāndhāraka-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Chanding jing* (Sutra on Dhyāna), one fascicle. Translated by Lokakṣema during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Ajātaśatru-rāja-paripṛcchā-pañcānantarya-sūtra* (Sutra on King Ajātaśatru’s Inquiry into the Five Heinous Crimes), one fascicle; also known as the *Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra*. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhi Chen during the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chihuadu si lu*.

One fascicle of the *Duan shier yinyuan jing* (Sutra on the Severing of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination), also titled *Ahan koujie shier yinyuan jing* (Oral Explanation of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination from the Āgama), also titled *Ahan koujie jing* (Oral Explanation of the Āgama), and also titled *Anhou koujie jing* (Oral Explanation by Lord An). Translated during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty by An Xuan at the capital.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, titled *Shǒuzhì wèn fó shí sì shì jīng* (The Scripture on Shouzhi Asking the Buddha Fourteen Questions). Translated by Zhi Yao in Luoyang during the Zhongping era of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Fallen Upāsaka*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Zhi Yao of the Later Han at Luoyang.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Minor Stages of the Path*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Yao at Luoyang during the era of Emperor Ling of the Later Han.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bàofú jīng* (Sūtra on Rebirth in the Blissful Land), also called the *Fúbào jīng*. Translated in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Xiàn of the Later Han by the foreign śramaṇa Kāṅ Mèngxiáng.
*Qīlòu jīng* (Sūtra on the Seven Leaks), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of Wu during the era of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Kālāma-brāhmaṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu state during the era of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng-lù*.

The *Xiūxíng fāngbiàn jīng* (Sūtra on the Expedient Means of Practice), one work in two fascicles, also titled the *Xiūxíng fāngbiàn chán jīng* (Sūtra on the Expedient Means of the Practice of Dhyāna); translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu state.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Huìguò fǎ jīng* (Sutra on the Method for Repenting Transgressions); also known as the *Xù shífāng lǐbài huìguò wén* (Text on the Narrative of Paying Homage and Repenting Before the Ten Directions). Alternatively, it omits the word "sūtra" (*jīng*) and is simply titled *Huìguò fǎ*. Translated by Zhīqián of the Wu dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Virtue of the Worthy One*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of Wu.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Dragon King Nāga* (Nán lóngwáng jīng), one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra on the Dragon Nāga*. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng Lù.
*The Sūtra on the Brahmacārin’s Observance of Purity* (Fànzhì jié jìng jīng), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
*Jingshui jiejing* (Sutra on the Precepts of the Ganges Water), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Weiriruzhannan jing* (The Sutra on the Miscellaneous Difficulties of the Sun), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Bofei heda kuangye gui shuofa jing* (The Sutra of the Buddha Preaching the Dharma to the Heda Ghost of the Vast Wilderness), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sūmatī-gṛhapati-sūtra*, nine sheets; translated by Zhīqián during the Wu period.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ānanda-catur-vastuka-sūtra*, one fascicle, three pages; translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Buddha-bhaiṣajya-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Zhu Luyouyan together with Zhi Qian at Yangdu during the Wu dynasty.
*Ajiti-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Parable of King Udayana’s Lion Milk*, one fascicle (one version lacks the characters "parable"). Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra Spoken by the Heretic Śreṇika on Deliverance*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
*Weishengyuanwang jing* (Sūtra on King Ajātaśatru), one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Sanpin Dizi Jing* (Sutra on the Three Grades of Disciples), one fascicle, three sheets; also titled *Dizi Xue You Sanbei Jing* (Sutra on the Disciple’s Learning in Three Ranks) or *Wu You Jing* (Sutra Without [the Character] "You"). Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Lu.
*The Sūtra of the Four Vows*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
It appears in the *Neidian lu* and the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on Converting the Brahmin*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.
*The Sūtra on Detachment from Desire Spoken by the Buddha for the Heretic Susīma*, one fascicle. Translated during the Wu dynasty by Zhi Qian. Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The above [entry] appears in the Chángfáng Lù.*
*The Scripture on Māra’s Trial of Maudgalyāyana*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Abhidharma*. Translated by Zhi Qian of Wu during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Later Wei.

Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*. *The Scripture of King Laṇḍa*, one fascicle. Also titled *The Scripture on the Causes, Conditions, and Merits of Maudgalyāyana*, and also titled *The Scripture on the Merits of Maudgalyāyana*. Seen in the *Wǔ Lù*. Translated by Zhi Qian of Wu during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Later Wei.
*The Sutra of One Hundred Parables*, one fascicle.
Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu state during the era of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Zuochan jing* (Sutra on Sitting Meditation), one fascicle. Translated by Kang Senghui during the Zhengshi era of the Wu state under the Wei dynasty’s Emperor Qi.
Appears in the Changfang lu.

*Bodhisattva erbai wushi fa jing* (Sutra of the Two Hundred and Fifty Dharmas of the Bodhisattva), one fascicle. Translated by Kang Senghui during the Zhengshi era of the Wu state under the Wei dynasty’s Emperor Qi.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Zhū shénzhòu jīng* (Scripture of Various Divine Spells) in three rolls; translated by Dharmarakṣa in Luoyang during the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Precious Treasury* (Ratnagarbha-sūtra), one volume in two fascicles; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin during the sixth year of the Taishi era.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Scripture on Future Transformations*, one volume; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fó wèi púsà wǔ mèng jīng* (Sūtra of the Five Dreams of the Buddha as a Bodhisattva), one fascicle; second translation. Also titled *Fó wǔ mèng jīng*, *Tàizǐ wǔ mèng jīng*, or *Xiānrén wǔ mèng jīng*. Translated by Zhú Fáhù in the second year of the Tà'ān era of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have consulted the *Jiùlù* (Old Catalogue) and the *Dàozhēnlù* (Record of Daozhen).

There is one fascicle of the *Mó Mùqiéluán běnjīng* (Sūtra on the Original Life of Mahāmaudgalyāyana), one version of which lacks the characters "hé" (呵) and "jiàn" (揵). This was translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Wǔgài yíjié shīxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Hindrances, Doubtful Ties, and Loss of Practice). Translated by Zhú Fáhù in the second year of the Yǒngmíng era of the Western Jìn dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Wǔfúshī jīng* (Sūtra on the Bestowal of the Five Blessings), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Sānpǐnhuìguò jīng* (Sūtra on Repenting of Faults in Three Chapters), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Guānxíng bù yí sìshì jīng* (Sūtra on the Four Matters of Unwavering Contemplative Practice), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The Sūtra of the Parable of the Four Wives, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Chángfáng’s Catalogue).
The Sūtra of King Aḍāka, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Danruo jing* (The Scripture of Danruo), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Longshi jing* (Sūtra on the Gift of the Dragon), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jigudumingde jing* (Sūtra on the Virtuous Merit of Anāthapiṇḍada), also titled *Jigudu shi jing* (Sūtra of Anāthapiṇḍada). Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Exhortation of King Daṭa by the Dragon Kings, Brothers*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Quanhua wang jing* (Sūtra on Exhorting and Transforming Kings), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jie wuchang jing* (Sūtra on Explaining Impermanence), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Yanwang wubai yan ju jing* (The Scripture of the Goose King and Five Hundred Geese), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra of the Parable of the City*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of Awakening the Mind*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Jianglong jing* (Sutra on Subduing Dragons), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Xié fǎ jīng* (Sūtra on Deviant Dharmas), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fàn zuì jīng* (Sūtra on Committing Offenses), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Response to Suffering*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Sanpin Xiuxing Jing* (Sutra on the Three Grades of Practice), one fascicle; also known as *Sanpin Huiguo Jing* (Sutra on the Repentance of the Three Grades). Dao’an states that it was compiled by a person of recent times from the *Daji Xing Jing* (Sutra on the Practice of the Great Collection). Translated during the Western Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle: *The Explanation of Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes. Translated by the śramaṇa An Faqin during the Taikang era of the Jin dynasty under Emperor Hui.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Naraka-sūtra*, one volume. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One scroll of the *Bāotāi jīng* (also titled *Bāotāi shòushēn jīng*), totaling seventeen sheets; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Tà'ān era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).
*Siziqin jing* (Sūtra on the Four Self-Inflicted Injuries), one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*The Scripture on Five Hundred Disciples Speaking of Their Own Past Causes*, one fascicle. The *Catalogue of Transformation and Salvation* states: "The *Scripture on Five Hundred Disciples Speaking of Their Own Origins*, twenty-four sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taikang era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù*.
*Jiàkè jīng* (The Sutra of the Merchant), one fascicle in two volumes; translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Catuṣpariṣatsūtra*, one fascicle, three pages; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Dharmodgata-lu*.
*Śrāmaṇyaphala-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture of the Horse-King*, one fascicle (right). Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Catuṣpariṣat-sūtra* (Sūtra of the Four Assemblies), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Daridrastrī-rājñī-bhāryā-sūtra* (Sūtra of the Poor Woman Who Became the King’s Consort), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin.
*Faguang jing* (Sūtra of Dharma-observation), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jingji sanpin feng jing* (Sutra on the Three Grades of Wind Affecting the Body), one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*Suoyu zhihuan jing* (Sutra on the Sufferings Brought About by Desires), one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Dàjiāshè běnjīng* (Sūtra of the Original Deeds of Mahākāśyapa), five sheets; the *Bǎochàng lù* omits the character "dà" (great). Translated by Zhú Fáhù of the Western Jin.
Extracted from the *Nèidiǎn lù*.

*The Scripture on Future Transformations*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Scripture on Future Transformations and Extinction*, two sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty;
alternatively attributed to An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Qingjing faxing jing* (Sutra on the Practice of Pure Dharma), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*. Recorded in the *Dharmodgata lu*.
*Past Buddhas’ Almsround Sūtra*, one fascicle, two pages; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin, as recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Suilanben jing*, one fascicle, three pages; translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
*Chixin fanzhi jing* (Sūtra of the Brahmacārin Holding the Mind), one fascicle. Translated by Bai Fazǔ during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Shishi jing* (Sūtra on Time and Non-time), one fascicle, three sheets; also titled *Shijing* (Sūtra on Time). Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng lù (Chángfáng Catalogue).

*Ajātaśatru-rāja-paripṛcchā-pañcānantarya-sūtra* (Sūtra on King Ajātaśatru’s Inquiry into the Five Heinous Offenses), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin period.
*Manfajing* (Sūtra on Arrogance toward the Dharma), one fascicle. Translated by Faju and Fali during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-mahoraga-upamā-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled the *Mahoraga-sūtra*. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Simile of Devadatta*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng Catalogue.

*The Sūtra of the Arhat Kātyāyanīputra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Kātyāyanīputra Sūtra*. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Arhat Meeting King Bimbisāra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on King Ajātaśatru Asking about the Origin of Hatred*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Kālodāyin during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of Vaidehī’s Son Asking His Mother on a Moonlit Night*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Sūtra of the Simile of Holding Soil with a Nail*, one fascicle. Also titled *Sūtra of Taking Soil with a Nail* or *Sūtra of Soil from a Nail-tip*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Śāili jīng* (Sūtra on Decline and Benefit), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Faju piyujing* (Sūtra of Parables from the Dharmapada), one work in six fascicles. Translated by Faju and Falì during the Western Jin dynasty;
included in Sengyou’s *Lù*.

*Lóuyún rěnrú jīng* (Sūtra on Rāhula’s Forbearance), one fascicle, three sheets. Also titled *Rěnrú jīng* (Sūtra on Forbearance). Translated by Faju and Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the True Matter Spoken by the Buddha for Young Bhikṣus*, one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì.
*Mahābhikṣu-sūtra*, one fascicle.
Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Zhòngshēng Wèirán Sānjiè Jīng* (Sūtra on the Three Realms of Sentient Beings Yet to Come), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Fǎfáng Lù*.
*Qiúyù Shuōfǎ Jīng* (Sūtra on Seeking and Desiring to Preach the Dharma), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra Explained by Nandika*, one fascicle, five sheets. Translated during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śāgha Bhikṣu Guṇa Sūtra*, one fascicle, three pages. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Bēnfēn Shàn’è Suǒqǐ Jīng* (Sūtra on the Distinction of the Origins of Good and Evil), one fascicle; also known as the *Shíshàn Shí’è Jīng* (Sūtra of the Ten Wholesome and Ten Unwholesome Deeds). Translated by the śramaṇa Zhì Fǎdù during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Zìshòu jīng* (Sutra on Self-Reception), one fascicle, five sheets; also titled *Zìshòu bùzìshòu jīng* (Sutra on Self-Reception and Non-Self-Reception). Translated by Dharmaruci at the capital of Yang during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
