*Jiuhu shenming ji renbing kuye jing* (Sūtra on Saving and Protecting Life and Delivering People from the Suffering and Calamities of Illness), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Wǔkǔ zhāngjù jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Suffering Chapters), one fascicle; also known as *Wǔkǔ jīng*, or alternatively titled *Jìngchú zuìgài yuèlè fófǎ jīng*, or simply *Wǔgǒu zhāngjù jīng*. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One scroll titled *The Mahākāśyapa Attends the Buddha at the Time of His Parinirvāṇa*, also known as the *Mahākāśyapa Sūtra*. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*Jiejing yijuan* (One Scroll of the Scripture of Admonitions). Translated by Dharmarakṣa in the first year of the Taishi era of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Zhòngshēng shēnhuì jīng* (Sūtra on the Impurity of Sentient Beings’ Bodies), one fascicle. Translated by Faju and Fali during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
*Dàyù shì jīng* (Sūtra on the Matter of the Great Fish), two sheets. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

See *Zhèngjīng* (Correct Scripture), one fascicle, nine sheets. Also known as the *Shēngsǐ biànní jīng* (Scripture on the Transformation of Consciousness at Birth and Death). Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Ānàn qī mèng jīng* (The Scripture of Ānanda’s Seven Dreams), one fascicle, two sheets; also titled *Ānàn bā mèng jīng* (The Scripture of Ānanda’s Eight Dreams), though some versions omit the character "eight" (bā). Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Āhēdiāo Ānàhán jīng* (Sūtra on the Arhat Āhēdiāo), one fascicle, two sheets; also titled *Hédiāo Ānàhán jīng* or *Ātiáo Ānàhán jīng*. Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*Zhì chánfǎ jīng* (Sutra on the Methods of Dhyāna), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fàntiān cèshù jīng* (Sūtra on Brahmā’s Calculation), one fascicle; also titled *Zhūtiān shì jīng* (Sūtra on the Affairs of the Various Heavens). Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Sengchángfáng).
*Zhutiandi jing* (Sūtra on the Various Heavens and Earths), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Ticheng nili jing* (Sūtra of the Iron City Hell), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.

*The Sūtra on the Five Dharmas by Which a Bhikṣu Enters Hell*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty. (Recorded in the *Changfang lu*).
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dharmatrāta-dhyāna-sūtra* (two volumes), also known as the *Aśubha-bhāvanā-sūtra* or the *Mārgabhūmi-sūtra*, consisting of five sheets. Translated by Buddhabhadra during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
One fascicle of the *Saṃgharakṣa-saṃyukta-sūtra* in three volumes; translated by Saṃghabhūti in the twentieth year of the Jiànyuán era of the Former Qín dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Chamajing* (The Sūtra on Kṣema), one fascicle. Translated by the Kapiśa śramaṇa Dharmayaśas during the Later Qin dynasty. Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Chàn fǎ yào* (Essentials of Dhyāna Methods), one work in three fascicles. Previously translated, it was re-collated in the ninth year of Hongshi; the preface was composed by Sengrui. Translated by Kumārajīva in the fourth year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle, two scrolls, of the *Ajātaśatru-sūtra* (阿闍世經), translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jian zhui zui fu jing* (Sūtra on Examining All Sins and Merits), one fascicle, ten scrolls. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
*The Scripture on the Transformation of the Body of the Māra King*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Scripture on the Dharma Canon of Wishes and Practices for Rebirth in the Land of Buddha Śāntamati in the Past*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Buddha’s Former Life as a Deer King*, one fascicle; also known simply as *The Sūtra of the Deer King*. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
This entry is found in the *Sengyou lu*.

*The Sūtra on the Manifestation of the Thousand-Spoked Wheel Mark at the Buddha’s Footprint*, one fascicle; excerpted from the fourth fascicle of the *Saṃyukta Āgama*. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Candana Tree*, one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin;
appears in the *Dharmoktara Record*.
*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Lamp-Finger*, one fascicle, ten sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

*The Sutra of Brief Instructions Spoken by the Buddha on the Eve of His Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle, six pages; also titled *The Sutra of the Bequeathed Teaching*. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin in Changan.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sīwú yàoliè fǎjīng* (or without the word "sūtra"). Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Chāng'ān during the Hóngshǐ era of the Later Qín dynasty.

*Yinggong fahang jing* (Sūtra on the Dharma Practice for Receiving Offerings), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Biqiu ying fahang jing* (Sūtra on the Bhikṣu’s Dharma Practice for Receiving Offerings). Translated by Kumārajīva during the Later Qin period.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Fùrén yùgū jīng* (Sutra on a Woman Encountering Calamity), one fascicle; also titled *Fùyù duì jīng* (Sutra on a Woman Encountering Retribution), two sheets. Translated by Fa-jian of the Western Qin dynasty; recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*Shànxìn nǚ jīng* (Sutra of the Virtuous Faithful Woman), one volume in two fascicles; also titled *Xìnshàn jīng* (Sutra of Faithful Goodness). Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema of the Northern Liang period.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Parinirvāṇa of King Śuddhodana*, one fascicle, seven pages. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang, during the Northern Liang dynasty.
Recorded in the *Nèidiǎn lù*.

*The Scripture on the Questions of the Elder’s Son Bianyi*, one fascicle, ten sheets; also titled *The Scripture on the Questions of the Elder’s Intent*. Translated by Dharmakṣema of the Later Wei dynasty.
It appears in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog).

The *Saṃyukta-ratna-piṭaka-sūtra*, one volume in eight fascicles, or ten fascicles, or thirteen fascicles, totaling one hundred and sixty-six pages. Translated at the Northern Terrace during the Yanxing era of the Later Wei dynasty by Ji Jiaye together with Tanyao.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Viyasapṛcchā-sūtra*, in two rolls and thirty-one pages; translated by Ratnamati during the Later Wei dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Vimalā-upāsikā-paripṛcchā-sūtra*, one fascicle, four pages. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci in the fourth year of the Xinghe era of the Eastern Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Cat of Precious Intent*, one fascicle. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci at Jinhua Temple in the capital of Ye during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Śubhavyūha-upāsaka-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhiyan of Liangzhou at Jiyuan Monastery in Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Catuḥmahārāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhiyan and Baoyun during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu (Catalogue of Dharma Treasures).
*Anāgāmi-sūtra*, one work in two fascicles. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhiyan of Liangzhou together with Baoyun at Zhuanlun Temple in Yangdu during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūn-ken-roku* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
*Fofazang jing* (Sutra on the Treasury of the Dharma Transmission), one volume in six fascicles. Translated during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Baoyun of Liangzhou.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng-lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
*Shanxin ershisi jie* (The Twenty-four Precepts for Good Faith), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇavarman during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Shi liu-shier jian jing* (The Scripture on the Sixty-two Views), one work in four fascicles; according to the separate catalog, the text states it is one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
*The Sutra Requested by the Bhikṣu Paṇḍita*, one fascicle. The above was translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
It appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture on the Twelve Dhūtas*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Dhūtas of Śramaṇas*. Both were translated during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the Western Region śramaṇa Guṇabhadra.
They appear in the Chángfáng Record.
*Thirteen Dhūta Sūtras*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng Record.
*Mahākāśyapa’s Conversion of the Poor Mother*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
*Shengsi jing* (Sūtra on Birth and Death), one fascicle in twelve chapters. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.

*Jiutituojia jing* (Sūtra of Jyotiṣka), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty;

*Xìngfǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Four Kinds of Training in the Dharma), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
*The Scripture on Āniruddha’s Seven Recollections*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.

*Shibofa santonglue* (A Brief Compendium of the Ten Retributive Dharmas), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Naxian biqiu jing* (The Sūtra of the Bhikṣu Nāgasena), one work in two fascicles, or one fascicle comprising thirty-six sheets. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Wǔkǔ zhāngjù jīng* (Sūtra of the Verses on the Five Sufferings). Translated by Jūqú Jīngshēng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Wǔ wúfǎnfù jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Without Repentance), one fascicle, three sheets; also titled *Wǔ yǒufǎnfù dàyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Great Meaning of the Five With Repentance). Translated by Jūqú Jīngshēng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dìzǐ sī fù shēng jīng* (Sūtra of the Disciple Who Died and Was Reborn). Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fóshuō dìzǐ shì fó jíxiong jīng* (One Scroll). Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng of Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fó dà sēng dà jīng* (The Great Sūtra of the Buddha and the Great Sangha), consisting of seven pages; translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Yejī jīng* (Yajña-sūtra), three sheets; translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Jūqú Jīngshēng.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The Mālava-rāja-sūtra, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang lu.
The Mada-rāja-sūtra, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Wǔ kǒngbù shì jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Terrors of the World), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of Northern Liang, during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Fēnhuótánwáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Prasenajit). Translated by Jūqú Jīngshēng during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of Caṇḍavyūha*, one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the Chángfáng Record.

*The Sūtra of the Lazy Ploughman*, one fascicle, two sheets. The old records call it *The Sūtra of the Lazy Ploughman’s Son*. Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn at Lùnyè Monastery during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
*Zhuyuan jing* (Sutra of Incantations and Vows), one fascicle. The above was translated by the monk Huijian during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.

The *Sūtra of the Wise and the Foolish*, one volume consisting of thirteen, sixteen, seventeen, or fifteen fascicles, totaling three hundred and seventy-five sheets. Translated during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty by Huijue and Weide at Gaochang Commandery.

*Jiushang jing* (Sutra on the Nine Wounds), one fascicle. Translated by the Southern Qi śramaṇa Daobei;
appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Shen zizhi shen jie jing* (Sutra of the Verses on Deep Self-Knowledge of the Body), one fascicle. Translated by the Southern Qi śramaṇa Daobei.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle titled *Ānàn jìng jīng* (The Scripture of Ānanda’s Admonitions). The aforementioned [entry] in Sēngyòu’s catalog states it is a "classical scripture" (*gǔdiàn jīng*).

*Zìjiàn zìwéi zhīwéinéngjìnjié jīng* (Sūtra on Self-Seeing and Self-Acting Knowing the Ability to Exhaust the Fetters), one fascicle. The right-hand entry in Sengyou’s catalogue states this is a classical scripture (*gǔdiān jīng*).

Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

while others select a single matter to establish the title of a fascicle.
Hao Zhi-shi was truly faithful to the classical texts.

[He translated] one fascicle of the *Sūtra of the Fifty-five Dharma Admonitions* (also known as the *Sūtra on the Practice of the Fifty-five Dharmas*), one fascicle of the *Essentials of All Meanings*, one fascicle of the *Sūtra Explaining the Paths of Good and Evil*, and one fascicle of the *Sūtra of the Heavenly King’s Descent to Become a Pig*. He also initiated the practice of bathing.
*The Buddha at That Time*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Twelve Worthies*, one fascicle (the old catalog states it is the *Sūtra of the Twelve Worthies’ Deeds*);
*The Sūtra of Uruvilvā-Kāśyapa*, one fascicle; *The Original Texts of the Four Sections*, one fascicle (Master Dao’an notes that the former two sūtras are derived from the *Dīrgha Āgama*;
another version states they are derived from the *Abhidharma*); *The Sūtra on the Gift of Virtue*, one fascicle (which contains the passage "There is a worthy").
*Fajing* (Dharmapada), one fascicle; *Brahmadatta-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets; *Uttara-sūtra*, one fascicle, also known as the *Uttara-mātṛ-sūtra*;
*Śukla-vitarka-varga-sūtra*, one fascicle—the old catalog states "Śukla-vitarka-yu," but according to the *Sheng jing* (Sūtra of Birth), there is no character "zhang" (chapter);
*Dao-di-zhong-yao-yu-zhang* (Essential Words from the Stages of the Path), one fascicle, also called the *Dao-di jing* (Sūtra of the Stages of the Path).
*The Sūtra on the Four Classes of Families Asking about the One Worthy of Receiving Alms*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Resolving Disputes and Clarifying What Is Not Understood*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Heterodox Teachers Questioning the Dwelling Place*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Heterodox Teachers Questioning the Root of the Dharma*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Strength of the Wise Man’s Hands*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Practice of the Eight Dharmas*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Evil People*, one fascicle.

*Juǎn zhāntán tiáo fó jīng* (The Sūtra on the Buddha Adjusted by Sandalwood), one fascicle; *Zhé fó jīng* (The Sūtra on the Broken Buddha), one fascicle. These were previously listed in the *Lìngwáng sēnyòu lù* (Sēnyòu’s Record of the Liang Dynasty) as "Ancient Heterodox Scriptures.

The *Xīnjí āngōng liángtǔ yìjīng* (New Collection of Heterodox Scriptures from Liangzhou by Master Ān) lists the following: *Chū sēnyòu lù yǒuwú jīng* (Scripture on Existence and Non-existence from Sēnyòu’s Record), one fascicle;

*The Yueguo Poor Man’s Sūtra on Hiring a Barber*, one fascicle; *The Simile of the Earthenware Pot Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Demons*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Four Impermanences*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Five Losses and the Covering*, one fascicle; *The Essential Truth Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Original Non-existence*, one fascicle;

one fascicle of the *Bārbǎosamādhi jing*; one fascicle of the *Sansheng jing*; one fascicle of the *Qiyu shu jing*—the old catalog states this is the *Qiyu sishu jing*;
one fascicle of the *Wugailiyi jing*; one fascicle of the *Taizhizhi jing*; and one fascicle of the *Kuxiang jing*.
*Sūtra on Requiring the Buddha for Deliverance*, one fascicle; *Sūtra on Causes and Conditions*, one fascicle; *Sūtra on the Three Wisdoms*, one fascicle;
*Sūtra on the Householder Kālaya of the Kingdom of Pūrṇavardhana*, one fascicle; *Sūtra on the Four Fearlessnesses*, one fascicle; *Sūtra on Resolving the Meaning of Dharma Affairs*, one fascicle;
*Sūtra on Skillful Transformation* (formerly titled *Mañjuśrī’s Sūtra on the Samādhi of Skillful Transformation*, or simply *Sūtra on Skillful Transformation*), one fascicle.
*Meijing* (Sūtra on Obscurity), one fascicle; *Ōuhējīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Āśravas), one fascicle; *Qīyánchànlìjīng* (Sūtra on the Seven-Syllable Benefits of Dhyāna), one fascicle;

The above were previously recorded in Sēngyòu’s catalogue as "Various Sūtras from the Liáng Territory" (*Liángtǔ yījīng*). They are now included in the "New Collection of Master Ān’s Various Sūtras from Guānzhōng. One [fascicle].

*Jǔ Ān wéi gǔdào zhòujīng* (The Sūtra on Ānanda Being Cursed by a Sorcery Spell), one fascicle; the old catalog states that although [An] was cursed by a sorcery spell, it is the *Wángshèchéng Língjiùshānjīng* (Sūtra of the Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain in Rājagṛha), one fascicle;

One fascicle: *The Sūtra of the Buddha at the Bamboo Grove*. One fascicle: *The Sūtra on Teaching the Dharma to People*. One fascicle: *The Sūtra on the Aspiration for the Path*. Two fascicles:

one fascicle: *The Sūtra of Prince Pila*; one fascicle: *The Sūtra of the Eight Virtues*; one fascicle: *The Sūtra of Good Virtue*. The above were previously included among the monastic scriptures.

it was translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu state during the era of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Jíshàn shí'è jīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Evil Deeds of Good Fortune), translated by Zhī Fǎdù; recorded in the *Bǎochàng lù*.
The *Zhìyì jīng* (Sūtra on Governing the Mind), one fascicle; recorded in the *Zhī Mǐndù lù*.

*The Scripture on the Five Divine Messengers of King Yama*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Huijian during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle, *The Scripture on the Four Kinds of Food*. The above was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty at the New Temple in Yangdu.

*The Scripture on the Questions of the Golden-Colored Rishi*, one fascicle in two volumes. Translated during the era of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Jñānagupta from North India at Yizhou.
The *Jingtu jing* (Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra), one fascicle in seven volumes, was translated in the first year of the Yongyuan era; [the Master] was eight years old.
The *Baoding jing*, translated in the first year of the Yongyuan era, he was eight years old. The *Zhengding jing*, translated in the second year of the Yongyuan era, he was nine years old.

The *Shengman jing* (Śrīmālādevī Siṃhanāda Sūtra), translated in the second year of the Yongyuan era, he was nine years old. The *Fahua jing* (Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra), translated in the second year of the Yongyuan era. [Recorded by] Changfang.
At the age of nine, the *Bhaiṣajyavastu-sūtra* was translated in the third year of the Yongyuan era.
At the age of ten, the *Kumārabhūta-sūtra* was translated in the third year of the Yongyuan era. At the age of ten, the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra* was translated in the third year of the Yongyuan era.
At the age of ten, the *Vārāṇasī-sūtra*, the *Uruvilvā-sūtra*, and the *Prajñapti-sūtra* were translated in the first year of the Tianjian era. At thirteen, the *Avataṃsaka-vaipulya-śiromaṇi-sūtra*.

In the first year of the Tianjian era (502 CE), at the age of thirteen, he produced the *Siṃhanāda-sūtra*. In the third year of the Tianjian era (504 CE), at the age of fifteen, he produced the *Udānavarga* (Yútuówèi jīng).

In the fourth year of the Tianjian era (505 CE), while at Huaguang Hall within the palace, at the age of sixteen, he produced the *Udāna-varga*, the *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa-sūtra* preface, the *Saptabhava-sūtra*, and the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* (Miàozhuānyán jīng) in one volume and four fascicles. These were added to the collection.

*Yi jing* (Sutra on Intention), one fascicle, two volumes; translated in the third year of the Tianjian era [504 CE]; he was fifteen years old. *Miaoyi shizihou jing* (Sutra of the Lion’s Roar of Sublime Meaning), one fascicle, three volumes;
translated in the fourth year of the Tianjian era [505 CE]; he was sixteen years old. *Anahan jing* (Sutra on the Anāgāmin), one fascicle, two volumes;
translated in the fourth year of the Tianjian era [505 CE]; he was sixteen years old. The above comprises twenty-one works.
