Reciting them from memory in continuous succession—
could this not be the result of reciting them in a previous life?
Yet it is claimed that they were divinely bestowed.
How can one be so foolish and blind as to obscure the path of wisdom?
*The Sutra of King Gao Contemplating Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle. During the Northern Qi dynasty, there was a prisoner whose crime merited the ultimate punishment.
In a dream, he saw a holy monk orally transmit the sutra to him;
he recited it with a sincere heart until the count reached a thousand repetitions.
When the execution was imminent, his blade snapped.
Consequently, he was spared from death;
this is now known as the *Gao Wang Jing*.
It is recorded in the *Qi Shu*, the *Biographies of Eminent Monks*, and Master Senglin’s *Bian Zheng Lun*.

However, as for the substance of these scriptures, they consist of passages from the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* concerning the invocation of Avalokiteśvara, through which all receive the fulfillment of their vows; they describe how he transforms according to the various types of beings and recites mantras to save suffering sentient beings.
The above comprises ninety-three scriptures in one hundred and seven fascicles, for which no translators are recorded.
The Great Táng Catalogue of All Determined Scriptures, Volume Seven;
The Great Táng Catalogue of All Determined Scriptures, Volume Eight.
Compiled by order of the Empress of the Great Táng, by the śramaṇa Míngquán and others of Fóshòujì Monastery.
Catalogue of Re-translated Scriptures of the Hīnayāna, Volume One. Three hundred and seventy-seven works in eight hundred and forty-six fascicles.
*The Scripture in Forty-two Chapters*, one fascicle, six sheets; first translated during the tenth year of the Yongping era of Emperor Ming of the Later Han dynasty.
Kāśyapa Mātanga and Zhu Falan translated [it] at the Baima Monastery;
this appears in the Record of Changfang.
*The Scripture in Forty-two Sections*, one fascicle, second edition; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu kingdom (as cited above).
This differs slightly from the version translated by Kāśyapa Mātaṅga.
*The Scripture in Forty-two Sections*, one fascicle, third edition; the above three scriptures are different translations of the same original text, as seen in the Chángfáng Lù.
*The Scripture on the Contemplation of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle; third appearance. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Scripture on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*, one fascicle; slightly different from the version translated by An Shigao of the Han dynasty. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Catalogue of Changfang.
The two preceding scriptures are translations of the same original text.
*The Scripture on the Sufferings One Desires to Encountered*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Yùsuǒyùzhìhuàn jīng* (Sūtra on What One Desires Leads to Suffering), one fascicle; the second edition, translated by Qiduomi of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding sutras are different translations of the same original text.
*Mādreyī-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as *Māndreyī-sūtra* or *Ānanda-huodong-nü-wohuo-jing*—three sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Modengnü jiexing zhong liushi jing* (The Scripture on the Six Matters of Resolving Form from the Mātaṅga Woman), one fascicle, three sheets; the translator is lost.
The above is recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

*Zuìyè bàoyìng jiàohuà dìyù jīng* (Sūtra on the Teaching and Transformation of Hell through the Retribution of Sinful Karma), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Diyù bàoyìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Retribution of Hell), six pages. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zuìyè bàyīng jīng* (Sūtra on the Retribution of Karmic Offenses). The *Bǎochàng lù* states that its alternative title is the *Zuìyè bàyīng jiàohuà dìyù jīng* (Sūtra on Teaching and Transforming Hell through the Retribution of Karmic Offenses). Translated by the śramaṇa Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two scriptures above are translations of the same original text.

*Ānán wèn shì fó jíxióng jīng* (The Scripture on Ānanda’s Inquiry into the Auspiciousness and Inauspiciousness of Serving the Buddha), one fascicle; the *Sēngyòu lù* states that it is also titled *Ānán wèn jīng* (The Scripture on Ānanda’s Inquiry) and consists of four sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
*Fenbie jing* (Sūtra on Discernment), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Ānanda-pṛcchā-vibhaṅga-sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Vibhaṅga-sūtra* or the *Ānanda-āśritya-bhagavat-maṅgalyāmaṅgalya-sūtra*. Translated by Dharmanandi of the Qifu clan during the Western Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

Disciple Màn compiled the *Qíyù jīng* (Jīvaka Sūtra) in one fascicle. The above was translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The four scriptures above are translations of the same original text.

One scroll of the *Śatruñjaya-sūtra* (also called the *Śatruñjaya-tāyī-ming-èrshíbā-xiù-jīng*, also called the *Tāyī-míngxīng-èrshíbā-xiù-jīng*, and also called the *Hǔ'ěr-jīng*) was translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Móṭéngjiā jīng* (Mātṛkā-sūtra), in three or two fascicles, totaling thirty-seven sheets. Translated during the Wu dynasty by Zhu Luyi and Zhi Qian at Wuchang.
The *Sūtra on the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions of the Crown Prince*, one fascicle, translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Śītavana-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-six sheets; also known as the *Sūtra on the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions of the Prince*, or the *Sūtra of Prince Vyāghra-karṇa*. The *Huàdù lù* (Record of Transformation and Deliverance) states that it is the second translation of the "Vyāghra-karṇa" section, sharing the same source but differing in its production; it differs slightly from the version translated by Gautama Saṃghadeva during the Han dynasty. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin during the Yongjia era.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The four scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.
*Wǔ mǔzǐ jīng*, one fascicle, two sheets; translated during the Wu dynasty by Zhi Qian.
*Śrāmaṇeraka-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema during the reign of Emperor An of the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
The *Arthavargīya-sūtra* (Yìzú jīng), one fascicle in two volumes and forty-one pages, was translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
It appears in the *Huàdù sì lù*.
*Yizu jing* (Scripture on the Fulfillment of Meaning), one fascicle in two volumes. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Tianshen jinbao jing* (Scripture on the Divine Prohibition of Treasures), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Jìngmiàn wáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Ādarśamukha). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jingmianwang jing* (Sūtra on King Mirror-Face), one fascicle. Translated by Kang Senghui during the Chilu era of the Wu dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jie tanwang jing* (Sūtra on King Jie’s Greed), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty.

Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng): *Fànzhì cící jīng* (The Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Words of Farewell), one fascicle; *Fànzhì yízhēng déjiětuō jīng* (The Sūtra on the Brahmin Resolving Doubts through Attaining Liberation), one fascicle; *Dǒulè fànzhì jīng* (The Sūtra of the Brahmin Dǒulè), one fascicle; *Fǎguān fànzhì jīng* (The Sūtra of the Brahmin Fǎguān), one fascicle; *Fànzhì guānwúcháng déjiětuō jīng* (The Sūtra on the Brahmin Observing Impermanence and Attaining Liberation), one fascicle; *Měngguān fànzhì jīng* (The Sūtra of the Brahmin Měngguān), one fascicle. These eleven preceding sūtras are all extracted from the *Yìzú jīng* (Sūtra of Meaningful Verses).

The *Rājadharma-smṛtyupasthāna-sūtra*, one fascicle, seventy scrolls, totaling one thousand four hundred and one pages. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci in the first year of the Xinghe era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Translated at the residence of the Grand Chancellor Gao Cheng in Ye City.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra of the Goose King Suprabha*; this former sūtra is derived from the *Saddharmasmṛtyupasthāna-sūtra*.
*The Sūtra of King Māndhātṛ*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty;
appears in the Changfang lu.
*The Sūtra of King Māndhātṛ*, one fascicle. The content is identical to the Mahādeva-sūtra in the eighth fascicle of the *Madhyama Āgama*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Jīvaka of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are translations of the same original text.

*The Sūtra on the Ten Wholesome and Ten Unwholesome Deeds*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra Distinguishing Good and Evil*. Translated by Zhi Fadu during the Yongning era of the Western Jin dynasty, under Emperor Hui.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Ten Wholesome and Ten Unwholesome Actions*, translated for the second time. This was translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in Yangzhou.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding scriptures are translations of the same original text.
*The Scripture of the Five Hundred Brahmans*, one fascicle: translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Bànzhì jīng* (Brahmacārin Sūtra), which is a different translation of the same text as the *Wǔbǎi bànzhì jīng* (Sūtra of the Five Hundred Brahmacārins).
The right-hand entry in the *Bǎochàng lù* states that Zhúlùtóuyán recited it out [from memory].
Recorded in the *Shixing lu* (Catalogue of the Beginning Prosperity).
The first two scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.

*Xiǎoběnqǐ jīng* (Sūtra on the Minor Account of the Arising), one volume in two fascicles; also called *Xiūxíngběnqǐ jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Arising of Practice) or *Xiūxíng jīng* (Sūtra on Practice). Translated by Zhi Yao in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Ling of the Later Han.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, two scrolls, thirty-eight pages of the *Xiūxíng běnqǐ jīng* (Sūtra on the Original Acts of Practice). The *Bǎochàng lù* states that it is also titled *Sùxíng běnqǐ*. It was translated by Zhú Tángguǒ and Kāng Mèngxiáng during the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures):

One fascicle, two scrolls, of the *Tàizǐ Běnyǐ Ruìyìng Jīng* (Sutra on the Auspicious Responses of the Prince’s Original Arising). Its initial publication also referred to it as the *Ruìyìng Běnyǐ*, and it is also titled the *Zhōngběnqǐ Jīng*. Translated by the foreign śramaṇa Kang Mengxiang of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle in one volume of the *Zhōngběnqǐ jīng* (also called the *Tàizǐ Zhōngběnqǐ jīng*), translated by Zhu Fanguo in the twelfth year of the Jiàn'ān era of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dàzǐ běnqǐ ruìyìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Auspicious Responses of the Great Son’s Original Arising) in two scrolls and thirty-five pages; also known as the *Ruìyìng běnqǐ jīng*. The second edition, translated by Zhīqiān at Jīnlíng during the Jiàn-xīng era of the Wú dynasty, differs slightly from the edition translated by Kāṅ Mèngxiáng.
Recorded in the *Chūn-nei-dian-lu*.
One fascicle, four scrolls: the *Past Causes and Effects Sutra* (*Guoqu yinguo jing*). Translated by Buddhabhadra at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor An of the Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang-lu*.
The *Past and Present Causes and Effects Sūtra* (Guoqu xianzai yinguo jing), one fascicle in four rolls, ninety-six pages; translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
It appears in the *Neidian lu*.
The seven preceding sūtras are different translations of the same original text.

The *Zazang jing* (Sūtra on the Miscellaneous Collection), one fascicle, nine pages, shares the same substance as the four versions including the *Guiwen Mulian egui baoying* (The Ghost’s Question to Maudgalyāyana on the Retribution of Hungry Ghosts) and the *Mulian shuo didiy egui yinyuan* (Maudgalyāyana’s Explanation of the Causes and Conditions of Hellish and Hungry Ghosts); they differ only in name and are distinct translations, as noted in the *Baoshang lu*. The above was translated at the capital of Yangdu by Buddhabhadra together with Faxian during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*Zazang jing*, one fascicle.
Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Scripture on the Ghosts’ Questions to Maudgalyāyana*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
included in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture on the Retribution of Hungry Ghosts*, one fascicle, also titled *The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions of the Hells and Hungry Ghosts Spoken by Maudgalyāyana*. The above four scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Qǐxíng xíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Arising of Practice), one fascicle in two volumes, also titled *Shíyuán jīng* (Sūtra of the Ten Conditions), thirty-six pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Kāṅ Mèngxiáng during the reign of Emperor Xiàn of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng):

*Mùqiāng cìjiǎo yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Being Pierced in the Foot by a Wooden Spear), one fascicle. This and the preceding sūtra from the *Xīngqǐ xíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Arising of Practice) are the same original text translated separately.
*Nàinǚ qíyù jīng* (Sūtra of the Maiden Nàinǚ and Jīyù), one fascicle; translated during the Later Han dynasty by Ān Shìgāo.

*The Scripture on the Elder’s Daughter and Jīvaka*, one fascicle, seventeen sheets; also known as *The Scripture on the Elder’s Daughter*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty. Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalogue).
It is also found in the *Changfang lu* (Changfang’s Catalogue).
The two preceding sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*The Sūtra of the Poor Old Man*, one fascicle, three pages; also titled *The Sūtra of the Poor Old Man*. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Dharmottara-lu*:
*The Sūtra of the Poor Old Man*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn at Lùnyě Monastery during the reign of Emperor Xiàowŭ of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The first two sutras above are different translations of the same original text.

*Yuè nán jīng* (Sutra on Overcoming Difficulties), one fascicle, two sheets; also titled *Nán jīng* (Sutra of Difficulties) or *Dì èr chū bǎo chàng lù yún yuē nán zhǎngzhě jīng* (The Sutra of Elder Nán as recorded in the second section of the *Bǎochàng lù*). Translated by the lay devotee Niè Chéngyuǎn of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng), it says:
*Nánjīng* (Difficult Classic) in one fascicle, also titled *Yuènán* (Difficulties of Yuè); translated by the Eastern Jin monk Shi Sōng.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Lù.

It is titled *Nan jing* (Difficult Scripture), one fascicle; also known as the *Yue nan jing* (Scripture on Questions from Yue). Translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
The three aforementioned scriptures are translations of the same original text.

The *Saptakumārikā-sūtra* (Seven Maidens Sutra), one fascicle, six pages; also known as the *Saptakumārikā-mūla-sūtra*. Changfang states it was translated from the Abhidharma. It was translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
It appears in the Changfang lu.
*Qīnǚběnjīng* (The Scripture on the Original Story of the Seven Daughters), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

This *Qīnǚběnjīng*, one fascicle, is largely identical with slight variations to that produced by Zhi Qian; it is also titled *Nǚběnxīnmíngjīng* (The Scripture on the Heart-Clearance of the Woman's Origin) and *Qīnǚjīng* (The Scripture of the Seven Daughters). Translated by Shèng Jiān of the Western Jin in the State of Hénán.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
The three scriptures above are translations of the same original text.
*Nāgarāja-bhrātṛ-sūtra*, one fascicle, three sheets; also titled *Durnāgarāja-sūtra*. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
*The Scripture on Maudgalyāyana Subduing the Dragon King*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two preceding sutras are different translations of the same original text.
*Chansi manzu jing* (Sutra on the Fulfillment of Dhyāna Contemplation), one fascicle; translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Treasures).

*Xiànsī Mǎnzú Jīng* (Sūtra on the Fulfillment of Dhyāna Contemplation), one fascicle. Translated by the Western Region śramaṇa Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
The two preceding sūtras are translations of the same original text.
*Quanjinxue dao jing* (Sutra on Encouraging the Study of the Way), one fascicle; one version lacks the character "quàn" (encourage). Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Xin xue jing* (Sutra on Advancing in Learning), one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-śikṣā-praśaṃsā-sūtra*, also titled the *Quànjìn jīng* (Sūtra on Encouraging the Study of the Path). Translated by the Song dynasty monk Shi Yong.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
The three preceding scriptures are different translations of the same original text.
*The Scripture of the Eight Masters*, one fascicle, three sheets; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
It appears in the Neidian lu and the Changfang lu.
*The Scripture on the Eight Teachers*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
It appears in the *Changfang lu*.
The two preceding scriptures are the same original text translated separately.
The *Sheng jing* (Sūtra on Birth), one fascicle, in five or four rolls; the *Baochang lu* states it consists of one hundred twenty-six sheets. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Shēng jīng* (Sūtra on Birth), five scrolls in total; translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Zhìyán of Liangzhou during the fourth year of the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Daughter Who Disputed in a Previous Life*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Scripture on the Son’s Passing Away*, one fascicle. Appears in the second fascicle [of the *Zhōngjīng Mùlù*]. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fó fù luǒxíng zǐ jīng* (The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Covering of the Naked Ascetic), one fascicle; also titled *Shěn luǒxíng zǐ jīng* (The Sūtra on Examining the Naked Ascetic). Extracted from the third fascicle. Translated by An Shìgāo of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Kātyāyana Sūtra*—also known as the *Kātyāyana Anitya Sūtra*—is found in the second volume; it was translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle titled *Wǒsuǒjīng* (The Scripture on What I Have Experienced), translated by Zhī Qián of the Wu state during the first year [of the era],
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jigou jing* (The Sutra of the Mad Dog), one fascicle; identical to the *Dungou*. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Jixiang zhou jing* (The Sutra of Auspicious Mantras), one fascicle; appears in the second fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu period.
*Fan zhi jing* (The Scripture of the Brahmacārin), one fascicle; appears in the fifth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Pañcārṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle. Found in the first fascicle. Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue. *Śṛgāla-danta-kṣata-svāmī-sūtra*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty; it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.

*The Scripture on the Five Sons of the King* (one fascicle), also titled *The Scripture on the Five Sons of Merit*, translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty; it appears in the third fascicle. Dao’an states that it is found in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.
*Prabhāsa-puṣpa-brāhmaṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle; appears in the fourth fascicle. Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty;
see Sengyou’s *Lu*. *Sarva-stotra-saṃgraha-sūtra*, one fascicle; appears in the fifth fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Zǒngchí jīng* (also titled *Fóxīn zǒngchí jīng*), appearing in the third fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wudi of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Elephant King Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Fushi jing* (Sutra on Making the Abdomen Firm), one fascicle; appears in the third fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Xianju jing* (Sutra on Dwelling in Seclusion), one fascicle; appears in the second fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin period.
*Mi-jù jīng* (The Sutra on Honey), one fascicle;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin dynasty. Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. The above [text] is from the fourth fascicle.

*The Scripture of the Five Hundred Boys*, one fascicle; also called *The Scripture of the Young Boys*. Extracted from the fourth fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bo Fazu of Henei during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.

*Xiye zihuo jing* (Sutra on Livelihood through Evil Deeds), one fascicle; translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti of the Western Jin dynasty. Found in the first fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*] and recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sūtra on the Illness of a Bhikṣu*, one fascicle; appearing in the third fascicle [of this collection]. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Individual Aspirations of the Bhikṣus*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty. Appears in the right-hand column [of the catalog];
recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*He-nan shi-jing* (The Scripture on the Explanation of He-nan), one fascicle; appears in the third fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmayaśas during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.

Recorded in the *Changfang lu*. *He-nan jing* (The Scripture of He-nan), one fascicle; appears in the first fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmayaśas during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*. One fascicle:
the *Bǐqiū fēnwéi jīng* (Sutra on the Alms-Gathering Bhikṣu); also called the *Fēnwéi bǐqiū jīng*. Found in the first fascicle; translated by Fǎjù and Fǎlì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dúyù jīng* (Poison Simile Sūtra), which differs slightly from the *Dúcǎo yù jīng* (Poisonous Herb Simile Sūtra). Found in the fourth fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Simile of Poisonous Herbs*, one fascicle. Found in the fourth fascicle; translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Kauśāmbī-rājahaṃsa-sūtra*, one fascicle; excerpted from the fourth volume. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Lǔtuó jīng* (Scripture Spoken by a Donkey). [Appears in] the fourth volume on the right. Translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty by Zhu Tanwulan at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in the capital of Yangdu.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).
One fascicle of the *Mayūra-ājñāta-sūtra*. [Appears] on the right in the fifth fascicle.
Translated by the Eastern Jin śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in the capital of Yangdu.

*Yejī jīng* (The Scripture of the Wild Chicken), one fascicle. Found in the first fascicle of the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Found in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Gǔxūwū jīng* (The Scripture of the Gǔxū Bird), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Gūxūwū jīng*. Found in Fascicle Three. Translated by Zhu Tánwúlán during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fùfū jīng* (Sutra on Husband and Wife), one fascicle; extracted from the fourth fascicle [of the *Mahāsaṃnipāta-sūtra*].
Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Ābhā-makkaṭa-sūtra* (The Scripture on the Turtle and the Monkey). Found in the first fascicle, translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dìzǐ guò mìng jīng* (Sūtra on the Disciple’s Transcendence of Life), appearing in the fourth volume above, was translated by Zhu Tanwulan at the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*Fóxīn zǒngchí jīng* (The Scripture on the Buddha-Mind Dhāraṇī), one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Mahiṣarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; included in the fourth fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Rājña-śaśaka-sūtra*, one fascicle; included in the fourth fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin.
Appearing in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Jiǔshēng jīng* (Sūtra on Uncle and Nephew). The above [entry] appears in the first fascicle; it was translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
It appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Shane’e jing* (Sūtra on Good and Evil), one fascicle; appears in the fourth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Zhubi wei niu jing* (Sūtra on Becoming an Ox Due to Debt), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
*Na-lai jing*, one fascicle.
Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śāriputra-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle. Extracted from the second fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Fallen Pearl Falling into the Ocean*, one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Sūtra of the Lay Practitioner Ayi Shanchi*, one fascicle. The *Dharmodgata Lù* states that the *Sūtra of the Lay Practitioner Ayi Shanchi and His Son* appears in the fifth fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng of Northern Liang during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
*Chanzhang fù lù* (Record of Dharma Master Chanzhang).

*Zhānshé mó bàozhì bǎng fó jīng* (The Scripture on Zhānshémo’s Violent Intentions and Slander of the Buddha), one fascicle. Found in the first fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the Catalogue of Changfang.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Questions of the Householder Haridraka*, appearing as the forty-eighth among the sūtras in the second fascicle and above.
The *Sūtra on Birth*.

The Madhyama Āgama, one collection consisting of sixty fascicles (or fifty-eight fascicles), totaling one thousand two hundred and eighty-seven sheets. According to the record of Dharmatrāta, it contains two hundred and twenty-two fascicles; according to the record of Seng Changfang, it contains sixty-nine sūtras. This was [translated] during the first year of the Long’an era of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Saṃghadeva translated [this work] in Yangzhou; it appears in the Changfang lu (Catalogue of Dharma-Repository).
The Madhyama Āgama, one collection in fifty-nine fascicles; translated for the first time by Dharmānandi during the Former Qin dynasty.
This appears in the Changfang Record.
The Catuḥsatya Sūtra, one fascicle; translated at Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Huan of the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
*The Scripture on What is Dharma and What is Not-Dharma*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yīqièliúshèshǒuyīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Cause and Condition of the Gathering and Guarding of All Outflows), one fascicle, four sheets; also titled *Liúshè jīng* (Sūtra on the Gathering of Outflows) or *Yīqièliúshèshǒujīng*. The *Wùlù* (Records of Wu) states it is also called *Liúshèshǒuyīnjīng* or *Shòuyīnjīng*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Lòufēn bù jīng* (Leakage Distribution Sūtra), eight pages. Translated by An Shigao in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Huan of the Later Han.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Layman Daśaśākha of the City of Aṣṭaka*, one fascicle (three pages), translated by An Shigao of the Later Han;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Mutual Reliance of the Original Forms*, one fascicle; the *Wú lù* calls it the *Dàxiāngyīzhì jīng*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Yuánběnzhì jīng* (Sutra on the Causes and Conditions of the Original Basis), three sheets; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Elder Brothers Visiting the Buddha*, one fascicle. Sengyou states that it is also titled *The Sūtra on the Two Brothers, the Elders Kṛṣṇa and Tāta, Visiting the World-Honored One*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fùmǔ ēnqín bàojīng* (Sutra on Diligently Repaying Parental Kindness), also titled *Fùmǔ ēn nánbào jīng* (Sutra on the Difficulty of Repaying Parental Kindness). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*The Brahmaṇa’s Practice Sūtra*, one fascicle. Appears in fascicle thirty-nine. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Catalogue.

The *Venerable Bakula Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Bakula Sūtra* (identical in title to the record in the *Huadusi lu*), and also known as the *Sūtra on the Meaning of the Heterodox Bakula*—is found in the eighth fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*The Scripture of Rāṣṭrapāla*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Yao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Aniruddha-aṣṭānusmṛti-sūtra*, one fascicle—also titled the *Dhyāna-practice of Gathering the Mind* or simply the *Aṣṭānusmṛti-sūtra*—appears in the eighteenth volume, four pages long. It dates from the era of Emperor Ling of the Later Han dynasty.
Translated by Zhi Yao in Luoyang;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Làitāhuólú jīng* (The Scripture of Rāṣṭrapāla). This second edition differs slightly from that of Zhi Yao. Some say it is the *Luóhàn Làitāhuólú jīng* (The Scripture of the Arhat Rāṣṭrapāla), found in the thirty-first fascicle, consisting of twelve sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
The *Fanmoyu jing* (Brahmadatta-sūtra), one fascicle, consisting of ten sheets, appears in the thirty-first fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. It was translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu period.
It is recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Zhāijīng* (Sūtra on the Fast), one fascicle; also known as *Bāguānzhāijīng* (Sūtra on the Eightfold Precept Fast) and *Ūpāsikāduōshèjiājīng* (Sūtra on the Laywoman Duōshèjiā). Extracted from the fifty-fifth fascicle, four pages. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Inner Canon Catalog).
One fascicle of the *Shenri jing* (Sūtra of Shenri), comprising eight pages. Translated by Zhi Qian at Luoyang and Ye during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Śrīmaṇava-sūtra*, also titled the *Pañcaskandha-hetuvastu-sūtra*, appearing in the twenty-fifth volume, four pages. Translated by Zhi Qian at Wuchang during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.

The *Dharmamūla-sūtra* in one fascicle appears in the second volume, on the right side of the second page, of the *Chūnèidiǎnlù*. It was translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty;
it appears in the *Chángfánglù*.
*Śūṇṭhaya-jātaka-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as *Brāhmaṇa-śūṇṭhaya-jātaka-sūtra*, three sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty].
Appears in the Chángfáng Catalogue. *Bimbisāra-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as *Bimbasāra-rāja-pañca-praṇidhāna-sūtra*. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu [Dynasty].
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Qīzhī jīng* (or, as some say, the *Qīzhì jīng*), two pages from the first fascicle; translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Questions of Bakula* (also known as *The Sūtra of Bakula*), one fascicle. Dao’an states that it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it is recorded in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*Pinqiong jing* (Sūtra on Poverty), one fascicle; extracted from the twenty-ninth fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty. Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Lexiang jing* (Sūtra on the Perception of Pleasure), one fascicle; extracted from the twenty-sixth fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Li shui jing* (Sūtra on Leaving Sleep), one fascicle.
Found in the twentieth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Found in the *Changfang lu*.
*Śaiśirī-sūtra*, one fascicle; extracted from the twenty-third volume. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng-lù*.
*Navasaṃvatsara-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmaratna during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*He ku jing* (The Scripture on the Sufferings of What), one fascicle. Found in the thirty-sixth fascicle; translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Zunshang jing* (Sūtra on the Honored Superior), one fascicle; extracted from the forty-third fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty. Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Yingfa jing* (Sūtra on the Corresponding Dharma), one fascicle; extracted from the forty-fifth fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
The *Yijing* (Scripture on Intent),
one fascicle, appears in the forty-fifth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. It was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty and is recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Scripture on Learning Spoken by the Buddha for the Elder Brahmin of the Yellow Bamboo Garden*, one fascicle; extracted from the thirtieth fascicle.
Dao’an states that it was translated during the Western Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
Extracted from Sengyou’s *Lu*.

One fascicle of the *Gangā-nadī-upamā-sūtra*, also known as the *Sūtra on the Eight Qualities of the Ocean*, the *Campa-bhikṣu-sūtra*, or the *Dharma-sāgara-sūtra*. The *Chángfáng-lù* states: "The *Gangā-nadī-upamā-sūtra* consists of three sheets; translated during the Western Jin dynasty by Zhu Faju."
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, two sheets, titled *The Sūtra on the Buddha Answering a Bhikṣu Regarding Many Upāsakas Who Have Passed Away*, translated by Dharmakṣema during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fóshuō qiúyù jīng* (Sūtra on Seeking Desire), one fascicle, eleven pages. Translated by Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fumijing* (The Sūtra of Fumi), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty. Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Dǐngshēngwáng gùshì jīng* (The Scripture on the Story of King Māndhātṛ), one fascicle. Also titled *Wénduójié wáng jīng* (The Scripture of King Māndhātṛ) or *Dǐngshēngwáng jīng* (The Scripture of King Māndhātṛ). Appears in fascicle eleven, five sheets. Translated by Zhu Faju during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zhānpó bǐqīu jīng* (The Sūtra of the Bhikṣu Campā); the *Dámólù* states it is the same as the *Héngshui jīng* (Sūtra of the Ganges) in four sheets. Translated jointly by Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the Western Jin dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Causes of Suffering and Darkness*, one fascicle; appears in the twenty-fifth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by Dharmagupta and Dharmasthita during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Ārdraka-sūtra*, one fascicle; second translation. Fascicle 29. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Puṇyacaryā-sūtra*, one fascicle; appears in fascicle 2. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the Ēdào jīng (Sūtra on Evil Realms), also titled the Èyì jīng (Sūtra on Evil Intentions) or the Yàoyì jīng (Sūtra on Essential Intentions). Found in the fifteenth fascicle. Translated by Fǎjǔ and Fǎlì of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Fuyin jing* (The Scripture on Subduing Lust), one fascicle; extracted from the thirtieth fascicle [of the *Chusanzang ji ji*]. Translated by Faju and Fali during the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Changfang lu*.
*Shengming jing* (Sutra on the Names), one fascicle; extracted from the thirty-sixth [fascicle]. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthita during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Souchi jing* (Sutra on Receiving and Maintaining), one fascicle; extracted from the fortieth [fascicle]. Translated by Zhu Faju and Dharmasthita during the Western Jin dynasty.
*Xi'ei jing* (Sutra on the Cessation of Anger), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Faju and Fali during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Anuhvāyu-sūtra*, one fascicle; extracted from the twenty-seventh fascicle. Translated by Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty. Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*. *Niraya-sūtra*, one fascicle;
extracted from the *Niraya-varga* of the *Madhyama Āgama*. Translated by the Western Region śramaṇa Zhu Dharmananda during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Translated at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of King Piṅgala’s Five Vows*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra of King Puṣkarasārin*, seven sheets. Translated by the monk Shi Sōng of the Eastern Jin.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha Asking the Asura about the Decrease of the Great Ocean*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Wentuojie Wang Jing* (Sūtra on King Māndhātṛ), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema at Guzang during the Northern Liang period.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Shí Mónán Běnjīng* (Original Sūtra of Śreṇika), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Śukasūtra*, also known as the *Touzhāo jīng*, appearing in the forty-fourth scroll, eight pages. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Āraṇya-sūtra*, found in the fortieth volume; translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Vimānasūtra*, one fascicle; extracted from the fifty-seventh [fascicle]. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Ba guān zāi jīng* (The Sūtra on the Eightfold Fast), one fascicle; the *Bǎochàng lù* states that its alternative title is *Bāfǎ shànxù jīng*. Translated by Jūqú Jīngshēng of Northern Liáng during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle, titled *Móyí bìqū jīng* (The Scripture of the Bhikṣu Māyī), also known as the *Móyí jīng* (The Scripture of Māyī). It appears in the tenth fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Upāsaka-pañca-dharma-sūtra*, found in the thirtieth volume; translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang.
*The Scripture on the Merchant Seeking Wealth*, one fascicle. Found in Fascicle 34. Translated by the Sramana Huijian of the Song Dynasty.
Found in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Prophecy of the Fruit for Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī*, one fascicle; excerpted from the thirty-eighth fascicle, seven pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn at Lùnyě Monastery during the era of Emperor Xiào Wŭ of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Gautamī-sūtra*, found in the forty-seventh volume; translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn at Lùnyè Monastery during the reign of Emperor Wŭ of the Song dynasty.

*Yanshui yujing* (The Scripture of the Salt Water Simile), one fascicle; recorded in the *Changfang lu*. Sengyou’s record states that Master Dao’an said it was extracted from the *Madhyamāgama*, while the old records state it is the *Yanshui poyu jing* (The Scripture of the Salt Water Parable) in two sheets, extracted from the *Āgamas*.
*Foyou wubai biqiu jing* (The Scripture of the Buddha and Five Hundred Bhikṣus), one fascicle; [recorded by] Jiu...
*The Sūtra of Mahākāśyapa* (one fascicle), also known as *The Sūtra on Kāśyapa Resolving Difficulties*, extracted from the fifteenth fascicle;
*The Sūtra of Joyful Delight* (one fascicle), five sheets, extracted from the twelfth fascicle according to the *Sengyou Lu*;
*The Sūtra of the Five Divine Messengers of King Yama* (one fascicle), also known as *The Sūtra of the Iron-City Hell*, five sheets, extracted from the twelfth fascicle of the Ancient [Canon].
*Laishishi jing* (Sūtra on the Times of Future Lives), one scroll; excerpted from the thirteenth fascicle, five sheets. *Changshouwang jing* (Sūtra of King Long-life), one scroll;

excerpted from the seventeenth fascicle, five sheets. *Mao raoluan jing* (Sūtra on the Disturbance by Māra), one scroll—also titled *Bimao shi Mulian jing* (Sūtra of the Wicked Māra Testing Maudgalyāyana) or *Mowang ru Mulian lanfu jing* (Sūtra of the Demon King Entering Maudgalyāyana’s Abdomen); excerpted from the thirtieth fascicle, eight sheets. *Xiejian jing* (Sūtra on False Views).

One fascicle; excerpted from the sixtieth fascicle. *Śalyasūtra* (The Arrow Simile Sūtra), one fascicle; excerpted from the sixtieth fascicle. *Mūlapariyāyasutta* (The Fundamental Exposition Sūtra), one fascicle; excerpted from the sixtieth fascicle.
*Brahmaṇadhammika-sūtra* (The Brahmin’s Discourse on the Purity of Water), one fascicle; excerpted from the twenty-third fascicle.

*Saptakṛtvahparama-sūtra* (The Sūtra on Seven Times), one fascicle; excerpted from the [same]. *Catvāri-smṛtyupasthāna-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Four Foundations of Mindfulness), one fascicle; recorded in Sengyou’s Catalogue. One.
*The Scripture on the Original Practices of the Four Foundations of Mindfulness*, Volume 24 (from the *Sengyou Lu*).

*The Scripture on the Three Matters of Folly and Insufficiency in Ordinary People*, one fascicle (*Fajing Lu* states: "Also titled *The Scripture on the Three Matters of Folly and Ignorance in Ordinary People*";
*Sengyou Lu* states: "Extracted from the *Āgama* [Nidāna-varga]: The Buddha asked the Asura about whether the great ocean decreases").
One fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on the Eight Matters of the Ocean*. Extracted from the eighth fascicle of the *Āgama*. One fascicle, *The Sūtra on Merit*;
extracted from the thirty-fourth fascicle of the *Āgama*. One fascicle, *The Parable of the Seven Chariots*. Sengyou’s Catalog states these were extracted from the *Āgama*.
The eighty-three sūtras mentioned above are extracted from the *Madhyama Āgama*.

The *Dīrgha Āgama* (Cháng āhán jīng), one work in twenty-two fascicles; the *Chángfáng Rùzàng Lù* states it consists of twenty-five fascicles and four hundred and ninety-eight sheets. It was translated in Chang’an during the fifteenth year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty by Zhu Fonian, in collaboration with Buddhayaśas.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Catuḥsatya-sūtra*, nine sheets. Translated by Kāṅ Mèngxiáng during the Xīngpíng era of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Fanwang liushi'er jian jing* (The Brahmajāla Sūtra on the Sixty-two Views), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Fanwang liushi'er jian jing* (The Brahmajāla Sūtra on the Sixty-two Views), one fascicle, also known as the *Fanwang jing*, twenty sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fànzhì Āluóyán wèn zhǒngzūn jīng* (The Scripture on the Brahmin Arāḍa’s Questions to the Honored One of the Seed), one fascicle, eight pages. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* in two scrolls; this is the *Yóuxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Wandering), translated by Zhi Qián during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
The *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* (Dàbānnièhuán jīng), one work in two fascicles; this is the *Caryā Sūtra*. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty.
It appears in the Changfang Record (*Chángfáng lù*).

The *Vaipulya-parinirvāṇa Sūtra* (Fāngděng nièhuán jīng), one fascicle; this is also the *Caryā Sūtra*. Translated by Buddhabhadra and Faxian of the Eastern Jin dynasty. It appears in the Changfang Record.
*Jizhiguojing* (Sūtra on the Fruits of the Śramaṇa), one fascicle, sixteen sheets. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Zhangzhezizi liuguochujiajing* (Sūtra on the Six Times a Householder’s Son Leaves Home), one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by the śramaṇa Shi Huijian during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
*Mahāprajāpatī-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the Śramaṇa Bo Fazu of Henei during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sutra on the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha’s Mother*, one fascicle; a different translation from the same original as that by the Marquis of Anyang. Translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Shi Huijian at Luye Monastery.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Sūdá jīng* (Sūtra of Sudatta), one fascicle; also known as *Zhǎngzhě Sūdá jīng* (Sūtra of the Elder Sudatta) and *Sānguī Wǔjiè Cíxīn Yànhuìdé jīng* (Sutra on the Three Refuges, Five Precepts, Compassionate Mind, and Renunciation of Merit). Three sheets. Translated by Guṇavidi at the capital of Yang during the Yongming era of the Qi dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Shíbǎofǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Ten Kinds of Retribution), in two scrolls, also titled *Duōzēngdào zhāng jīng* (Sūtra of the Chapters on the Path of Many Increases), totaling twenty-seven sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Yijue lüjing* (One Scroll), also known as *Yijue lüfahxing jing*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Sengyou lu* and the *Changfang lu*.

The *Brahmacārin Ababa Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Abba Māṇava Sūtra* or the *Sūtra on the Buddha’s Explanation for the Brahmacārin Ababa*. Thirteen pages. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu Kingdom.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Tiāndì chéngbài jīng* (Sūtra on the Succession and Failure of Heaven and Earth). The above was stated by Dào'ān;
it was translated during the Jìn dynasty by Zhú Fǎhù.
Recorded in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.
*Sanye jing* (Sutra of the Three Kalpas), one fascicle. To its right, Dao’an states that it was translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
Recorded in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

One fascicle, the *Fǎpǔyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Meaning of Universal Dharma). This is the second translation; it shares the same source as the version by An Shigao but is a different translation. It is also called the *Jìn yì jīng* (Jin Dynasty Sūtra on Meaning). Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Lóutàn jīng* (Lòutan Sūtra), in six, five, or eight fascicles; translated by Zhú Fǎhù of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Loutan jing* (Lòutàn jīng), one fascicle in eight scrolls; the third translation, differing in its degree of detail. Translated by Zhu Faju and Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Lou tan jing* (Loutan jing), one fascicle, six rolls; second translation. Translated by Zhu Faju and Falì in Luoyang during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Gṛhapati’s Sixfold Prostration*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostration*, alternatively titled *The Great Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostration*, or *The Gṛhapati Vighuṣṭa’s Sixfold Prostration*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Taian era of the Jin dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu’s Practice in Accordance with the Dharma*, one fascicle. Translated by Kumārajīva of the Later Qin at Cháng'ān.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Scripture on the Names and Surnames of the Parents of the Seven Buddhas*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture on Women Not Inviting the Buddha* or *The Scripture on the Names and Surnames of the Seven Buddhas*. Four sheets. Translated during the reign of Emperor Qi of the Wei dynasty. This scripture appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sutra on the Four Searches*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on What is Not Your Own*, also known as *The Sutra on the Bhikṣu Hearing of Almsgiving*; *The Sutra on Two Bhikṣus Obtaining a Portion*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on the Dharma-body Śarīra*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on the Śarīra Remaining in the Kingdom of Rājagṛha*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on Solitary Dwelling and Contemplation, Self-Reflecting on Cessation*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on Inquiring into the Clarified Categories*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on Solitary Seated Contemplation and the Arising of Thoughts in the Mind*, one fascicle; *The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Such Being the Case Regarding the Bhikṣus*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on the Form Sought by the Bhikṣu*, one fascicle; *The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Path and the Bhikṣu*, one fascicle; *The Sutra on the Contemplation that Form is Impermanent*. From the *Sutra on the Four Searches* to the *Sutra on the Contemplation that Form is Impermanent*.
The *Chū āhan jīng* (Ekottarika Āgama).
The thirty-seven sūtras above are from the *Dīrgha Āgama*.

The *Zēngyī āhan jīng* (Ekottarika Āgama) consists of one volume of fifty fascicles; the second translation, according to Bǎochàng, consists of either thirty-three or forty-two fascicles. To its right [is noted]: translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Gautama Saṃghadeva at Mount Lu in the first year of the Long’an era of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
[This entry] appears in Changfang’s Record (*Chángfáng lù*). The aforementioned *Bǎochàng lù* states: "Regarding 'Clarifying Samādhi' (*Míngdìng*):
previously, [the teachings] mostly discussed the Four Noble Truths, the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination, the Five Aggregates, the Six Sense Bases, and the Eighteen Elements."
It records the events of the novice Sudāya’s departure and his attainment of the precepts through debate on the Dharma;
subsequently, it details the formation and destruction of the world,
as well as his realization of the Way and the deliverance of sentient beings.
Furthermore, he manifested three jeweled stairways leading to the three paths;
he manifested King Prasenajit’s ten dreams;
and he manifested a high, broad, and grand bed.
These were fashioned from gold, silver, ivory, and other materials.
Furthermore, it clarifies how the seven Buddhas attained the Way and established the precepts;
this was translated by Saṃghadeva.
It was translated on the second day of the first month in the first year of the Long’an era of the Jin dynasty.
Zhu Daozu recorded the oral dictation in writing,
resulting in thirty-three fascicles.
The *Chūdo-so* (Record of the Patriarchs’ Succession) from the Jin Dynasty consists of seven hundred and thirty-seven sheets of paper.
Furthermore, it was translated by Dharmaratna on the first day of the fourth month in the twentieth year of the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin.
The Buddha-mind dictated as it was received by the scribe,
resulting in forty-two fascicles.
This was completed in the eleventh month of that year.
Currently, both versions exist.
However, the records of the Tripiṭaka Master Sengyou state that Zhu [Fa-hu] arrived in the summer of the twentieth year of Jianyuan.
Dharmaratna translated it in thirty-three fascicles;
this appears to be an error,
as it is recorded in Sengrui’s *Biographies of the Two Qin Dynasties* (Erqin lu).
The two preceding sūtras appear twice with slight variations in their wording.

Regarding the *Ekottarika Āgama* in one volume-set of fifty fascicles (or, according to the Inner Canon, fifty-one fascicles), the initial translation by Changfang’s *Lùrù záng lù* states it consists of forty-two sūtras and nine hundred and thirty-nine sheets. It was translated in Chang’an by Dharmanandin during the twentieth year of the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin dynasty.

*Fǎpǔyì jīng* (Sūtra on the Meaning of Universal Dharma), one fascicle; also known as *Jùfǎxíng jīng* (Sūtra on the Practice of Complete Dharmas), nine sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śīkṣānanda-ṣaḍ-abhimukha-praṇāma-sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Mahāmārgabhūmi-sūtra*, one work in two fascicles; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han period.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dàoyì fāxíng jīng* (The Scripture on Dao-yi’s Practice of the Path), one fascicle, two scrolls; translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Da shiermen jing* (The Great Sūtra of the Twelve Gates), one fascicle in two volumes, or one volume; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty. Appears in the *Changfang lu*. 1. *Diyi simen jing* (Sūtra of the First Four Gates), one fascicle;

an excerpt from the *Shiermen jing*, clarifying meditative concentration (*samādhi*) according to the universal teaching of the Three Vehicles. 2. *Di'er simen jing* (Sūtra of the Second Four Gates), one fascicle; an excerpt from the *Shiermen jing*, identical to the preceding. 3. *Di-san simen jing* (Sūtra of the Third Four Gates), one fascicle; this is the *Ganlu daolü jing* (Sūtra on the Path of Ambrosia and Discipline) and the *Ganlu zhengyi jing* (Sūtra on the Correct Meaning of Ambrosia), clarifying meditative concentration. The above four sūtras were translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Chū hōshōroku* (Record of the Eminent Monks):
*Shō jūnimon kyō* (Short Twelve Gates Sutra), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Chōbōroku* (Changfang Record).
*The Merchant’s Son Performs Buddha-Deeds Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on Mahākāśyapa Meeting a Nirgrantha*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Abhidharma-pañcadharmasūtra*; the old catalogs state it is the *Abhidharma-pañcadharmacaryāsūtra*. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Qīfǎ jīng* (Sūtra on the Seven Dharmas); the old catalogs state it is the *Āpítán qīfǎ xíng jīng* (Abhidharma Sūtra on the Practice of the Seven Dharmas). Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Duosengdaozhang jing* (The Scripture on the Many Monks and the Path), one fascicle; an alternative version of the *Shibofa* (Ten Retributions). The character "dao" (path) was absent from the old catalog. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the Changfang lu.
*The Ganges Water Sūtra*, one fascicle. *Baochang’s Record* states: "The *Ganges Water Precept Sūtra*, four sheets; translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
It appears in the *Dharmarakṣa Record* and the *Wangzong Record*."
*The Sūtra of King Vaidūrya*, one fascicle; first appearance above. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of Ānanda’s Fellow Students*, one fascicle; appears in the thirty-eighth fascicle, four sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
*The Scripture on Anāthapiṇḍada’s Transformation of His Seven Sons*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Za si shi si pian jing* (Sūtra in Forty-four Miscellaneous Chapters), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*Bai liu shi pin jing* (Sūtra in One Hundred and Sixty Sections), one fascicle. The old catalogues state it is the *Zengyi ahan bai liu zhang jing* (Ekottarika Āgama Sūtra in One Hundred and Sixty Chapters). Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
*The Sutra on the Death of a Brahmin’s Son and His Unceasing Affection*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Brāhmaṇa Avoiding Death*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han;
recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Water Simile*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*The Sutra on the Almsgiving of Worldly Robbers*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on Brahmā’s Visit to the Brahmin Lecture Hall*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Five Types of Combatants*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Yúqiā Jūshì Jiàn Fó Wén Fǎ Tíwù jīng* (also titled *Xiūjiātóu Jūshì Fó Wèi Shuō Fǎ Dé Xǐngwù jīng*), translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Samajie jīng* (also known as the *Xumoti nü jīng*, the *Nán guówáng jīng*, or the *Shuhétán wáng jīng*). The *Bǎochàng lù* states: "One fascicle of the *Sāmájì jīng*, eight pages; translated in the Wu dynasty by Zhū Lùtóuyán at Yángdū."
*Yingyao liejing* (The Scripture on Hawks and Falcons for Hunting), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu state during the Huangwu era.
Found in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Great Withered Tree* (1 fascicle), also known as *The Scripture on the Withered Tree* or *The Scripture on the Burning of a Pile of Wood*. Three sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Chīniǎo shì jīng* (The Scripture on the Owl Bird), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Sūmótí nǚ jīng* (The Scripture of the Girl Sumati), one fascicle, seven sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Huangwu era of the Wu dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Meditation on Impurity*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the Wu period.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Qībǎo jīng* (Sūtra on the Seven Jewels), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Lìshì yishān jīng* (Sūtra of the Malla Moving the Mountain), one fascicle; also known as *Yishān jīng*, five sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
The *Catvāry-āścaryādbhuta-dharma-sūtra*,
one fascicle (three sheets), translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin, appears in the *Chángfáng nèidiǎnlù* (Catalogue of Buddhist Texts by Sengzhao).
It is recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Householder Vīrasena’s Enjoyment of the Five Desires*, one fascicle.
The above was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
according to Dao’an, it appears in the *Chángfáng Lù* and the *Sēngyòu Lù*.
*Vaiḍūryarāja-sūtra*, one fascicle, six sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin at the Qing Gate in Chang’an.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.
*Aṅgulimālya-sūtra*, one fascicle, also known as the *Aṅgulimālīya-sūtra*, five sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Aṅgulimālīya-sūtra*, the second translation, which is said to be a different translation of the same original text as the *Fǎhù Yǐnmàn* (Dharmarakṣa’s Fingernail Garland). Translated by Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù.
*Ekottarika-āgama-sūtra*, one fascicle, three sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthita during the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù.
*Qun niu pi jing* (Sutra on the Parable of the Herd of Cows), one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Jīmù shāorán jīng* (Sutra on the Burning of a Heap of Wood), one fascicle. Essentially the same as the *Kūshù jīng* (Sutra on the Withered Tree) with minor differences. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bōsìníwáng yì Fówǒyǒuwēiyí jīng* (The Sūtra on King Prasenajit’s Five Modes of Reverence Visiting the Buddha), translated by Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Sutra on King Prasenajit’s Mourning for His Mother*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Sutra on King Prasenajit’s Mother Passing Away and Her Body Being Covered in Dust*, one fascicle, one sheet. Translated by Zhu Faju and Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra of the Simile of the Flying Bird*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Son of a Good Man*, second fascicle. Translated by Zhī Fǎdù of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Tiān yú xiūluó yù dòuzhàn jīng* (Sūtra on Heaven and Asura Intending to Fight), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Confused Minds of Learners*, one fascicle. Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra of King Puṣyanī’s Ten Dreams*, also titled the *Sūtra of the King’s Seven Dreams*, consisting of five sheets. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Zhìfáng).

One fascicle of the *Sānshísāntiān Yuánguān jīng* (Sūtra on the Gardens and Pavilions of the Thirty-three Heavens). Translated by the śramaṇa Zhú Tánwúlán at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Wéi-gé zhǎngzhě liù xiàng bài jīng* (The Scripture on the Venerable Wéi-gé’s Sixfold Prostrations), also written as *Wéihuā*. Translated by Qíduōmì of the Eastern Jin.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Angulimālīya-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Aṅguli-keśa-sūtra*. Translated by Qiduomi of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Liùxiàngbài jīng* (Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostrations), one fascicle. The *Chángfáng lù* states it is the third translation of the *Weigé liùxiàngbài jīng*. Translated by the layman Zhú Nántí at Guangzhou during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*Fó kāi jiě fànzhì fán jīng* (The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Explanation for the Brahmin Bhadra), one fascicle. Translated by the Eastern Jin monk Shi Fayong.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Gopālaka-sūtra*, one fascicle, five sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva at the Xiāoyáo Garden in Cháng'ān during the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Tóngjiāshè jiě nán jīng* (The Sūtra on Kaśyapa the Younger Resolving Difficulties), one fascicle. Second appearance; same text as the *Kaśyapa-sūtra* translated by Kumārajīva, though translated separately. Translated by the śramaṇa Fǎjiān during the reign of Qífú [Yǔchén] of the Xīqín dynasty.
*The Scripture on King Prasenajit’s Mourning for His Mother*, one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang, during the Northern Liang dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Mahāprajāpatī-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Buddhamātṛ-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*, four sheets. Translated by Jing Sheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Juqu clan, in the capital Yangdu during the Song dynasty. Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

*The Story of the People of Śrāvastī Who Went Mad after Losing Their Son*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra of the Brahmin Who Lost His Daughter*. Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn during the reign of Emperor Wŭ of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*. One fascicle:
the *Er yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on Two Causes and Conditions). Translated by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Scripture on the Confused Minds of Learners* (one fascicle), also known as *The Scripture on the Confused Minds of a Mother and Son Becoming Bhikṣus and Bhikṣuṇīs* (two sheets). Translated by the Sòng dynasty śramaṇa Huìjiǎn.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Huijiao).

One fascicle of the *Shànshēng nánzǐ jīng* (Sūtra on the Birth of a Virtuous Son), also known as the *Yìchū liùxiàngbài jīng* (Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostration of a Different Translation). Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the monk Huìjiǎn at Lùnyè Temple.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Hǎi bādé jīng* (Sūtra on the Eight Virtues of the Sea); the *Dámó lù* states it is three pages long and was translated together with the *Zhānpó bǐqǔ* (Bhikṣu Campaka). Right: Translated during the Qin dynasty by Kumārajīva; recorded in the *Dáduōluó lù*.

*Fahai zang jing* (Sutra on the Dharma-Treasury), one fascicle. Recorded by Dharmarakṣa as being the same length as the *Haidede jing* (Sutra on the Eight Virtues of the Sea), totaling four sheets. Translated during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Han dynasty by the śramaṇa Zhu Falan.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Fǎhǎi jīng* (Dharma Ocean Sūtra). Translated during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty by Fǎjù and Fǎlì together.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Seven Practices with Immediate Retribution*, one fascicle; from the thirtieth volume, one page. *The Sūtra on Devadatta Entering Hell*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra on King Prasenajit’s Admonition that Desire is Not the Ultimate Joy*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra on Sweeping the Ground*, one fascicle; recorded in the *Sengyou lu*. *The Sūtra on the People of Rājagṛha Inviting the Buddha*, one fascicle; recorded in the *Sengyou lu*. *The Sūtra on the Four Great Nirayas*, one fascicle; alternatively, without the character "da" (great). *The Sūtra on Receiving Five Meritorious Rewards for Bestowing Food*, one fascicle; also titled *The Sūtra on Merit* or *The Sūtra on Bestowing Physical Strength and Beauty*, three pages. *The Sūtra on the Appearance of the Four Persons in the World*, one fascicle.
