*The Sūtra of the Lesser Parinirvāṇa*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Inquiry Concerning the Buddhas of Future Ages*, one fascicle; also titled simply *The Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Inquiry*. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Wúwèi Líchē Bǎi Ānán jīng* (The Sūtra on Vīra Licchavi Addressing Ānanda), appearing in the twenty-first volume; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.

*Jingqin Siniànchù Jīng* (The Scripture on Diligent Practice of the Four Foundations of Mindfulness), one fascicle. Found in the second volume of the *Chángfáng Lù*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Found in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Shìjiān yán měisè jīng* (Sūtra on the World’s Beautiful Colors), one fascicle; extracted from the twenty-fourth fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty. Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Yīqiè xíng bùhéng ānzhù jīng* (Sūtra on All Phenomena Not Abiding Constantly), one fascicle; extracted from the thirty-fourth fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Xiànglèi jīng* (Sūtra on Similitudes), spoken by the Buddha for the Brahmin Bindu; extracted from the eleventh fascicle. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Buddha Preaching the Dharma for the Village Head of the Horse-Taming Settlement*, one fascicle; found in the thirty-second volume. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fó wèi shìhuǒ póluómén shuō chūjiā fǎ wùdào jīng* (Sutra on the Dharma of Leaving Home and Awakening to the Way Spoken by the Buddha for a Fire-Worshipping Brahmin). Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
*The Brahmin’s Deceptive Sūtra*, one fascicle. Found in the thirtieth volume on the right; translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Transformation of Fire and the Renunciation of a Brahmin*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Renunciation and Attainment of the Way by the Cāṭaka Brahmin*, one fascicle. Appears in fascicle forty-three. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*The Sūtra of Verses Spoken by the Buddha for the Arrogant Brahmin*, one fascicle. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Brahmin’s White-Robed Sūtra*, one fascicle; excerpted from the twenty-eighth fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han; recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Sūtra on Plowing the Field Spoken by the Buddha for a Brahmin*, one fascicle (the character "field" may be omitted). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Báluómén tōngdá jīnglùn jīng* (Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Mastery of the Sūtras and Śāstras), volume twenty-five; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*The Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Understanding of Various Arts*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Four Dharmas Spoken by the Buddha for a Brahmin*, one fascicle; extracted from the second fascicle. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao. Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on Maudgalyāyana Seeing Sentient Beings Whose Body Hair is Like Arrows*, one fascicle; extracted from the nineteenth fascicle. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng):

*Guòqù tánqín rén jīng* (Sūtra on the Man Who Played the Lute in a Past Life), one fascicle; from the forty-eighth fascicle. *Ānàlǜ sīwéi mùlián shénlì jīng* (Sūtra on Āniruddha’s Contemplation and Maudgalyāyana’s Supernatural Powers), one fascicle; from the nineteenth fascicle. The above were translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
*The Sūtra of the Śrāmaṇera Cunda*, one fascicle. Found in the twenty-fourth volume; translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Ekadhanika-gṛhapati-sūtra*, one fascicle, appearing in the thirty-sixth volume; also known as the *Ekadhanika-gṛhapati-dravyānarpita-sūtra* or the *Anapatya-pariṇāmana-sūtra*. Translated during the Later Han dynasty by An Shigao.
*The Scripture on the Merchant Escaping the Peril of Bandits*, one fascicle. Found in the twenty-second fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Found in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Sūtra on the Renunciation of Heretics*, one fascicle; appears in the twenty-seventh fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Record (*Chángfáng lù*).
*The Sūtra on the Brahmin Asking the Buddha about Receiving Merit through Almsgiving*, one fascicle; appears in the thirty-seventh fascicle. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Dòuzhē póluómén lúnyì chūjiā jīng* (Sūtra on the Brahmin Dòuzhē’s Debate and Renunciation of the Home Life), found in the forty-second fascicle; translated by Ān Shìgāo during the Later Han dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle titled *The Scripture on the Eight States of Horses* (*Mǎ yǒu bā tài jīng*), also known as *The Scripture on the Eight Vicious States of Horses* (*Mǎ yǒu bā bì è tài jīng*), or alternatively *The Scripture on the Eight States of Horses Compared to Humans* (*Mǎ yǒu bā tài pì rén jīng*). Two sheets. Translated by Zhīyào during the Later Han dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Three Marks of Horses*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Zhi Yao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Hezhong Caogui jing* (The Scripture of the Turtle in the River Grass), one fascicle; extracted from the forty-third fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty]. Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Buzi shouyi jing* (The Scripture on Not Guarding One’s Intentions), one fascicle, one sheet; also titled *Zishou jing* (Scripture on Self-Guarding) or *Zishouyi jing* (Scripture on Self-Guarding Intentions). Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty].
*Wumuzi jing* (Sutra on the Mother and Son), one fascicle. Compiled from the second volume of the *Changfang lu*. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Compiled from the *Changfang lu*.
*Catuḥśubhāśvavyākaraṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle; extracted from the thirty-third fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. *Sarvāsravakṣaya-sūtra*, one fascicle; extracted from the tenth fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
*Shòumìng cù jīng* (Sūtra on the Shortening of Life), one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of Wu.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Impermanence of Form*, one fascicle; extracted from the tenth fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra on the Three Kinds of Excellent Horses*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.

*The Scripture on the Five Dharmas by Which a King Accomplishes Long Endurance in the World*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Wu Kingdom in the Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Snowy Mountain Monkey*, one fascicle; appears in the twenty-fourth fascicle. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu [Dynasty]. Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Sūtra of the Illness of the Longevity Youth Seeing the World-Honored One*, one fascicle; appears in the forty-seventh fascicle. Dao’an states it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin Dynasty.
I have seen this in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.
One fascicle of the *Licchavi-apramāda-sūtra*, appearing in the forty-seventh volume; Dao’an states that it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
I have seen this in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

One scroll of the *Fojing yu biqiu youposai qiren youxing yu waidao shuofa jing* (The Scripture on the Buddha’s Traveling with Bhikṣus, Upāsakas, and Begging Monks, Encountering the Preaching of Heretics), translated during the Western Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu; it appears in the thirty-second fascicle. Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin period; I have seen this in Sengyou’s record.

*The Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of the Tīrthika’s Progression and Questioning the Buddha Regarding Rebirth in the Tuṣita Heaven*, one fascicle; included in the thirty-second fascicle. According to the *Sengyou Lu*, it was translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.

*The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions for Rebirth in Heaven through Battle, as Asked by Non-Buddhists* (1 fascicle), appearing in the thirty-second volume. The aforementioned record by Sengyou states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin.
*Catuṣpuruṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Siviridevaputra-bhagavatsūtra-gāthā*, one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Āyuwáng huòguǒbào jīng* (Sūtra on King Aśoka Receiving Karmic Retribution). Right: Sengyou’s catalogue records that this was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty;
Dao’an also noted this.
*The Scripture on the Man Who Struck the Drum in the Past*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalog.
*The Scripture on King Aśoka Producing Great Reverence and Faith Toward the Buddha*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
I have seen this in Sengyou’s *Lù* (Catalogue).
One fascicle of the *Yīwáng jīng* (Sūtra of the King of Physicians) appears in the fifteenth volume; it was translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin and is recorded in Changfang’s catalogue.
*The Scripture on the Immortal’s Account of the Asuras’ Submission*, one fascicle. Found in the thirty-ninth volume. Dao’an states that it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin period;
this is recorded in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*The Buddha’s Discourse in Verse for an Old Brahmin*, one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it is recorded in Sengyou’s catalogue.
*Sūtra on the Seal of the Holy Dharma*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa in the fourth year of the Yuankang era of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Aśokarāja-pradāna-ardhāmala-phala-sūtra*. Regarding this, Dao’an states it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin period;
it appears in the *Sēngyòu lù*.
*Abhedyaprasāda-sūtra*, one fascicle. The above was translated by Zhu Fahu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin, according to Dao’an;
it appears in Sengyou’s *Lu*.
*Sattrayaskandha-sūtra*, one fascicle. The above was translated by Zhu Fahu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin, according to Dao’an.
*Jian sengyou lu*.
*Dishi li sanbao gongyang jing*, one fascicle. Right: Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Seen in the *Sengyou lu*.
*Shen guan jing* (Sūtra on Contemplating the Body), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*San xing jing* (Sūtra on the Three Practices), one fascicle. Appears in the twenty-first volume. Dao’an states it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
I have seen this in Sengyou’s *Chū sānzàng jìlù*.

It is titled *The Scripture on the Demon Assuming an Impure Form to Disturb with Lust*, one fascicle; it appears in the forty-ninth volume. Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Western Jin dynasty.
Seen in the *Sengyou lu*.

"The Two Boys See [the Buddha]" and "The Sutra on the Buddha’s Verses for Offering" in one fascicle; these appear in the twenty-third fascicle. Translated by Baifazhu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bhikṣu yú sè yànlí jīng* (The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu’s Loathing and Detachment from Form), appearing in the twenty-sixth volume; translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Śejū shìwù jīng* (Sutra on Abandoning All Worldly Affairs), Volume 26. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Yīng’ér pì jīng* (The Scripture of the Simile of the Infant); the *Chángfáng lù* states that the *Yīng’ér yù jīng* (The Scripture of the Parable of the Infant) appears in the twenty-sixth fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Héngshuǐ liúzhu jīng* (also titled *Fú mù pìyù jīng*), found in the forty-third fascicle; translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Huīhé jīng* (Sūtra of the Ash River), found in the forty-third fascicle; translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Chenhuīhé pìyù jīng* (The Sūtra of Similes of the River of Dust and Ash), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Faju and Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sutra on the Death of King Prasenajit’s Grandmother*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Faju and Falu of the Western Jin dynasty; appears in the forty-sixth fascicle [of the *Taishō Tripiṭaka*] and is listed in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Parable of Casting Gold*, one fascicle; appears in the forty-seventh fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthita during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Seven Jewels of the Cakravartin King Appearing in the World*, one fascicle; appears in the twenty-seventh fascicle. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthita during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xiàngxié fǎbiàn jīng* (Sutra on the Deviation from the Dharma through Tending toward the Evil), found in the twenty-eighth fascicle; translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appearing in the *Chángfáng lù* (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Tiānfú yù jīng* (Sūtra of the Parable of the Farmer), appearing in the twenty-ninth volume; translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xìn rén zhě shēng wǔ zhǒng guòhàn jīng* (Sūtra on the Five Kinds of Calamities for Those Who Believe); the *Huàdù sì lù* states it is from the fourth fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhú Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.

*Shāoduò zhìjì jīng* (Sūtra on the Minor and Major Precepts), one fascicle; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhú Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty; recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*, volume forty-three.
*The Sūtra on a Bhikṣu Attempting Suicide to Avoid a Woman’s Ill Repute*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Zhu Faju and Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the Changfang Record.

*The Sūtra of the Simile of the Wooden Pestle*, one fascicle; extracted from the forty-seventh fascicle [of the *Dīrgha Āgama*]. Translated by Zhu Faju together with Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Jinshi jingshe zunzhe bing jing* (The Sutra on the Illness of Venerable Jinshi Jing-she), one fascicle; extracted from the forty-seventh fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Daughter of King Prasenajit Passing Away and Visiting the Buddha*. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Āyuṣmān Ghoṭīka Ekākivihārasūtra*, appearing in the thirty-ninth volume; translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appearing in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Rénmín jíyì shòu sānguī jīng* (Sūtra on People Afflicted by Epidemics Receiving the Three Refuges). Appears in the thirty-ninth fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Buddha Preaches the Sūtra on Extremely Deep and Precipitous Places for Bhikṣus*, found in the sixteenth volume; translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Faju together with Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Yángqún yù jīng* (The Scripture of the Parable of the Flock of Sheep), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Faju together with Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Sūtra of the Simile of the Bhikṣu Kṣema on Serious Illness*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*Pushi jing* (Sutra on Universal Giving), one fascicle; excerpted from the fourth fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Faju together with Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Buddha’s Discourse on the Sūtra of Great Power for Bhikṣus*, one fascicle; extracted from the eleventh fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Arising of Disgust for the Four Great Elements and the Physical Body*, one fascicle; extracted from the twelfth fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty by the śramaṇas Zhú Fǎjù and Fǎlì.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Buddha Speaks the Sūtra on the Three Dharmas for Bhikṣus* (Fó wèi bǐqiū shuō sānfǎ jīng). Found in the fourteenth fascicle [of the *Zhōngāhán jīng*]. Translated during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin by the śramaṇa Zhú Fǎjù together with Fǎlì.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Xiāngyìng xiāngkě jīng* (Sūtra on Corresponding Compatibility). Translated by the śramaṇas Fǎjù and Fǎlì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yan sexiang ji jing* (Sūtra on the Eye and Form Being Bound Together), one fascicle; extracted from the twenty-first fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Dharmakṣema and Fali during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on the Parable of Burning the Head Spoken by the Buddha for the Bhikṣus*, one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa together with Fali.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Shujing* (Numerical Sūtra), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
*Chuzhong xingdao jing* (Sūtra on Practicing the Path in the Middle Way), one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Udāyin-āsana-vṛkṣa-śānti-damana-sūtra*, also titled *Upāsikā*; it is the ninth fascicle in the aforementioned collection. Translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Fali during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Buddha Preaches the Sūtra on Not Contemplating Worldly Contemplations for the Bhikṣus* (also titled *The Sūtra on Not Contemplating the World*), volume sixteen; translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Faju together with Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Wúshǐ běnjì jīng* (Sūtra on the Beginningless Fundamental Limit), appearing as the thirty-fourth volume on the right; translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Fajū together with Fālì during the reign of Emperor Huì of the Western Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Yèyù duōshǎo jīng* (Sūtra on the Many Leaves as a Simile), Volume 15. Translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Faju together with Falì during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Yìxìn yìyù jīng* (Sūtra on Different Faiths and Different Desires), appearing in the fourteenth volume; translated by the śramaṇas Zhu Faju and Fali during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
*The Scripture on the Rāva-bird Seized by a Hawk*, one fascicle. Found in the twenty-fourth fascicle [of the *Kaiyuan Shijiao Lu*]. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin.
Found in the *Changfang Lu*.
*Śīlasaṃprayuktaka-sūtra*, one fascicle; also titled *Śīlasaṃprayukta-sūtra*. Two sheets. Translated by Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Jièdéxiāng jīng* (Sūtra on the Fragrance of Moral Virtue), one fascicle; also known as *Jièdé jīng* (Sūtra on Moral Virtue). Two sheets. Translated by Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Sūtra on Listening to the Bestowal of Alms* (one fascicle), also known as *The Sūtra on Listening to the Bestowal of Alms to Bhikṣus* (three sheets). Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on Śakra Devānām-indra Visiting Maudgalyāyana and Emitting Light*, one fascicle; translated during the Eastern Jin dynasty by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu. (Appears in Volume 19.)
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Quànhángxíngyǒuzhèngjīng* (Sūtra on Encouraging Practice with Verified Accounts). Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xiè Zhènxi Sī in Yángdū during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zhòngshēng Tǐng Yǒu Tiěmò Shènghuǒ Chìrán Jīng* (The Sutra on the Iron Grindstone with Blazing Fire upon the Crowns of Sentient Beings). Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Translated at Xi Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

One fascicle: *The Scripture on a Sentient Being Whose Entire Body Is Coated with Excrement*. The *Huadu lu* states that its alternative title is *The Scripture on the Impurities of a Sentient Being’s Body*, and it appears in the nineteenth volume. It was translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Translated at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu.
Appears in the Changfang lu (Catalogue of Changfang).

*The Sūtra of Maudgalyāyana Seeing a Great-Bodied Being with His Body Bound by Burning Iron*, one fascicle; appears in the nineteenth volume. Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin by Zhu Tanwulan.
Translated at Yangdu;
listed in the Chángfáng lù.
*Sūtra on the Four Heavenly Kings Inspecting the World*, one fascicle. [Compiled] during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin by Zhu Tanwulan.
Translated at Xi Zhenxi Temple in Yangdu.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bhikṣu Wèn Fó Shìtíhuánīn Jīng* (Sūtra on the Bhikṣu Questioning the Buddha Regarding Śakra Devendra). Appears in the fortieth fascicle. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin, translated by the Central Asian śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan.
Translated at Yangdu;
recorded in the Chángfáng Lù.
*Aśokarāja-pūjita-bodhivṛkṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Tiāndìshì shòu jiè jīng* (Sūtra on the Ordination of Śakra Devendra). Found in the fortieth fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fó jiàn fàntiān dǐng jīng* (The Sūtra on the Buddha Beholding the Crown of the Brahmā Heaven), one fascicle; extracted from the forty-fourth volume. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Dìshī cíxīn zhànshèng jīng* (Sūtra on Śakra’s Compassionate Heart and Victory), found in the forty-sixth fascicle; translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin.
*Shehang fajing* (Sūtra on the Dharma of Serpent-Walking), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmaruci during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Sūtra on Being Drifted by Water Froth*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra on the Great Mass of Froth in a River* or *The Simile of the Mass of Froth*. Extracted from the tenth fascicle. Compiled during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty by the śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan.
Translated at Xi Zhenxi Temple in Yangzhou. Appears in the Changfang lu (Record of Changfang).
One fascicle: *The Sutra on the Ten Dharmas Accomplishing Evil Karma and Entering Hell*. Found in Volume 37. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Fójiàn mùniǔ zhě shìdào jīng* (Sūtra on the Buddha Showing the Way to a Cowherd), found in the thirty-eighth fascicle; one fascicle of the *Bǐqiū yù yùtiānzǐ fàngguāng jīng* (Sūtra on a Bhikṣu Bathing and Encountering a Devaputra Emitting Light), found in the thirty-eighth fascicle. Both were translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Buddha Speaks the Sūtra on the Great Heat Hell* for Bhikṣus; found in the sixteenth fascicle. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).
One fascicle of the *Śāriputra-ādibhikṣu-pratilabdha-kāyāsākṣātkriyā-sūtra*. Found in the eighteenth fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
*Ekādaśa-rūpa-tathāgata-anusmṛti-sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Yichu qichu sanguan jing* (Sūtra on the Seven Stations and Three Contemplations in Different Places), one fascicle. Translated by Guṇabhadra at Qihuan Temple in Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Appearance of Four Persons in the World*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Scripture of Brahmā’s Star*, one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of Northern Liang, during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
*Shengsi bian shi jing* (Sūtra on the Transformation of Consciousness at Birth and Death), one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng in Guzang during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Śākya Clan Questioning the Upāsaka*, one fascicle; extracted from the thirty-third fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Dàlìshī chūjiā dédào jīng* (Sutra on the Great Strongman Leaving Home and Attaining the Way), also titled the *Lìshì bātuo jīng* (Sutra of the Strongman Bhadra). Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Shi Huìjiǎn.
Extracted from the Chángfáng Lù (Record of Chángfáng).

One fascicle of the *Ér lǎo nán nǚ jiàn fó chūjiā dédào jīng* (Sutra on Two Elders, Male and Female, Seeing the Buddha, Leaving Home, and Attaining the Way), found in the thirty-second fascicle; translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-bhikṣu-sūtra* (after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa), also titled the *Lìshì-báduō-jīng* (Sūtra of the Malla Bhadra). Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn during the reign of Emperor Wŭ of the Song dynasty.
*Piyū jīng* (Sūtra of Parables), one fascicle;
extracted from the fifth fascicle of the *Chángfáng lù*. Translated by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn during the reign of Emperor Xiàowŭ of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Ash River Scroll*, one fascicle; extracted from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*. Translated by the Śramaṇa Shi Fadu during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Southern Qi dynasty.

Recorded in the *Changfang Lu*. *Sutra on the Deva Wishing to Battle with the Asura*, one fascicle; extracted from the fortieth fascicle. *Sutra on the Demon Transforming into a Youth to Approach the Buddha and Recite Verses*, one fascicle; extracted from the twentieth fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Elder Citta Inviting Bhikṣus*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Elder’s Death and Rebirth in the Avṛha Heaven*, one fascicle, both from the twenty-first fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Brāhmaṇa Avoiding Death*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Elder’s Death and Rebirth in Tuṣita Heaven*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Praising Hell*, one fascicle;

*The Sūtra on the World-Honored One’s Mindfulness*, one fascicle, both from the twenty-second fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Accumulation of Bones*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Four Snakes*, one fascicle—also known as the *Sūtra of the Simile of the Four Vipers*—[all] from [the twenty-second fascicle].
Volume Forty-three: The *Saṃyukta Āgama*, Chapter Thirty, one fascicle; the *Saṃyukta Āgama*, one fascicle (twenty-one pages); the *Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra Sūtra*, one fascicle;

the *Sūtra on the Buddha’s Stay in the Kingdom of Kośala*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Buddha’s Stay in the Kingdom of Udumbara*, one fascicle; the *Sūtra on the Self-Restraint of Brahmā at That Time*, one fascicle; the *Bha*... [text fragment].

*The Brāhmaṇa Who Does Not Believe in the Sūtras*, one fascicle; *The Buddha’s Discourse to Śaradvat*, one fascicle; *The Discourse on a Person Speaking of His Own Bones Not Knowing They Are Rotting*, one fascicle.
The preceding one hundred and seventy-four sūtras are all extracted from the *Saṃyukta Āgama*.

The *Separate Translation of the Saṃyukta Āgama*, one fascicle, twenty scrolls, three hundred and seventy-nine pages; and the *Sūtra on the Twelve Wanderings*, one fascicle, five pages. The above were translated by the śramaṇa Jiang Lianglou at Guangzhou during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin dynasty.
*Chū hōshōroku*. One fascicle, five sheets of paper. Translated by the śramaṇa Kālodaka during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Scripture on the Twelve Wanderings*, one fascicle. Translated during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Guṇabhadra.
It appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
These three preceding scriptures are different translations of the same original text.

*Xiuxing daodi jing* (Sutra on the Stages of Cultivating the Path), one volume in seven or six fascicles, totaling one hundred and thirty-six pages. Translated by the śramaṇa An Shigao in the first year of the Yongkang era of the Later Han dynasty.

*Ren shou shen ru yin jing* (Sūtra on People Receiving Bodies and Entering the Skandhas), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty. Found in the first fascicle of the *Changfang lu*.
Source: *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on the Four Hundred and Four Diseases of the Human Body*, one fascicle. Appears in the first fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty. Appears in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Scripture on Human Disease That Physicians Cannot Cure*, one fascicle; also titled *The Scripture on Human Disease That Physicians Cannot Cure Themselves*. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.

*Diye zhui ren zhong ku shi jing* (Sutra on the Various Sufferings of the Sinners in Hell), one fascicle; appears in the third fascicle [of the *Chu sanzang jiji*]. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*Wǔyīnchéngbài jīng* (Sūtra on the Formation and Dissolution of the Five Aggregates), one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Xiūxíng jīng* (Sūtra on Cultivation), one work in seven fascicles. This second translation differs slightly from that translated by An Shigao. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin in the fifth year of the Tàikāng era.
*Chūjiángfǎlù* (Record of Zhǎngfáng).
*Xiūxíngcíjīng* (Sutra on the Practice of Loving-Kindness), one fascicle. Translated by Zhīqián during the Wu dynasty.
From the *Chūjiángfǎlù*.
*Jue kongbu pin jing* (Sūtra on Eliminating Fear), one fascicle. Dao’an states that this was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty;
it appears in Sengyou’s catalogue.

*Xiuxing quan yi jing* (Sūtra on Cultivating and Exhorting the Mind), one fascicle. An excerpt from the *Madhyama Āgama*. Dao’an states that this was produced by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
I have seen this in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.

The *Ren shen ba shi zhong chong jing* (Sūtra on the Eighty Kinds of Worms in the Human Body), one fascicle, appears in the first volume; Dao’an states it was translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.

According to Sengyou’s Catalogue (*Chu sanzang jiji*), there is one fascicle of the *Xiaoshi jing* (Sutra on Morning Meals), which is extracted from the *Xiuxing daodi jing* (Treatise on the Stages of Cultivating the Path). It was translated by the śramaṇa Zhu Faju together with Falu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Diyù zhòngshēng xiānghài jīng* (Sūtra on the Mutual Harm among Beings in Hell). The *Bǎochàng lù* states that the *Diyù xiānghài jīng* appears in the third fascicle; it was translated by Zhu Tanwulan during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Translated at Xi Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu; recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

One fascicle of the *Huanyue pin jing* (Sūtra on the Chapter of Joy) appears before the fourteenth sūtra in the fourth fascicle; it is also found in the *Xiuxing daodi jing* (Treatise on the Stages of Practice).
*The Scripture on Bathing the Assembly of Monks in a Warm Chamber*, one fascicle. First appearance: translated by An Shigao of the Later Han.
*The Scripture on Bathing the Assembly of Monks in a Warm Chamber*, one fascicle, four sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa of the Western Jin.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
The two scriptures above are different translations of the same original text.
*Yùjié jīng*, one fascicle, four pages; also titled *Zhǎngzhě yì fó shuō zǐfù wújìng jīng* or *Qīfù jīng*. Translated by Dharmaruci during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Translated at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu;
recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*Āsujāta-sūtra*, one fascicle, two sheets. Translated by Guṇabhadra during the era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
The above two sūtras are recorded in the *Chángfáng lù* as being translations of the same original text with different versions.

There is also a separate version of the *Ullambana Sūtra* in one fascicle and three pages, which states it is five pages long and is titled the *Jìngtǔ Ullambana Sūtra*; its provenance is unknown. It was translated during the Jin dynasty by Dharmarakṣa.
Extracted from the Catalogue of Changfang.

*Guānlà jīng* (The Sūtra on the Offering of Incense), one fascicle, two sheets; also titled *Bānníhuán hòu sìbèi guānlà jīng* (The Sūtra on the Offering of Incense by the Four Classes after the Parinirvāṇa). Translated during the Jin dynasty by Zhu Fahu.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Bǎo'ēn fèngpén jīng* (Sūtra on Repaying Kindness by Offering the Bowl), one fascicle, two sheets; the three sūtras above share the same original text and have been re-translated.
*Ānán huò jīng* (Sūtra on Ānanda’s Confusion), one fascicle; extracted from the *Rénběn yùshēng jīng* (Sūtra on the Origin of Human Desire). Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
*Ren shou cong lai jing* (Sutra on Where People Come From), one fascicle. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Āraṇyaka-cīvaradhāraṇa-dhyāna-dharma-sūtra*, one fascicle; extracted from the first fascicle of the *Bodhisattva-cīvaradhāraṇa-dhyāna-dharma*. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Āraṇyaka-cīnadharmaparyāya-sūtra*, in two rolls (or omitting the word "sūtra"), consisting of fifty-two sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva at Cháng'ān during the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zuòchán sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Seated Meditation), in three or two fascicles, totaling fifty-six sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva in Cháng'ān during the Later Qín dynasty.
From the Record of Changfang:
*The Āraṇyaka Śikṣā Sūtra*, one fascicle, two scrolls. Translated by Guṇabhadra at Xinsi Monastery in Jingzhou during the era of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.
The four scriptures above are translations of the same original text.

*Zuifubaoying jing* (Scripture on the Retribution of Sin and Merit), one fascicle; also known as *Fenwuzhi bier baoying jing* (Scripture on the Separate Retributions in Five Sections). Translated during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Song dynasty by Guṇabhadra.
Translated at the New Temple in Jingzhou;
recorded in the Changfang Catalogue.
*Karmavibhaṅga-sūtra*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated by Tanfazhi during the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty.
Extracted from the *Lù dìng nèi wài diǎn lù*.
The two aforementioned sūtras are different translations of the same original text.
*Dà zhōu kān dìng zhòng jīng mùlù*, Scroll Nine.
*Da Zhou Kan Ding Zhong Jing Mu Lu*, Scroll Ten, compiled by order of the Empress of the Great Tang by the śramaṇa Mingquan and others at Foshouji Monastery.
Section on Hinayāna Vinaya and Hinayāna Śāstras: One hundred and ninety-four works in one thousand three hundred and forty-one fascicles.

The Vinaya of the Hīnayāna: one hundred and four sections, totaling four hundred and twenty-eight fascicles; the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, one section, fifty-nine fascicles. The above was translated by Puṇyatāra during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Kumārajīva translated the words.
This appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One section of the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, sixty-two fascicles, totaling one thousand six hundred and sixty-five sheets. The above was translated by Vimalākṣa of the Eastern Jin.
It was translated at Shijian Temple in Shouchun in three fascicles.
Together with the previous fifty-nine, these form sixty-two fascicles in total,
as recorded in the Chángfáng Lù.
*Daśabhāṇavāra-bhikṣuṇī-śīla*, one fascicle. Some versions contain characters that differ slightly from those produced by Dharmatrata. Translated by Zhu Fahu of the Western Jin dynasty;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Śāriputra-bhikṣu-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-nine sheets. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu during the sixth year of the Taikang era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
The *He-seng-chun-tan-mo-chi* (Combined Monastic Pure Dharma-holding) by Zhu Sengshu consists of three families [of texts] compiled together into one fascicle;
it appears in the *Changfang-lu*.

The *Vini-sung* (Recitation of the Vinaya), one work in three fascicles, is a portion of the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya* (Ten Recitations); it was translated in Chang’an during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master and Vinaya Master Vimalākṣa from Kaśmīra.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Śāriputra-vinaya-bhikṣu-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, twenty-nine sheets. Translated in Cháng'ān by the Śramaṇa Dharmadhara of the Former Qín, together with Zhu Fóniàn.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Śāriputra-daśabhāṇavāra-bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, thirty-four pages. Translated in Cháng'ān by the Śramaṇa Huìcháng together with Dharmagupta during the Former Qín dynasty.
*The Text for the Two-Year Ordination Platform for Teaching Bhikṣuṇīs*, one fascicle (appears in the *Chángfáng lù*). Translated by Dharmakṣema together with Zhu Fonian during the Former Qin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Shisonglü Shizasa Wen Yibu* (The *Śāriputra-vinaya* Commentary on Miscellaneous Matters, Questioning One Section), two fascicles; translated by Dharmapriya during the Former Qin dynasty.
Appears in the catalogue of Jing Tai.

*Shisong Biquni Jieso Chubenmou* (The *Śāriputra-vinaya*: The Origin and Details of the Bhikṣuṇī Precepts), one fascicle; translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou during the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Shísòng lǜ záshì* (Miscellaneous Matters of the Ten Recitation Vinaya). Translated by the Kasmirian Śramaṇa Dharmayaśas during the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Bǎochàng lù*.

The *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya Bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle; it differs slightly from the version translated by Dharmagupta. The above was translated by Kumārajīva in Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Shísòng sēngní yào shì jīemó* (The Essential Karmavācanā for Monks and Nuns of the Ten Recitations), in two volumes. Translated during the reign of Emperor Fei of the Song dynasty by the Vinaya Master Śramaṇa Sengqu.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya* (Four-Part Vinaya), one section, in forty-five fascicles—or seventy fascicles, or sixty fascicles—totaling one thousand five hundred twenty-eight sheets. Translated at Chang’an during the Hongshi era of the Later Qin dynasty by Buddhayaśas together with Zhu Fonian.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Sifen biqiuseng jieben* (Four-Part Bhikṣu Saṃgha Prātimokṣa), twenty-seven sheets. Translated by Buddhayaśas in Cháng'ān during the Later Qin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):
*Dharmaguptaka-karman*, one fascicle, forty-six pages. Translated by Tandi at Luoyang in the first year of the Zhengyuan era of the Former Wei.
Recorded in the *Chūn-ten-roku* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Sifen-jie-mo-jing* (Four-Part Karmavācanā Sūtra), also known as the *Biqiuni-jie-mo* (Bhikṣuṇī Karmavācanā) in fifteen sheets. Translated by Guṇavarman in the eighth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Translated at Jivakārama Monastery in Yangzhou; recorded in the Changfang lu (Catalogue of Changfang).
One fascicle: *The Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa Sūtra of the Dharmaguptaka School*. This was produced by the śramaṇa Sengwei of Lingyao Monastery in the third year of the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty.
*Jian baochang lu*:
*Sifen biquni jiben*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Sengwei of Lingyao Temple in the third year of the Tianjian era [504 CE].
Recorded in the *Baoshang lu*.

The Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya, one collection in forty fascicles, totaling one thousand one hundred and thirty-five pages. Translated by the śramaṇa Buddhabhadra together with Faxian during the twelfth year of the Yixi era of the Eastern Jin dynasty, under Emperor An.
Translated at Yangdu and Mount Lu; included in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Master Chángfáng).
One fascicle of the *Mahāsāṃghika-śīla-sūtra* (Sengqí jièběn), first translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakāla at the Bǎimǎ Temple during the Jiāpíng era of the Former Wèi.
From the Record of Changfang:
*Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇī Karmavācanā*, one fascicle. Translated by the śramaṇa Buddhayaśas at Daochang Monastery during the Yixi era of the Eastern Jin dynasty; recorded in the Record of Changfang.

The *Mahāsāṃghika-bhikṣu-śīla-mūla*, one fascicle; the second translation, twenty sheets. Translated during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty, in the twelfth year of the Yixi era (416 CE), by the śramaṇa Buddhabhadra.
Translated at Yangdu and Mount Lu;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle: the *Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra*. This second edition differs slightly from that translated by Kākalī during the Wei dynasty. It was translated by Faxian together with Juqu Jingsheng during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Mishāsē wǔfēn lǜ* (The Five-Part Vinaya of the Mahīśāsaka), one work in thirty-four fascicles, totaling six hundred and ninety-four sheets. To the right [of this entry], in the first year of the Jǐngpíng era of the Song dynasty (423 CE), the śramaṇa Buddhayaśas, together with Zhú Dàoshēng, Zhìshèng, and Shì Huìyán, [translated it].
Translated at Longguang Temple in the capital of Yangdu;
recorded in the Changfang lu.

One fascicle of the *Mūlasarvāstivāda Bhikṣu-śīla-sūtra*, also called the *Pañcavargika Śīla-sūtra*, consisting of nineteen sheets. The above was translated by the śramaṇa Buddhayaśas and others in the capital of Yangdu during the Jingping era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Mahīśāsaka-karman*. Translated by the śramaṇa Buddhayaśas and others at the capital of Yang during the Jingping era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.
*The Mūlasarvāstivāda Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa*, one fascicle. The above was produced by the Śramaṇa Mingzheng at Jianchu Monastery during the third year of the Putong era of the Liang dynasty;
it appears in the Baochang lu.
*An Excerpt from the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya*, one fascicle. The above was translated by the Śramaṇa Saṃghavarman of Siṃhala.
*Chū hōshōroku*.
Two fascicles on the combined differences of the two hundred and sixty precepts. Translated by Zhu Falan during the reign of Emperor Ming of the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*Fanjizuibao qingzhong jing* (Sūtra on the Lightness and Heaviness of the Retribution for Violating the Precepts), one fascicle; also known as *Chuifan jing* (Sūtra on Committing Offenses). Two sheets. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Appears in the *Changfang lu*.
*The Scripture on the Three Thousand Dignified Manners of a Great Bhikṣu*, one work in four fascicles (or two fascicles), forty-seven pages. Translated by An Shigao during the Later Han dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*The Gaṅgā River’s Non-Recitation of the Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle. Translated by An Shigao of the Later Han dynasty. Appears in the *Dharmaloka Record* and the *Wangzong Record*.

*The Sūtra on the Five Precepts of the Path’s Foundation*, one fascicle. Appears in the *Changfang Record*. *The Sūtra on Dignified Conduct*, one fascicle. Appears in the *Changfang Record*. *The Sūtra on the Regulation of Robes*, one fascicle. Appears in the *Changfang Record*. *The Sūtra on the Śrāmaṇera’s Departure from Dignified Conduct*, one fascicle. Appears in the *Changfang Record*. *The Sūtra on the Great Precepts*, one fascicle. Appears in the *Changfang Record*. *The Sūtra on the Precepts for Eliminating Calamities*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Sūtra on Subduing and Eliminating Calamities through the Precepts*. Four sheets. Translated by Zhi Qian of the Wu dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dàbǐqū wēiyí jīng* (The Scripture on the Dignified Deportment of Great Bhikṣus), one work in two fascicles.
To the right, Dao’an states that it was translated by Zhu Fahu during the Jin dynasty.
Found in Sengyou’s *Chu sanzang jiji*.
One fascicle of the *Jiejujing* (Sutra on Exhortations to Full Ordination). Translated by the Western Jin śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa;
recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*The Account of Kāśyapa’s Compilation of the Sūtras*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *The Compilation of the Vinaya Sūtra*. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Jiè wáng jīng* (Sūtra on Admonishing the King), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Western Jin dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Jiè luóyún jīng* (Sūtra on Admonishing Rāhula), one fascicle. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Yìjiào fǎlǜ sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Dharma-Regulations of the Bequeathed Teaching), in three or two fascicles. Translated by Dharmakṣema and Dharmasthiti during the Western Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

*The Two-Volume Compilation of Differences in the Three Sections of the Two Hundred and Sixty Precepts*. Translated by Zhu Tanwulan at Xie Zhenxi Temple in the capital of Yangdu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Vinayamātṛkā-śāstra* in eight rolls and one hundred twelve pages. Translated by Fúlán during the Tàishān era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Dámóyùduōluò lù*.
The *Abhidharmahṛdaya-kārikā* in one section, four fascicles, eighty sheets; translated by Saṃghadeva in the first year of the Tàishān era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
It appears in the catalog of Dharmottara.
*The Dharma of Instructing Bhikṣuṇīs*, one fascicle. Translated at Mount Lu by the śramaṇa Gautama Saṃghadeva during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng Lù*.
*Jawen lishi* (Miscellaneous Questions on Vinaya Matters), one work in two fascicles. Translated by Vimalākṣa during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Changfang lu*.

*Jawen lishi* (Miscellaneous Questions on Vinaya Matters), one work in two fascicles. The place of translation differs and the text is distinct from the former; see the *Bielu*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmayaśas in the fourth year of Long’an, during the reign of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
*The Vinaya Sūtra Compiled by Kāśyapa*, one fascicle. Translated by the Eastern Jin monk Shi Sōng.
From the Chángfáng lù.
*The Kāśyapa Prohibition Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as *The Mahābhikṣu Sūtra* or *The Sūtra on Genuine and False Śramaṇas*. Three sheets. Translated by the Eastern Jin monk Shi Tugong.
From the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Bhikṣuṇī-śīla-sūtra*. The above was compiled during the reign of Emperor Jianwen of the Former Qin by the Vinaya Master Huichang, together with Dharmamitra, Zhu Fonian, and others.
Translated in Chang’an;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Vinaya-mātṛkā* (Nèiyè lǜ), one volume, ten fascicles; also known as the *Śīla-hetupratyaya-sūtra*. Translated in Chang’an by Zhu Fonian and others during the Later Qin dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Upāsaka-śīla-sūtra* (Uposatha-śīla-mūla), translated by Dharmakṣema together with Juqu Mengxun during the Northern Liang dynasty.
Recorded in the *Bǎochàng lù*.
*Mahāprajāpatī Bhikṣuṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes. The aforementioned entry in Sengyou’s catalogue states that this is a distinct scripture from the Liang territory.
*Pratimokṣa-sūtra*, one fascicle; twenty-one sheets. Translated by Gautama Prajñāruci during the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Vinaya-vimśati-viniścaya-prakaraṇa-śāstra*, also simply called the *Viniścaya-śāstra*, consisting of twenty-four sheets; translated during the Chen dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha.
*The Treatise on the Bequeathed Teaching*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Saṃghasūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle; the Chen dynasty term for its title is *Zǒngshè* (Compendium). Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Śrāmaṇera-īryāpatha-sūtra*, one fascicle, nineteen sheets. Translated at Yangdu by Guṇavarman of the Song dynasty.

Recorded in the *Chūnēidiǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures). *Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-saṃkṣepa-śāstra*, one fascicle; also known as *Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-lakṣaṇa*. Translated by Guṇavarman at the Jetavana Monastery in the eighth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
*Upāsaka-pañca-śīla-lakṣaṇa*, one fascicle, fifteen sheets. Translated by Guṇavarman during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Baoshang lu*.
*Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-vidhi-sūtra*, one fascicle, twenty-three pages. Translated by Guṇavarman at the Jetavana Monastery in the eighth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
From the *Baochang lu*:
One work in ten fascicles and two hundred forty-four sheets, titled the *Sarvāstivāda-mātṛkā*. Translated by Saṃghavarman at the capital of Yangdu during the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chūnèi Diǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Liùzāi Bājì Jīng* (Sutra on the Six Fasting Days and Eight Precepts). Translated by Guṇabhadra at the capital of Yang during the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Xiánzhě lüyí jīng* (Sūtra on the Vinaya of the Wise), also called the *Wēiyí jīng* (Sūtra on Dignified Conduct). Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of Northern Liang.

*The Scripture on Kāśyapa’s Prohibitions*, one fascicle. The above was translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of the Northern Liang, according to the *Chángfáng Lù*.
It appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

The *Upāsaka-pañcaśīla-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as the *Pañcalakṣaṇa-sūtra*. Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng, Marquis of Anyang of Northern Liang. Recorded in the Chángfáng Lù.

*The Sutra on the True and False Śramaṇas*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sutra of the Mahābhikṣus*, three sheets. Translated during the era of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by the śramaṇa Huìjiǎn at Lùnyè Monastery.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù.

*Juédìng zhūbù píní* (The Decisive Vinaya of All Schools), one work in two fascicles. This was produced in the first year of the Shèngmíng era of the Sòng dynasty by the śramaṇa Dàoyǎn, based upon various vinayas.
I have consulted the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Tāpīlì lǜ* (Mahīśāsaka-vinaya) was translated by the śramaṇa Mahāsaṃghadeva at Zhúlín Monastery in Guǎngzhōu during the reign of Emperor Wŭ of the Qi dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Śāriputra-abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śīla* (Shànjiàn pípóshā lǜ) in eighteen scrolls and four hundred twenty-six pages. The above was compiled by the śramaṇa Śīlasena (Shèngyī) during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Southern Qi dynasty.
Invited the foreign Dharma Master Saṃghabhadra to translate it at Zhulin Monastery in Guangzhou;
it appears in the Changfang Record.
*Vibhāṣā*, one fascicle. The above was translated by the foreign śramaṇa Śīladharma during the Yongming era of the Qi dynasty.
*Chū hōshōroku*. Recorded by the disciple Jīyù:
*Mànjiè jīng* (Sutra on the Precept Against Pride), one fascicle. Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty by Juqu Jingsheng of Northern Liang.
Appears in the *Chángfánglù*.
*The Sūtra on the Dignified Conduct of the Wise*, one fascicle. Translated by Juqu Jingsheng of Northern Liang during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Song dynasty.
Appears in the *Chángfáng Lù*.

*The Record of the Distinction between Sūtras and Vinayas*, one fascicle; *The Vinaya of the Three Vehicles Without Limitation*, one fascicle. These appear in the *Chángfáng Lù* under the four-part Vinaya section.
*The Clarification of Heavy and Light Matters*, one fascicle (recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*). *The Origin and History of the Bhikṣu Precepts*, one fascicle (recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*).
*Commentary on the Various Vinayas*, one fascicle (recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*). *Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa*, one fascicle (recorded in the *Sēngyòu lù*).
*Sīmā-bandha Sūtra*, one fascicle (recorded in the *Sēngyòu lù*). *The Sūtra of Upāli’s Questions to the Buddha*, one fascicle (recorded in the *Sēngyòu lù*).

Some say there is the *Upāli-vinaya* in twenty-three sheets (recorded in Changfang’s catalogue); the *Yingxing lü jīng* (Scripture on the Practice of the Vinaya) in one fascicle and three sheets (Record of Baochang);

the *Bhikṣu zhujìnlǜ* (Various Prohibitions and Vinayas for Bhikṣus) in one fascicle (Record of Sengyou); the *Dàshāmén bāiyī jiémó* (One Hundred and One Karmas of the Great Śramaṇa) in one fascicle and twenty-two sheets (Record of Changfang);
and the *Wùjiè bàoyìng jīng* (Sutra on the Retribution of the Five Precepts) in one fascicle (Record of Baochang).

*The Sūtra on the Precepts Spoken by the Buddha in the Kingdom of Campā*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on Maudgalyāyana’s Questions*, recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue, one fascicle, twenty-seven sheets;

*The Ten Precepts for Śrāmaṇerikās*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Dignified Conduct and Attire of the Five Divisions*, one fascicle—also titled *The Sūtra on the Names and Colors of the Robes of the Monks of the Five Divisions*, recorded in the Bǎochàng Catalogue; *The Sūtra on Miscellaneous Matters of the Worthy One*, one fascicle, recorded in the Sēngyòu Catalogue.
*Jiājīng lüyí jīng* (Sutra on the Lay Precepts), one fascicle; *Chángfáng lù*: *Jiānchuí fǎ* (Methods for the Ritual Gavel), one fascicle; *Chángfáng lù*:

*Chū lüyí yào* (Essentials of the Vinaya Precepts), one work in twenty-two fascicles; *Chángfáng lù*: *Shāmí shíjiè bìng wēiyí* (The Ten Precepts for Śrāmaṇeras and Their Deportment), one fascicle, twenty-one sheets;
*Bǎochàng lù*: *Shāmí líjiè jīng* (Sutra on the Separation from Precepts for Śrāmaṇeras), one fascicle; *Chángfáng lù*: [Works of] Śāriputra.
*Wen jing* (Questions on the Sūtra), one fascicle, eleven sheets; *Chángfáng lù* (Record of Chángfáng) lists this as *Ērbǎiwǔshí jiè* (Two Hundred and Fifty Precepts), one fascicle.
*Yōubósā wúxué lüèlùn* (Abridged Treatise on the Five Trainings for Upāsakas), one work in two fascicles; *Chángfáng lù* lists this.
*Sàpōduō bīní pípóshā* (Sarvāstivāda Vinaya Vibhāṣā), one work in nine fascicles—or eight fascicles, totaling one hundred and ninety-seven sheets; *Chángfáng lù* lists these above.
Aside from the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya*, all others are branches and offshoots of the various Vinayas.

Regarding the Small Vehicle treatises (*Hīnayāna-śāstra*), there are fifty-four works totaling eight hundred and fifty-six fascicles. Among them is the *Abhidharma-aṣṭanavati-saṃyojana-dharma* (one fascicle). The *Chángfáng-lù* states: "The *Abhidharma-aṣṭanavati-saṃyojana-sūtra*, translated by An Shigao of the Later Han."
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle of the *Fēnbié gōngdé lùn*, in five, four, or three fascicles, totaling seventy-two sheets. Translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Western Jin dynasty.
The explanation of the meaning of the *Ekottarika Āgama* appears in the records of Dharmatrāta.
The *Dharmaskandha-śāstra*, one work in two or three fascicles, was translated by Saṃghadeva at Mount Lu during the sixteenth year of the Taiyuan era of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One work in thirteen fascicles, the *Zá āpítán xīn* (Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra). Translated by the śramaṇa Faxian together with Xuangao during the third year of the Long’an era of Emperor An of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
This is the second translation; it is largely identical with slight variations to that produced by Saṃghabhūti under the Former Qin.
From the *Biographies of Eminent Monks* (*Gaoseng zhuan*).
One work in sixteen fascicles, or thirteen fascicles: the *Abhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra*. Translated during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty by the Kasmirian śramaṇa Saṃghadeva.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Abhidharmahṛdaya* (The Heart of Abhidharma), one work in four fascicles. Translated by Saṃghadeva for Master Huiyuan at Mount Lu during the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty.
Extracted from the Record of Changfang.

*The Treatise Compiled by Bhadanta Vasumitra*, one volume in twelve fascicles (or ten fascicles), totaling three hundred and seven sheets. Translated during the nineteenth year of the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin dynasty by Saṃghabhūti together with Buddharakṣa.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One section of the *Abhidharma-vibhāṣā*, in fourteen fascicles or eleven fascicles; Sengyou’s *Lù* states it is the *Saṃyukta-abhidharma-vibhāṣā*, or sometimes contains the character "xīn" (mind). Translated during the Former Qin period by Saṃghabhūti.

The *Abhidharmahṛdaya* (A-pi-tan xin), one fascicle in five rolls, translated during the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin by Saṃghadeva together with Dao’an in Chang’an; it appears in the *Chángfáng lù*. *Note: "Qín yán zhòng xiàn yì" (秦言眾現譯) likely refers to the title or a descriptive note regarding the translation style or provenance.*
Record from the Yishi Shansi Monastery Collection:

*Vibhāṣā-abhidharma-śāstra*, one volume consisting of nineteen fascicles, or fifteen, or fourteen; alternatively called *Vibhāṣā* or *Prapañca*; four hundred and fifty sheets. Translated in Luoyang during the Jianyuan era of the Former Qin by Saṃghadeva.
Extracted from the Chángfáng lù (Record of Chángfáng).
*Sāndharmapravicaya-śāstra* (Three Treatises on the Dharma), one work in two fascicles. Translated in Cháng'ān by Dharmaratna of the Former Qin;
it differs slightly from the version translated by Saṃghadeva.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha* (A-pí-tán bā-gàn-dù), one work in thirty fascicles (or twenty fascicles), also known as the *Kātyāyanīputra-abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha*, totaling four hundred and fifty sheets. Translated during the Jiànyuàn era of the Former Qín by the śramaṇa Saṃghadeva together with Zhú Fóniàn.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One treatise, the *Śāriputrābhidharma*, in thirty fascicles (or twenty, or twenty-two), totaling seven hundred and sixty sheets. Translated in Chang’an during the tenth year of the Hongshi era of the Later Qin by the śramaṇas Dharmagupta and Dharmayaśas.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

The *Tattvasiddhi-śāstra* (Chéngshí lùn), one volume consisting of twenty-four fascicles, or twenty fascicles, or sixteen fascicles, or fourteen fascicles, totaling four hundred and seventy-seven sheets. Translated by Kumārajīva in Cháng'ān during the Later Qín dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-vibhāṣā*, one work in eighty-four fascicles, or ninety-one fascicles, or sixty fascicles, totaling 1,378 sheets. Translated during the Juqú period of the Northern Liáng by Buddhavarman, together with Dàoshēn and others.
Translated at Guzang. Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Master Zhìfǎng).
One fascicle: *Túzǐ dàorén wèn lùn* (The Treatise on the Questions of the Vātsīputrīya Monk). The above was translated by Gautama Prajñāruci during the Xinghe era of the Later Wei dynasty.
Translated at Jinghua Temple in the capital of Ye;
recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Changfang).

*Abhidharma-amṛtarasa* (The Flavor of Ambrosia of Abhidharma), one work in two fascicles; alternatively titled *Amṛtarasa-abhidharma*. Lost translation during the reign of Emperor Qi of the Later Wei dynasty.
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Chángfáng).

*Sārvastivāda-vibhāṣā-śāstra* (Zhòngshìfēn āpítán lùn), one volume in twelve fascicles, totaling two hundred thirty-seven pages. Translated at Yángdū by Guṇabhadra during the reign of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty in the twelfth year of Yuánjiā.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One work in fourteen fascicles, the second translation of the *Zá āpítán pípóshā* (Saṃyuktābhidharmavibhāṣā). Translated by Saṃghavarman at Chánggān Temple during the tenth year of the Yuánjiā era of Emperor Wén of the Song dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zá āpítán xīn* (Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya) in ten scrolls; translated by Saṃghavarman during the third year of the Yuánjiā era of the Song dynasty. The translation was discontinued at the end of the "Selection" (*zhé*) chapter.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Zá āpítán xīn* (Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya), in thirteen or fourteen scrolls, totaling three hundred and twenty-seven pages. Translated by Guṇavarman in the eighth year of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Vimuktimārga-śāstra* (or twelve fascicles), totaling one hundred and ninety-eight sheets. Translated by Saṃghavarman during the Tianjian era of the Liang dynasty, in the fourteenth year.
Translated at the Zhanyun Hall in the capital of Yangdu.
Recorded in the Chángfáng Catalogue.
*Treatise on the Distinction of the Three Times*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha in Guangzhou during the Chengsheng era of the Liang dynasty.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.
*Dharmatrāta-abhidharma-śāstra*, one fascicle, six rolls, one hundred and three pages. Translated by Saṃghavarman and Fazhi during the Tiāntóng era of the Later Qí dynasty.
Furthermore, the Record of Dhamayuttara states that during the Yao Qin period,
it was translated by Zhu Fonian based on the recitation of Saṃghabhūti;
it appears in the Neidian lu (Record of Inner Scriptures).

The *Abhidharmahṛdaya-śāstra* translated separately by Dharmatrāta, one fascicle in six rolls, totaling one hundred and twenty-two pages. Translated by Saṃghavarman together with Fazhi during the fifth year of the Tiāntǒng era of the Qi dynasty.
Extracted from the *Dharmottara-lu*.
One work in four fascicles, seventy sheets: the *Catuḥsatya-śāstra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty at Nankang Commandery in Guangzhou.
Extracted from the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Suíxiàng lùn* (Treatise on Following Characteristics) in two rolls and thirty-four pages; alternatively called the *Gūnamādì suíxiàng lùn*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty.
*Chūnèidiǎnlù* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).
One fascicle, seven sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen Dynasty.
Appears in the *Chūnèidiǎnlù*.

*Vibhāṣā-viniścaya-śāstra*, one fascicle, nine sheets; also known as *Viniścaya-vibhāṣā-śāstra*. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha of the Chen dynasty at Zhizhi Wangyuan Monastery in Guangzhou.
Recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.

One fascicle of the *Lìshì apítán lùn* (Abhidharmakośa-śāstra), totaling ten scrolls and one hundred seventy-three pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the third year of the Yongding era of the Chen dynasty.
Translated at the two monasteries of Zhizhi and Wangyuan in Guangzhou, and at Shixing Commandery;
recorded in the *Chángfáng lù*.
One fascicle: *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā*. The above was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the Chen Dynasty.
Translated at two locations, Zhizhi Temple and Wangyuan Garden in Guangzhou;
recorded in the Changfang lu.
One work in twenty-two fascicles comprising four hundred and fifty-eight sheets. Right: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Paramārtha during the Chen Dynasty.
Translated at Zhiyi Wangyuan Monastery in Guangzhou. Recorded in the Chángfáng lù (Catalogue of Dharma Master Chángfáng).

*Sūbadra-in-yuán-lùn* (The Discourse on the Causes and Conditions of Subhadra), one work in two fascicles. Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Yaśogupta.
Translated at the Four Heavenly Kings Temple (Sìtiānwáng sì).
Recorded in the Chángfáng lù.

*Mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra*, one volume consisting of two hundred fascicles and three thousand one hundred nine sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuánzàng at the Western Capital during the Yǒnghuī era of the Great Táng.
Recorded in the *Chu-nei-dian-lu* (Catalogue of Buddhist Scriptures).

One fascicle of the *Nyāyānusāra-śāstra*, consisting of eighty scrolls and one thousand four hundred and twenty sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the Great Ci'en Monastery during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Chūn-tien-lu* (Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures).

*Xianzong lun* (Treatise Elucidating the Doctrine), one volume, forty fascicles, six hundred and forty-four pages. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the Great Ci'en Monastery during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.
Extracted from the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures):

*Abhidharma-jñānaprasthāna-śāstra*, one volume in twenty fascicles, totaling three hundred and sixty-four sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang within the Imperial Palace during the Yonghui era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures:

*Abhidharmakośa-śāstra*, one volume in thirty fascicles, totaling four hundred and seventy sheets. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang within the Imperial Palace during the Xianqing era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu* (Catalogue of Inner Scriptures).
One fascicle of the *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā*, totaling thirty-four sheets; translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the *Neidian lu*.

The *Vijñānakāya-pāda-śāstra*, one fascicle in sixteen volumes, totaling two hundred seventy-one pages; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Xuanzang at the palace during the Xianqing era of the Great Tang.
Recorded in the Catalogue of Inner and Outer Scriptures:

their translations have been vast and numerous indeed. Consequently,
marketplaces and courtiers, mountains and valleys— everything has shifted from place to place.

This volume contains the catalog of missing texts for both Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna scriptures, totaling one fascicle. Regarding the eighty-eight sections of missing Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna scriptures:
Since the palm-leaf manuscripts first reached the East, the passage of time has been long and distant;
the transmission and translation have been vast and remote,
and the orthodox lineages have shifted many times.
Consequently, the net of the Teachings has drifted away, perishing along with the passing of men.

also titled *The Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of Buddha-Recollection*; ninety-five sheets. *The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Vimaladattā’s Responsive Eloquence*, one fascicle; also called *The Sūtra of Responsive Retribution*; twenty-six sheets. *The Sūtra of the Girl Vimalāprāptā*, one fascicle; twenty-five sheets. *The Sūtra of the Girl Abhayamati*, one fascicle. *The Sūtra of the Girl Āśokadattā, Daughter of King Ajātaśatru*, one fascicle; first appearance, seventeen sheets. *The Sūtra of the Dharma-Gate of Boundless Retention*, one fascicle; seventeen sheets; also titled *The Sūtra of the Limitless* or *The Sūtra Asked by the Girl Vajramukhī*. The *Aṣṭamaṅgalaka-mantra-sūtra*, second translation, three sheets; the *Daśa-maṅgala-sūtra*, first translation, four sheets; the *Nāgadattā-bodhisattva-pūrva-yoga-sūtra*, second translation; the old catalog states it is the *Nāgadattā-mūla-sūtra*, two sheets. *Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara Hṛdaya Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, twelve sheets; *Amoghapāśa Divine Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Hṛdaya Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Aniḥspṛha Sūtra*, one fascicle—also known as the *Gajapada Sūtra*, twenty-two sheets; *Gaja-pārśva Sūtra*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets. The *Kulaputradevapāla-sūtra*, one fascicle in two volumes, also known as the *Śrīgupta-kulaputra-sūtra*; this is a different translation of the same text as the *Jñānīputra-sūtra* and the *Candraprabha-kumāra-sūtra*. The Abhidharmasamuccaya in one volume, seven fascicles, totaling one hundred and eight pages; the Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya in one volume, three fascicles, totaling sixty-one pages. These two treatises, comprising ten volumes in total, are contained in the same case.

The *Prajñāpradīpa-śāstra*, one work in fifteen fascicles (or thirteen fascicles), totaling two hundred and forty sheets; the *Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchā-sūtra-śāstra*, one work in four fascicles (or three fascicles), totaling sixty sheets. The *Daśabhūmika-sūtra-śāstra*, one work in twelve fascicles, totaling two hundred and eighty-four sheets; the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-bhāṣya*, one work in fifteen fascicles, totaling two hundred and twenty sheets; the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-mūla-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles, totaling thirty-four sheets; and the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha-mūla-śāstra*, one work in three fascicles, totaling fifty-eight sheets. The above three treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles.

*Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, one work in twelve fascicles, 335 sheets; *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, one work in ten fascicles, Asvabhāva’s commentary, 220 sheets; *Mahāyānasaṃgrahabhāṣya*, one work in ten fascicles, Vasubandhu’s commentary, 180 sheets; *Mahāyānasaṃgrahaśāstra*, one work in ten fascicles, Paramārtha’s commentary, 125 sheets; *Bodhisattvabhūmi-viniścayasaṃgrahaṇī*, one work in ten fascicles (or eight), 250 sheets; *Śataśāstra-vyākhyā*, one work in ten fascicles; *Śataśāstrakārikā*, one fascicle, 16 sheets. The above three treatises are contained in the same volume.

The *Bodhicaryāvatāra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Provisions for Enlightenment), one fascicle, six rolls, one hundred and sixty-seven pages; the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra-śāstra* (Treatise on the Ratnakūṭa Sūtra), one fascicle, four rolls. The *Maitreya-bodhisattva-paripṛcchā-sūtra-śāstra*, one work in six fascicles, or ten fascicles, or five fascicles, totaling 145 sheets; the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhicitta-sūtra-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles, also titled the *Gayāśīrṣa-sūtra-śāstra*, totaling 34 sheets; and the *Mahāpuruṣa-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles, totaling 40 sheets. These three treatises comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

The *Madhyāntavibhāga-śāstra*, one fascicle, two rolls, thirty-eight sheets; the *Madhyāntavibhāga-bhāṣya*, one fascicle, three rolls; the *Madhyāntavibhāga-kārikā*, one roll; the *Buddha-abhidharma-śāstra*, one fascicle, two rolls, forty-four sheets; and the *Anupūrva-madhyama-śāstra*, one fascicle, two rolls—these five treatises, totaling ten rolls, are contained in the same volume.

*Mahāyāna-vistara-pañcaskandha-śāstra*, one fascicle, eighteen sheets; *Dūṣaṇa-catur-mahā-tīrthika-siddhānta-śāstra*, one fascicle, two sheets; *Dūṣaṇa-tīrthika-nirvāṇa-śāstra*, one fascicle, six sheets. The above ten treatises, including the *Upāya-hṛdaya*, comprise ten fascicles in a single volume.

*Viniscaya-samgrahani-śāstra*, three fascicles; *Vigraha-vyāvartanī-śāstra*, one fascicle (twenty-five sheets); *Mahāyāna-śraddhotpāda-śāstra*, one fascicle; *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-pūrvāstitva-adhunā-nāstitva-gāthā-śāstra*, six sheets; *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra-śāstra*, eleven sheets. The *Dharmacakrapravartana-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle; the *Ratnacūḍa-bodhisattva-caturdharma-sūtra-śāstra*, one fascicle (twelve sheets); the *Amitāyus-sūtra-upadeśa*, composed [in] eight sheets; the *Vijñānapariṇāma-śāstra*; and the *Muṣṭivyākhyāna-śāstra*. These three treatises are in the same volume.

alternatively called the *Pariśuddha-pāpa-nīvaraṇa Sūtra*; also known as the *Buddhadharma-sukha Sūtra*; or named the *Pañca-gati-pada Sūtra*.
