The *Buzishouyi jing* (Sūtra on Not Guarding One’s Own Mind), also known as the *Zishou jing* (Sūtra on Self-Guarding) or the *Zishouyi jing* (Sūtra on Self-Guarding the Mind); the *Shengfayin jing* (Sūtra on the Seal of the Noble Dharma); the *Bowosijiwang zumu mingzhong jing* (Sūtra on the Death of King Prasenajit’s Grandmother); the *Biqiu bi nü eming yu zisha jing* (Sūtra on a Bhikṣu Attempting Suicide to Avoid a Woman’s Ill Repute); the *Jiexiangyingfa jing*, also known as the *Jiexiangying jing*; the *Jiedexiang jing*, also known as the *Jiede jing*; and the *Biqiu tingshi jing*, also known as the *Tingshi biqiu jing*. These seven sūtras are contained in one volume.
The *Saṃyukta Āgama*, one fascicle. The above, together with the eighteen scriptures such as the *Yogācārabhūmi* and others, comprise eleven fascicles in this single volume.

*Ekottarika Āgama*, one work in fifty fascicles (the Inner Canon or alternatively fifty-one fascicles; according to Changfang’s *Ruzanglu*, forty-two fascicles). *Dirgha Āgama*, one work in twenty-two fascicles (Changfang’s *Ruzanglu* states twenty-five fascicles; it contains eighteen sūtras). *Madhyama Āgama*, one work in sixty fascicles (or fifty-eight fascicles). *Jātaka Sūtra*, one work in five fascicles (or four fascicles). Baochang states that the *Lunsheng jing*, the *Sidi jing*, the *Fashi feifa jing*, and the *Yiqie liu she shou yinyuan jing*—also known as the *Liucheshou jing* or the *Yiqie liu cheshou jing*—are these three sūtras combined in a single volume. The *Wulu* states: "The *Liucheshou yin jing*, also known as the *Shouyin jing*. *Yiqie liu cheshou yinyuan jing*, also named *Liucheshou jing* or *Yiqie liu cheshou jing*. The *Wulu* states: "The *Liucheshou yin jing*, also known as the *Shouyin jing*. These three sūtras are contained in one volume.

The *Āsravabhājanīya-sūtra*, the *Daśa-kuṭumbika-aṣṭanagara-puruṣa-sūtra*, the *Mūlapratyaya-samniśraya-sūtra* (the *Wùlù* records it as the *Dàxiāngyǐzhì-jīng*), the *Pratyaya-mūla-niśraya-sūtra*, and the *Aniruddha-aṣṭasmṛti-sūtra*—also known as the *Dhyānacaryā-cittasaṃgraha-sūtra* or simply the *Aṣṭasmṛti-sūtra*: these five sūtras are contained in one volume.
The *Ratthapāla Sūtra* (also known as the *Arhat Ratthapāla Sūtra*); the *Brahmāyu Sūtra*. These two sūtras are in one volume.

The *Upoṣadha Sūtra* (also known as the *Aṣṭāṅga-upoṣadha Sūtra* or the *Upāsikā-śakya-prapāta Sūtra*); the *Śunīraka Sūtra* (also known as the *Śreṇika-mānava-mūla Sūtra* or the *Pañcaskandha-hetuvastu Sūtra*); the *Sarvadharmamūla Sūtra*; the *Sundarika-bhāradvāja Sūtra* (also known as the *Brāhmaṇa-sundarika-bhāradvāja Sūtra*); the *Saptajñāna Sūtra* (also known as the *Saptajñāna Sūtra*). These six sūtras are in one volume.

The *Gaṅgā-upamā-sūtra* (also known as the *Sūtra on the Eight Qualities of the Ocean*, the *Campā-bhikṣu-sūtra*, or the *Dharma-sāgara-sūtra*). The *Chángfáng-lù* states: "The *Gaṅgā-upamā-sūtra*, the *Bhikṣu-praśna-bahūpāsaka-maraṇa-sūtra*, the *Buddha-bhāṣita-kāma-arthin-sūtra*, and the *Navasārddha-sūtra*; these four sūtras are in one volume."
The thirty-one sūtras beginning with the *Cūdā-brāhmaṇa-sūtra*, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Sūtra on the Former Deeds of King Mūrdhaja*—also known as the *Sūtra of King Mandhātṛ* or the *Sūtra of King Mūrdhaja*—and the *Niraya-sūtra*: these two sūtras are contained in the same fascicle.

The *Pañcavāra-puṇyaskandha-sūtra* (also known as the *Rājā Puṣya-sūtra*), the *Śuka-sūtra* (also known as the *Tuṭṭha-sūtra*), and the *Gotamī-vaipulya-phala-sūtra*: these three sūtras are contained in one volume.

The *Kṣārodaka-upama-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Simile of Salt Water), according to the catalogue of Saṃghavarman and the records of Master Dao’an, was translated from the *Madhyamāgama*. An old record states that the *Kṣārodaka-upama-sūtra* appeared in the *Āgama-sūtras*. The *Yamaloka-pañca-dūta-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Five Messengers of King Yama), also known as the *Lohakumbha-niraya-sūtra* (The Sutra of the Iron City Hell)—these two sutras are contained in the same volume.
The *Gulou shishi jing* (Sutra on the Times of Ancient Ages) and the *Changshouwang jing* (Sutra of King Long-life); these two sutras are in one volume.

The *Mo raoluan jing* (Sutra on Māra’s Disturbance), also known as the *Bimoshishi Mulian jing* (Sutra on the Wicked Māra Testing Maudgalyāyana) or the *Mowang rumujianlanfu jing* (Sutra on the Demon King Entering Maudgalyāyana’s Belly), in one volume. The *Fanzi Aba jing* (Sutra of the Brahmin Aba), also known as the *Abamojia jing* (Sutra of the Māṇava Aba) or the *Fokaijie Aba fanzhi jing* (Sutra of the Buddha Expounding the Liberation of the Brahmin Aba), in one volume. The *Pufa yi jing* (Sutra on the Meaning of Universal Dharma), also called the *Puyi jing* (Sutra of Universal Meaning) or the *Jufaxing jing* (Sutra on the Practice of Endowed Dharma), in one volume. The *Shibofa jing* (Sutra of the Ten Retributions), one work in two volumes, also known as the *Duozeng daozhang jing* (Sutra of the Chapter on the Path of Many Increases). These thirteen sutras, beginning with the *Dingshengwang jing* (Sutra of King Māndhātṛ), totaling nine volumes, are contained in the same fascicle.

*Lou tan jing* (Loutan Sūtra), one fascicle; six, five, or eight fascicles. *Jia luoyue liu xiang bai jing* (Sūtra on the Layman Kāla’s Sixfold Prostration), one fascicle—also known as *Liù xiàng bài*, *Da liù xiàng bài jing*, *Weihuā zhǎngzhě liù xiàng bài qīfó fùmǔ xìngzì jing*, *Fùrén wúpǐ qǐng fó jing*, or *Qīfó xìngzì jing*. *Ānán tóngxué jing* (Sūtra on Ānanda’s Fellow Students). *Ānabindī huà qīzǐ jing* (Sūtra on Anāthapiṇḍada Converting His Seven Sons). *Sāmājī jing* (Sūtra of Sāmājī)—also known as *Xūmótí nǚ jing*, *Nán guówáng jing*, or *Shùhuótán wáng jing*. According to the *Bǎochàng lù*, these four sūtras are contained in a single volume. *Sāmākè jing*. [End.]

The *Lishi yishan jing* (also known as the *Yishan jing*), the *Simingfa jing*, the *Liuliewang jing*, the *Ongujie jing* (also known as the *Zhiman jing*), and the *Zengyi ahan jing*: these five sūtras are contained in one volume.

The *Qunǔ pì jīng* (Sutra of the Simile of the Herd of Cows), the *Jīngxíng qīxíng xiànbào jīng* (Sutra on the Seven Practices of Walking Meditation with Immediate Retribution), the *Shīshí huò wǔfú bào jīng* (Sutra on Receiving Five Kinds of Meritorious Rewards for Giving Food)—also known as the *Fúdé jīng* (Sutra on Merit) or the *Shī sèlì jīng* (Sutra on Bestowing Physical Strength)—and the *Guówáng bùlīxiānní shí mèng jīng* (Sutra of King Piliyanī’s Ten Dreams)—also known as the *Guówáng qīmèng jīng* (Sutra of the King’s Seven Dreams)—and the *Fàngniú jīng* (Sutra of the Cowherd). These five sutras are contained in one volume.
The aforementioned sixteen sūtras, including the *Loutan jing* (Lokānuvartana-sūtra) and others, comprise ten fascicles in one volume.

The *Fanwang liangshi jian jing* (Brahmajāla-śāstra-dvāṣaṣṭi-dṛṣṭi-sūtra), one fascicle; also known as the *Fanwang jing*. The *Daban niepan jing* (Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra), one work in two fascicles; the *Daban niyuan jing* (Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra), one work in two fascicles; the *Ban niyuan jing* (Pari-nirvāṇa-sūtra), one fascicle; the *Jizhi guo jing* (Śramaṇaphala-sūtra); the *Zhangrezizi liu guochujia jing* (Sūtra on the Six Times a Householder’s Son Leaving Home); and the *Daidao baniepan jing* (Mahāprajāpatī-parinirvāṇa-sūtra). The *Xuda jing* (Sudatta-sūtra)—also known as the *Zhangrezixuda jing* or the *Sanguiwujie Cixin Yande jing*—these three sūtras share one volume.

The above eight sūtras comprise eight fascicles in one volume. [Included here are: the *Saṃyuktāgama* translated separately, one part in twenty fascicles; the *Zuòchán sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra on Dhyāna Samādhi), one part in three fascicles (or two); the *Yùyé jīng* (Yamavī Sūtra)—also known as the *Chángzhě yì fó shuō zǐfù wújìng* (The Elder Visits the Buddha to Discourse on the Disrespect of a Daughter-in-law) or the *Qīfù jīng* (Sūtra of the Seven Wives); the *Āsūdá jīng* (Aśokadatta Sūtra); and the *Yúlán pén jīng* (Ullambana Sūtra). Regarding the latter, a separate manuscript of five sheets titled the *Jìngtǔ Yúlán jīng* (Ullambana Sūtra of the Pure Land) exists, though its provenance is unknown. [Also included are: the *Zìqīn jīng* (Sūtra of Self-Offense); the *Guànlà jīng* (Candle-Molding Sūtra)—also known as the *Bānníhuán hòu sìbèi guànlà jīng* (Sūtra of the Candle-Molding Ceremony for the Four Classes after the Parinirvāṇa); and the *Bàoen fèngpén jīng* (Sūtra on Repaying Kindness by Offering the Bowl). These six sūtras share one volume.

*Āraṇyaka-cīnadharmaparyāya-sūtra*, two fascicles; alternatively, without the word "sūtra" [in the title]. *Pāpapunyavipākaphala-sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as *Vibhaṅgavipākaphala-sūtra*. *Karmavipākaprabheda-sūtra*, one fascicle. *Mātangī-sūtra*; also known as *Mādangī-sūtra* or *Ānanda-vaśīkṛta-strī-sūtra*. *Mātangī-vimocana-ṣaḍvastu-sūtra*. *Ānanda-vibhaṅga-sūtra*; also known as *Vibhaṅga-sūtra* or *Ānanda-prcchā-buddhapūjā-śubhāśubha-sūtra*. *Pañcamātṛputra-sūtra*. *Śamīra-sūtra*. The above five sūtras are contained in one volume.

*The Scripture on the Transformation of Hell through the Retribution of Sinful Karma*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture on the Retribution of Hell*. *The Scripture on the Auspiciousness and Inauspiciousness of Serving the Buddha Asked by Ānanda*, one fascicle; the *Sengyou Record* states it is also titled *The Scripture of Ānanda’s Questions*. The seventeen scriptures beginning with "Right Dhyāna," totaling eleven fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

The *Mātṛkā-sūtra* (摩登伽經), one fascicle in three or two rolls; the *Śikhālaṃkāra-sūtra* (舍頭諫經), one fascicle—also titled the *Sūtra on the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions of the Prince* (太子二十八宿經) or the *Record of the Conversion of Prince Vyāghraka* (虎耳太子化度錄)—the latter being the second translation from the same source as the *Mātṛkā-sūtra* but differing slightly from the version translated by Dharmarakṣa during the Han dynasty; the *Arthavargīya-sūtra* (義足經), one fascicle in two rolls; the *Sūtra on the Original Arising of Practice* (修行本起經), one fascicle in two rolls—the *Catalogue of Baochang* (寶唱錄) states it is also titled the *Sūtra on the Original Arising of Past Deeds* (宿行本起經); and the *Sūtra on the Auspicious Response of the Prince’s Original Arising* (太子本起瑞應經), one fascicle in two rolls—its first appearance was also called the *Sūtra on the Auspicious Response of the Original Arising* (瑞應本起經) or the *Middle Sūtra on the Original Arising* (中本起經). These five sūtras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

*Zhongbenqi jing* (Sutra of the Middle Arising), one work in two fascicles; also called *Taizi zhongbenqi jing* (Sutra of the Prince’s Middle Arising). *Guoxuzaineng yinguo jing* (Sutra on Past and Present Causes and Effects), one work in four fascicles. *Zazang jing* (Sutra of Miscellaneous Treasuries), which is the same work as the four texts titled *Guiwen Mulian egui baoying* (The Hungry Ghosts’ Retribution as Asked by a Ghost of Maudgalyāyana), *Mulian shuo didiy egui yinyuan* (The Causes and Conditions of Hells and Hungry Ghosts Spoken by Maudgalyāyana), and others; these are different translations of the same substance with different names, as recorded in the *Baochang lu*. The *Guiwen Mulian jing* (Sutra of the Ghost Asking Maudgalyāyana) and the *Egui baoying jing* (Sutra of the Hungry Ghosts’ Retribution)—also known as the *Mulian shuo didiy egui yinyuan jing*—these three sutras are contained in a single volume.

*The Scripture on the Arising of Practice*, one fascicle, in two rolls; also known as *The Scripture on the Ten Conditions*. *The Scripture on the Maiden of the Apple and Jīvaka*, one roll; also called *The Scripture on the Maiden of the Apple*. *The Scripture on the Poor Old Man*, one roll; also known as *The Scripture on the Poor and Aged*. *The Scripture on Overcoming Difficulties*, one roll; also known as *The Scripture on Difficulties*. The second edition appears in Baochang’s Record (*Bǎochàng lù*) as *The Scripture on the Elder Mukan*. *The Scripture on the Seven Daughters*, one roll; also known as *The Original Scripture of the Seven Daughters*. The Chángfáng Record states it was translated from the *Abhidharma*. *The Scripture on the Brothers Nāga Kings*, one roll; also known as *The Scripture on King Nanda*. *The Scripture on the Eight Teachers*. *The Scripture of the Forty-two Sections*. *The Scripture on the Sufferings Brought About by Desires*. The above seven scriptures are contained in one volume.
The fourteen scriptures beginning with the *Madhyama-āgama* (Middle-length Discourses) comprise eleven fascicles in one bundle.

These include: the *Upāsikā-śīla-saṃvara-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Saṅgharakṣita-nidāna-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Guhyakapāda-vajrapāṇi-paridevana-sūtra* (one fascicle, sometimes titled *Nidāna-buddha-parinirvāṇa-sūtra*); the *Buddha-parinirvāṇa-śarīra-saṃskāra-sūtra* (also known as the *Bhikṣu-guru-sūtra* or *Guru-bhikṣu-sūtra*); and the *Aṭānāṭiya-sūtra*, the *Kātyāyana-dharmadeśanā-kṣaya-gāthā-sūtra*, and the *Pañca-gati-pāpa-puṇya-vipāka-sūtra*. These last four scriptures are contained in a single volume.

*The Scripture on Making an Image of the Buddha*, also known as *The Scripture on King Udayana Making an Image of the Buddha*, and also known as *The Scripture on the Causes and Conditions for Making an Image*; and *The Oral Explanation of the Āgama on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*. These two scriptures are contained in one volume.
The *Adbhuta-dharma-sūtra*, the *Śucinirhāra-sūtra*, the *Putrajīva-phala-sūtra*, the *Viśvabhū-rāja-sūtra*, and the *Gṛhapati-luṣi-sūtra*—these five sūtras are in one volume.
The *Pañcarāja-sūtra*, the *Candanarāja-sūtra*, the *Khaṭvāṅga-sūtra*, and the *Anuttara-sthāna-sūtra*—these four sūtras are in one volume.
The eighteen sūtras beginning with the *Śuddhacarita*, totaling eight fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
The Hīnayāna Vinaya Piṭaka consists of thirty-five works totaling two hundred and sixty fascicles, arranged in twenty-eight bundles.
These include one work, the *Daśabhāṇavāra-vinaya*, in sixty-one fascicles, and one work, the *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, in forty fascicles.
The *Mahāsāṃghika-vinaya* in either seventy fascicles or sixty fascicles;
one work, the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-pañcavargika-vinaya*, in thirty-four fascicles; one work, the *Sudarsana-vibhāṣā-vinaya*, in eighteen fascicles;
and one work, the *Vinaya-nidāna*, in ten fascicles—also known as the *Śīla-hetu-pratyaya-sūtra*—[concerning] the Bhikṣuṇī Mahāprajāpatī.
The *Bhikṣuṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle, two volumes; the *Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Kāśyapīya Vinaya*, one fascicle;
the *Sarvāstivāda Bhikṣu Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Sarvāstivāda Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Mahāsāṃghika Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle;
the *Mahāsāṃghika Mahābhikṣu Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; the *Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇī Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; and the *Dharmaguptaka [Vinaya]*.

*The Bhikṣu-saṃgha-śīla-mūla*, one fascicle; *The Bhikṣuṇī-śīla-mūla* according to the Four-Part [Vinaya], one fascicle. These nine scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are bound together in one volume. *The Mahābhikṣu-trisahasra-vidhi-sūtra*, one work in three fascicles;

*The Śīla-kṣema-vyasanapraśamana-sūtra*, one fascicle (also called *Śīla-vinaya-vyasanapraśamana*); *The Mahīśāsaka-bhikṣu-śīla-mūla*, one fascicle (also called the *Pañcavargika-śīla-mūla*); *The Mahāśramaṇa-ekottara-karman*, one fascicle; *The Sarvāstivāda-monastic-essential-karman*, one work in two fascicles; *The Dharmaguptaka-karman*, one fascicle; *The Dharmaguptaka-karman*, one fascicle. These seven scriptures, totaling ten fascicles, are bound together in one volume.

*Upāli-asks-the-Buddha Sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively titled *Upāli on the True and False Śramaṇas*, one fascicle; also known as the *Mahābhikṣu Sūtra*. *Kāśyapa’s Prohibitions on Precepts*, one fascicle; also known as the *Mahābhikṣu Sūtra* and the *Sūtra on True and False Śramaṇas*. *Śrāmaṇera Ten Precepts with Dignified Conduct*, one fascicle. *Śrāmaṇera Separation from Precepts Sūtra*, one fascicle. *Śāriputra-asks Sūtra*, one fascicle. *Vinaya-viniścaya-upāli-śāstra*, twenty-two fascicles; also simply called the *Viniścaya-śāstra*. *Śrāmaṇera Dignified Conduct Sūtra*, one fascicle. *Upāsaka Five Precepts Characteristics*, one fascicle. *Upāsaka Five Precepts Dignified Conduct Sūtra*, one fascicle. The above ten sūtras and śāstras, totaling ten fascicles, are contained in the same volume.
The *Vinayamātṛkā-śāstra*, one work in eight fascicles; the *Sarvāstivāda-mātṛkā*, one work in ten fascicles;
the *Sarvāstivāda-vinaya-vibhāṣā*, one work in nine fascicles;
and the Hīnayāna Abhidharma Piṭaka, comprising thirty-six works totaling seven hundred and forty-four fascicles in seventy-three bundles. Great.
The *Vibhāṣā-śāstra*, one work in two hundred fascicles; the *Nyāyānusāra-śāstra*, one work in eighty fascicles;
the *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha-vibhāṣā*, one work in eighty-four fascicles, or ninety-one fascicles, or sixty fascicles;
the *Abhidharmakośa-prakaraṇa-śāstra*, one work in forty fascicles; the *Jñānaprasthāna-śāstra*, one work in twenty fascicles; and the *Abhidharma*...
The *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya* in one section, thirty fascicles; the *Abhidharmakośa-kārikā* in one fascicle;
the *Purṇavasu-saṃgīti-śāstra* in one section, twelve fascicles (or ten fascicles);
the *Vibhāṣā-abhidharma-śāstra* in one section, nineteen fascicles (or fifteen fascicles, or fourteen fascicles), also called the *Vibhāṣā* or the *Vistara*.
The *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha* in one collection, thirty fascicles (or twenty fascicles); also known as the *Kātyāyanīputra-abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha*.
The *Śāriputra-abhidharma* in one collection, thirty fascicles (or twenty fascicles, or twenty-two fascicles).
The *Tattvasiddhi-śāstra* in one collection, twenty-four fascicles (or twenty fascicles, or...).

The *Dharmatrāta-abhidharma-śāstra* in either sixteen or fourteen fascicles, one work in six fascicles; the above three treatises comprise forty-one fascicles in four bundles. The *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra*, one work in eleven fascicles;

the *Vibhāṣā-śāstra on the Analysis of Merit*, one work in five, four, or three fascicles; the *Tridharmaka-śāstra*, one work in three or two fascicles; and the *Abhidharma-amṛta-rasa-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles (also known as the *Amṛtarasa-abhidharma*). The above three treatises comprise ten fascicles in one bundle.

The *Saṃgītiparyāya-śāstra* (Abhidharma-saṃgīti-paryāya-śāstra), one volume in twelve fascicles; the *Vimuktimārga-śāstra*, one volume in thirteen fascicles (or twelve); the *Catuḥsatya-śāstra*, one volume in four fascicles; the *Anuśaya-lakṣaṇa-śāstra*, one volume in two fascicles (also called the *Guṇamati-anuśaya-lakṣaṇa-śāstra*); the *Abhidharmavatāra-śāstra*, one volume in two fascicles; the *Samayabhedoparacanacakra-śāstra*, one volume; and the *Aṣṭādaśanikāya-bheda-śāstra* (also titled *Bheda-nānāvāda-śāstra* or *Nānāvāda-bheda-śāstra*). The latter two treatises are contained in the same volume.
The above six treatises comprise ten fascicles in one bundle. The *Lokaprajñapti-abhidharma-śāstra*, one work in ten fascicles;

the *Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya*, one work in twenty-two fascicles; the *Saṃgītiparyāya-pāda-śāstra*, one work in twenty fascicles; the *Dharmaskandha-pāda-śāstra*, one work in twelve fascicles; the *Vijñānakāya-pāda-śāstra*, one work in sixteen fascicles; and the *Abhidharmahṛdaya*, one work in four fascicles. The latter two treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles.
The *Prakaraṇapāda-śāstra*, one work in eighteen fascicles; the *Pañcavastuka-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles. These two treatises comprise twenty fascicles in two bundles.

The *Dhātu-kāya-pāda-śāstra*, one work in three fascicles; the *Tri-mi-ti-śāstra*, one work in three fascicles; the *Pratyekabuddha-nidāna-śāstra*, one work in two fascicles. These three treatises comprise eight fascicles in a single bundle.

The *Collection of the Biographies of Worthies and Sages* consists of twenty-one works in forty-one fascicles, arranged in four bundles. The *Buddhacarita* (Praise of the Buddha’s Deeds) is one work in five fascicles, composed by the Bodhisattva Aśvaghoṣa. The *Aśokarājāvadāna* (Biography of King Aśoka) is one work in either five or seven fascicles. These two biographies comprise ten fascicles and are contained in the same bundle.

The *Dhyāna-guhyārtha-sūtra*, one work in four fascicles; also known as the *Dhyāna-guhyārtha-sūtra* (without the character "jing") or the *Dhyāna-dharmaguhyārtha-sūtra*, one work in five fascicles—also titled the *Dhyāna-dharmaguhyārtha* or in two fascicles; the *Commentary on the Dhyāna-dharmaguhyārtha*, one work in two fascicles; and the *Secret Essentials for Treating the Diseases of Dhyāna*, one fascicle. These four works, totaling twelve fascicles, are contained in the same volume.

Fei Changfang of the Sui dynasty considered this to be due to habitual conditioning (*vāsanā*);

Regarding the above scriptures, they have been traditionally transmitted since antiquity as being spurious and erroneous.
Observing their phrasing, it is verbose and cluttered; as for their principles and meanings, they are superficial and frivolous.
Although they pilfer the name of the Buddha’s teachings, they ultimately reveal the true nature of human scheming.
The various classes of beings who fall into delusion do not fail to do so because of this.
Therefore, I have compiled and listed them in detail as above.

[These were] issued by imperial decree in the first year of the Fengzheng era (677 CE), within the context of the Buddha-dharma, clarifying all Buddha-dharmas. All were respectfully certified. One fascicle.
Order that apocryphal scriptures,
as well as miscellaneous talismans and registers, be sent to the Sacrificial Department for submission to the Imperial Court.
Since the aforementioned teachings contravene the intent of the Buddha, [they must be suppressed].
To construct separate heterodox doctrines is precisely the limit of spurious and miscellaneous talismans and registers.
Furthermore, according to the edict of the second year of the Shengli era:
As for those who study the three stages,
they merely practice begging for food, observing the long fast, abstaining from grain, maintaining the precepts,
and practicing seated meditation; all such actions are in violation of the Dharma.
Fortunately, having received Your Majesty’s enlightened decree,
I have been enabled to rectify past errors;
I dare not venture to include them in the catalog.
Furthermore, [the texts] were edited and revised to serve as a model for future generations.
